t: 歡迎使用 TraceDraw 說明
h: 本說明的編排方式 在 TraceDraw 中取得說明 從哪裡開始
x: 歡迎使用 TraceDraw 說明 TraceDraw 是一款免費的開放原始碼向量繪圖程式。你可以用它繪製插畫、標誌、圖表、版面和印刷品，它們由在任何尺寸下都保持清晰的形狀、線條和文字組成，還能與點陣圖結合。同一個程式可在 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 以及網頁瀏覽器中執行。 本說明一步步解釋如何在 TraceDraw 中完成工作，以及每個對話方塊、面板和工具的用途。 本說明的編排方式 左側的目錄依照工作的順序排列： 入門 介紹工作區、新繪圖、開啟和儲存。 線條、形狀和外框、物件、符號和圖層 以及 色彩、填色和透明度 介紹繪製和排列物件。 特殊效果、文字、範本和樣式、頁面和版面 以及 點陣圖 涵蓋其餘的繪圖工作。 列印、網頁圖形 和 檔案格式 介紹如何把作品從 TraceDraw 輸出。 自訂和自動化 介紹選項、工作區、指令碼和 AI 功能，參考 列出每個功能表命令、工具、面板和鍵盤快速鍵。 使用 搜尋 索引標籤可依頁面中的任何字詞找到頁面，使用上方的語言清單可用另一種語言閱讀同一頁面。 在 TraceDraw 中取得說明 按 F1 開啟眼前內容的頁面：開啟的對話方塊，否則是顯示的面板，再否則是目前的工具。 按一下對話方塊或選項頁面底部的 ? 按鈕，開啟它的頁面。 選擇 說明 > 說明主題 開啟本頁。 提示 面板會在你工作時說明目前的工具；其中的 深入了解 連結會開啟該工具在這裡的頁面。請參閱 提示。 頁面會在網頁瀏覽器中以 TraceDraw 設定的語言開啟。 從哪裡開始 如果你剛開始使用 TraceDraw，請先閱讀 工作區，接著閱讀 建立繪圖 和 繪製線條和曲線。

s: 歡迎使用 TraceDraw 說明
h: 在程式中查看新內容 最近版本的重點
x: 新功能 TraceDraw 的每個版本都會加入功能和修正。本頁說明如何得知變更內容，並列出最近版本的重點。 在程式中查看新內容 選擇 說明 > 新功能 開啟歡迎畫面的新功能頁面，其中有本版本的新聞。 開啟 說明 > 標示新功能，在功能表中標出本版本的新內容：每個新命令的結尾、通往新命令的子功能表箭頭旁，以及包含新命令的功能表標題上方都會出現一個小圓點。關閉該命令後標記消失，下次啟動 TraceDraw 時該命令又會關閉。 每個版本的完整變更清單在專案的 變更記錄 中。 最近版本的重點 物件縮圖。 物件 面板在每個物件的名稱旁顯示其縮小的圖形；在清單上按 Ctrl 捲動滾輪或拖曳底部的滑桿可調整大小。請參閱 組織物件與圖層。 使用你的語言的說明。 每個 ? 按鈕和 F1 都會以 TraceDraw 設定的語言開啟本說明中關於眼前對話方塊、面板或工具的頁面。 文件屬性。 檔案 > 文件屬性 保存繪圖的語言、標題、主旨、作者、版權、標籤、備註和評等，並附有繪圖內容的完整報告。請參閱 文件屬性。 色彩管理。 工具 > 色彩管理 設定繪圖的描述檔和新繪圖的預設值，並為開啟或匯入的檔案設定原則。請參閱 色彩管理。 條碼和 QR 碼。 三步驟精靈可放置條碼，QR 碼則是可在 屬性 面板中編輯的動態物件。請參閱 條碼和 QR 碼。 效果。 效果 功能表集中了各效果面板；漸變可以按固定間距沿路徑排列，並以順時針或逆時針旋轉色彩。請參閱 漸變。 路徑文字 有自己的方向、位置、距離和位移設定。請參閱 新增和編輯文字。 字型管理員 整理已安裝的字型、資料夾、我的最愛和集合。請參閱 字型和字符。

s: 歡迎使用 TraceDraw 說明
h: 關於方塊 檢查更新 自動檢查 歡迎畫面 社群和支援
x: 關於 TraceDraw 和更新 TraceDraw 免費且開放原始碼。本頁說明如何查看你的版本、如何取得較新的版本，以及在哪裡尋求協助。 關於方塊 選擇 說明 > 關於 TraceDraw 可查看執行中的版本、作者、授權、原始碼連結以及程式的組成。按 關閉、Enter 或 Esc 關閉。  檢查更新 在桌面版中，TraceDraw 可以在新版本發行時通知你。 立即檢查： 選擇 說明 > 更新。 TraceDraw 向專案的發行頁面查詢最新版本，並說明它是否比你的版本新。測試版和每夜建置從不提供。 有較新的版本時，選擇要做的事： 下載 開啟適用於你系統的檔案下載（Windows 上為安裝程式或可攜式壓縮檔，Mac 上為符合處理器的磁碟映像，Linux 上為 AppImage 或壓縮檔）。之後由系統的安裝程式完成安裝。 版本資訊 開啟該版本的變更清單。 略過此版本 不再提供該版本。 關閉 關閉方塊。 當 TraceDraw 以 Linux AppImage 執行時，方塊也可能提供 安裝：它把新的 AppImage 下載到執行中的檔案旁，檢查下載是否完整且真實，然後取代舊檔案。新版本會在你下次開啟 TraceDraw 時啟動。若有任何檢查不通過，舊檔案保持原樣，方塊會告訴你原因。 若檢查失敗（例如沒有網際網路連線），方塊會說明並提供發行頁面。  自動檢查 工具 > 選項 > 全域 的 一般 頁面有一個啟動時檢查更新的設定。它預設開啟：TraceDraw 每天在啟動時安靜地檢查一次，只有在出現你未略過的新版本時才提示。 TraceDraw 首次啟動時會詢問是否檢查更新：一律檢查 或 永不檢查。在您回答之前，TraceDraw 不會自行建立任何連線。您的回答會設定此選項，之後可隨時在此處變更。 注意： 瀏覽器版本永遠是最新的。在瀏覽器版本中， 說明 > 更新 會開啟發行頁面。 歡迎畫面 歡迎畫面是 TraceDraw 啟動時的第一個索引標籤。你可以在這裡建立繪圖、開啟最近使用的繪圖（每個都附縮圖；清除清單 會清除它們）、從範本開始、閱讀新聞並找到學習資源。選擇 說明 > 歡迎畫面 可再次顯示它。說明 > 影片教學、 快速入門指南 和 使用指南 開啟它的學習頁面， 新功能 開啟它的新聞。 社群和支援 說明 > 社群 開啟專案的討論論壇，你可以在那裡提問和分享想法。 說明 > 支援 開啟問題追蹤系統，你可以在那裡回報問題。 說明 > 訊息設定 開啟設定 TraceDraw 訊息的選項。
入門 這些頁面介紹 TraceDraw：視窗的各個部分，如何建立、開啟和儲存繪圖，如何在繪圖中移動和復原操作，以及繪圖時在哪裡取得說明。 TraceDraw 可在 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 上執行，也可以不安裝任何東西就在網頁瀏覽器中執行。兩者是同一個程式；瀏覽器版本的少數差異在 瀏覽器版本 中說明。

h: 視窗的各個部分 標準工具列 屬性列 工具箱和展開工具列 面板 繪圖視窗 調色盤 狀態列 排列各列 處理多個繪圖 介面大小
x: 工作區 TraceDraw 視窗包含您的繪圖，以及處理繪圖所需的一切。本頁說明視窗各部分的名稱，讓本說明的其他頁面更容易理解。 視窗的各個部分 由上到下、由左到右： 選單列包含所有指令，分布在 檔案、編輯、檢視、版面、物件、效果、點陣圖、文字、表格、工具、視窗 和 說明 選單中。每個指令旁邊都會顯示其快速鍵。沒有開啟任何繪圖時，只會顯示 檔案、工具、視窗 和 說明。選單指令頁面列出了所有指令。 標準工具列包含常用指令（請參閱下文）。 屬性列顯示您目前操作的設定。 文件分頁為每個開啟的繪圖顯示一個分頁。 左側的工具箱包含各種工具。 尺規沿著繪圖視窗的頂端和左側排列。 繪圖視窗顯示頁面及其周圍的桌面。 面板位於右側。 調色盤沿著底部排列。 最底部的狀態列描述作用中的工具和選取範圍。 標準工具列 標準工具列依群組包含： 新增、開啟（其箭頭會列出您最近使用的繪圖）、儲存和列印。 剪下、複製和貼上。 復原和重做。其箭頭會列出各個步驟，因此您可以選擇一個步驟，一次復原或重做多個步驟。 匯入、匯出和發佈為 PDF。 縮放方塊：輸入縮放比例並按 Enter，或開啟其清單以縮放至選取範圍、所有物件、頁面、頁面寬度或高度，以及 10% 到 1600% 的比例。接著是全螢幕預覽。 顯示尺規、顯示格點和顯示參考線，開啟時會以按下狀態顯示。 關閉貼齊（Alt+Q）以及要貼齊對象的清單。 選項，會開啟選項頁面的清單。 啟動：字型管理員、歡迎畫面和色彩管理。 將指標停留在按鈕上，即可查看其名稱、快速鍵和用途。 屬性列 屬性列會隨著您的操作而改變。沒有選取任何物件且 選取 工具作用中時，它會顯示頁面大小和方向、繪圖單位以及微調距離。選取物件時，它會顯示物件的位置、大小、縮放比例、旋轉和鏡射按鈕，接著是該類物件的設定。每個工具都會加入自己的設定，並在該工具的頁面中說明。 在數值欄位中，您可以輸入算式，例如 10+5，或以其他單位輸入值，例如 1 in，它會轉換為繪圖單位。 工具箱和展開工具列 工具箱中每一組工具都有一個按鈕。角落有小箭頭的按鈕包含一個展開工具列，也就是一份相關工具的清單。若要開啟展開工具列，請按一下箭頭、以右鍵按一下按鈕，或按住按鈕。之後按鈕會顯示您在該群組中最後使用的工具。將指標停留在工具上，即可查看其名稱、快速鍵和用途。 按兩下某些按鈕會執行捷徑動作：選取 會選取所有物件，縮放 會縮放至符合所有物件，矩形 會加入一個與頁面同樣大小的矩形。 工具箱末端的 + 按鈕會列出各個群組，每個群組都有一個核取方塊可顯示或隱藏，並可重設工具箱。工具箱頁面列出了所有工具。 面板 面板包含您在工作時保持開啟的設定，例如一開始就開啟的 屬性、物件 和 提示。開啟的面板會以分頁形式排列在右側；按一下分頁可將其面板移到最前面，或按一下最前面的分頁將面板收合起來。從 視窗 > 面板 或使用其快速鍵開啟其他面板；分頁下方的 + 可新增面板。每個面板的標題列都有收合和關閉按鈕。面板頁面列出了所有面板。 繪圖視窗 頁面位於桌面上，也就是頁面周圍的區域，您也可以把物件放在那裡。繪圖下方有： 頁面導覽器：在前面插入頁面、第一頁、上一頁、頁碼、下一頁、最後一頁以及在後面插入頁面； 每個頁面一個分頁（按一下可前往該頁面，按兩下可重新命名）； 水平捲軸。拖曳頁面分頁與捲軸之間的虛線分隔器，可分配兩者之間的空間。 捲軸之間角落的導覽器按鈕，在您按住時會顯示頁面的縮圖；將指標移到縮圖上即可移動檢視。使用 選取 工具按兩下頁面邊框，會開啟頁面大小選項。 調色盤 按一下調色盤中的色彩可填滿選取的物件；以右鍵按一下可為其外框上色。繪圖視窗下方的文件調色盤會收集您的繪圖所使用的色彩。請參閱調色盤。 狀態列 狀態列會顯示作用中工具的提示、選取了什麼以及在哪個圖層上，還有選取範圍的填色和外框。按兩下填色或外框部分即可變更它們。狀態列頁面說明了每個部分。 排列各列 您可以移動工具箱、調色盤、標準工具列、屬性列和狀態列：拖曳列的虛線握把到視窗的其他邊緣，或拖離邊緣使其浮動。以右鍵按一下握把可鎖定各列或重設其位置。若要顯示或隱藏某一列，請使用 視窗 > 工具列。您也可以將整個排列儲存為工作區；請參閱工作區。 處理多個繪圖 每個開啟的繪圖在尺規上方都有自己的分頁，顯示其名稱，並在有未儲存變更時顯示 *。最後一個分頁之後的分頁會建立新繪圖。每個繪圖都保有自己的頁面、復原歷程、選取範圍、縮放比例和單位。 視窗 > 重疊顯示、水平並排 和 垂直並排 會將每個繪圖顯示在各自的視窗中；合併視窗 會將它們恢復為分頁。新增視窗 會為同一個繪圖開啟第二個視窗，例如同時查看兩個頁面或兩種縮放比例；在一個視窗中的編輯會顯示在所有視窗中。 介面大小 如果選單和按鈕看起來太小或太大，請選擇 工具 > 選項 > 自訂，並在 外觀 頁面上設定介面大小。介面大小永遠不會變更您繪圖的大小。請參閱自訂選項。

h: 建立繪圖 一般 尺寸 色彩設定 略過對話方塊 其他開始方式
x: 建立繪圖 每個繪圖都從頁面大小、頁數、色彩模式和解析度開始。您可以在 建立新文件 對話方塊中選擇這些設定。 建立繪圖 選擇 檔案 > 開新檔案（Ctrl+N）、按一下標準工具列上的「新增」、按一下最後一個文件分頁後面的 +，或按一下歡迎畫面上的「新增文件」。 在 建立新文件 對話方塊中，設定下列各項值。 按一下 確定 或按 Enter。 繪圖會在自己的分頁中開啟。對話方塊會記住您的設定值，供下一個繪圖使用。  一般 名稱 為繪圖命名。預設為下一個 Untitled-N。 預設集 會一次設定色彩模式、頁面大小、單位和解析度。預設集包括 TraceDraw 預設 和 預設 CMYK（CMYK、A4、公釐、300 dpi）、預設 RGB（RGB、A4、公釐、300 dpi）以及 網頁（RGB、1920 x 1080 像素、72 dpi）。當您變更其中某個值時，預設集會顯示 自訂，除非這些值再次符合某個預設集。 預設集旁邊的按鈕包含 儲存預設集（會要求輸入 預設集名稱，並將目前的值加入清單）和 刪除預設集（會移除您儲存的預設集）。內建的預設集無法刪除。 頁數 設定繪圖的頁數，從 1 到 999。每個頁面都命名為「頁面 N」，並且有一個圖層。 主要色彩模式 可選 CMYK（用於印刷）或 RGB（用於螢幕）。 尺寸 頁面大小 列出各種紙張大小，或「自訂」。選擇大小時會保留目前的方向。若您輸入的寬度和高度符合某個紙張大小（無論哪個方向），就會選取該大小的名稱。 寬度 和 高度 設定頁面大小，單位為您在寬度旁邊清單中選擇的單位。這些單位會成為屬性列的繪圖單位。 方向：直向 或 橫向。 解析度，以 dpi 為單位（預設為 300）。它用於會轉換為像素的效果，以及以像素測量大小：1920 像素在 300 dpi 時為 162.56 mm，在 72 dpi 時為 677.33 mm。當單位為像素時，變更解析度會保留頁面的像素大小。 色彩設定 開啟 色彩設定 以選擇繪圖的 RGB 描述檔、CMYK 描述檔 和 灰階描述檔，以及 演色意圖。預設值為 sRGB、內建的 CMYK 描述檔、20% 網點擴大的灰階，以及相對色度。請參閱色彩管理。 略過對話方塊 勾選 不要再顯示此對話方塊 即可直接以上次使用的值建立新繪圖。若要再次顯示對話方塊，請在 工具 > 選項 > TraceDraw 的 一般 頁面上開啟對應的設定。請參閱 TraceDraw 選項。 其他開始方式 檔案 > 從範本開新檔案 從範本開始。請參閱範本。 檔案 > 開啟 開啟現有的繪圖。請參閱開啟和儲存繪圖。

h: 開啟繪圖 開啟後的通知 儲存繪圖 另存新檔 關閉繪圖 自動備份與復原
x: 開啟和儲存繪圖 機器翻譯：本頁可能落後於英文版。 TraceDraw 以自己的格式 .tdraw 儲存繪圖，這種格式會保留所有內容；它也可以儲存 .cdr 檔案。它還能開啟許多其他格式；請參閱支援的檔案格式。 開啟繪圖 選擇 檔案 > 開啟（Ctrl+O），或按一下標準工具列上的「開啟」。 選擇檔案並確認。 繪圖會在新的分頁中開啟。若要開啟最近使用過的繪圖，請使用 檔案 > 開啟最近使用的檔案、「開啟」按鈕的箭頭，或歡迎畫面上的清單；清除清單 會清空清單。若只要從歡迎畫面的清單移除一個繪圖，請指向它並按一下右側的 x，或在它上面按右鍵並選擇 Remove from list；檔案本身會保留在原處。檔案 > 匯入（Ctrl+I）則是將檔案的內容加入目前開啟的繪圖；請參閱匯入檔案。 您也可以從檔案管理員將檔案拖曳到 TraceDraw。繪圖（例如 .tdraw 或 .cdr 檔案）放在標題列、功能表、工具列或文件分頁上時，會在自己的分頁中開啟；放在繪圖視窗上時，會匯入目前開啟的繪圖。拖曳時顯示的外框和標籤會說明將發生什麼事。在系統不告知指標位置的環境（Linux、macOS）中，繪圖會在分頁中開啟，圖片則會匯入。 繪圖最初如何顯示（整個頁面、其物件、頁面寬度、實際大小，或儲存時的頁面、位置和縮放）由 工具 > 選項 > TraceDraw 的 顯示 頁面上的 View when a drawing opens 設定。 開啟後的通知 當開啟的檔案中有些物件無法讀取，或繪圖使用了電腦上未安裝的字型時，檔案開啟後會有一則訊息告知： 對於無法讀取的物件，訊息會列出其數量。回報按鈕會在專案的問題追蹤系統中為該檔案開啟一個新的問題，以便修正問題。 對於缺少的字型，Missing Fonts 對話方塊會列出每個字型以及目前繪製它的已安裝字型，並讓您選擇只在本次工作階段使用另一個字型，或在繪圖中取代它。請參閱缺少的字型。 勾選不要再顯示此訊息即可停止顯示這些訊息。您可以在 工具 > 選項 > 全域 的 警告 頁面上再次開啟它們。 儲存繪圖 選擇 檔案 > 儲存（Ctrl+S）可將繪圖寫回其檔案。新的繪圖，或是從 TraceDraw 只能讀取的格式開啟的繪圖，還沒有檔案，因此「儲存」會開啟 儲存繪圖 對話方塊。 另存新檔 檔案 > 另存新檔（Ctrl+Shift+S）會以其他名稱、在其他資料夾或以其他格式儲存繪圖。  以新名稱儲存繪圖： 選擇資料夾。左側的清單有 主資料夾、桌面、文件、下載 和 圖片 以及各磁碟機的捷徑。上移一層 會移至上一層資料夾；您也可以在路徑列中輸入資料夾。按兩下清單中的資料夾即可開啟；按一下檔案即可使用其名稱。 輸入 檔案名稱。所選類型的副檔名會自動加上。 選擇 存檔類型：TraceDraw（*.tdraw）或 CDR 檔案 (*.cdr)。 選擇 版本。對於 TraceDraw 檔案，這是格式的版本，最新的在最前面。對於 .cdr 檔案，這是檔案的版本，從 27 到 7；較舊的程式只能開啟與其本身同樣舊或更舊的版本。您選擇的版本會隨繪圖保留，因此「儲存」會直接再次以該版本寫入，不會詢問。 選擇要和繪圖一起放入檔案的內容： 對於版本 16 以上的 .cdr 檔案，嵌入色彩描述檔 會將繪圖的 CMYK 描述檔儲存在檔案中。 嵌入字型（預設關閉）會在授權允許時，將文字使用的字型儲存在 TraceDraw 檔案和版本 16 以上的 .cdr 檔案中。核取方塊會顯示字型增加的檔案大小。要交給可能沒有這些字型的電腦時，請勾選它。 在桌面版的 TraceDraw 檔案中，Package 會將繪圖連同其連結的圖片、字型檔和一份報告儲存在以繪圖命名的資料夾中，Include a PDF 則會加入一份 PDF。請參閱封裝繪圖。 這些選擇都會保留到下一次。 視需要填寫 標題、主旨 和 評等（再按一下亮起的最後一顆星即可取消）。這些是繪圖的屬性，也會顯示在文件屬性中。 按一下 儲存 或按 Enter。如果檔案已存在，TraceDraw 會詢問是否要 取代。 對話方塊會從繪圖所在的資料夾開始；若沒有，則從您上次儲存的資料夾開始；再沒有則從您的文件資料夾開始。從 .cdr 檔案或其他格式開啟的繪圖，會從該檔案所在的資料夾並以其名稱開始，因此以相同格式儲存會取代它。 在檔案清單中，新增資料夾 會建立資料夾並讓您立即輸入名稱；F2 或按右鍵可重新命名資料夾或檔案；輸入字母會跳到以這些字母開頭的項目，Enter 會開啟所選的資料夾。在路徑列中輸入的資料夾不必按 Enter 即會採用。 注意： 在瀏覽器版本中，每次儲存都是一次下載：對話方塊會保留名稱、類型、版本和屬性，而瀏覽器會將檔案放在其下載資料夾中。 其他儲存方式：檔案 > 另存為範本 會儲存範本（請參閱範本），匯出 會寫入其他格式（請參閱匯出），發佈為 PDF 會寫入 PDF（請參閱發佈為 PDF），傳送到 會將 PDF 儲存到您的桌面或文件資料夾，或將其附加到電子郵件中，Package 會將繪圖、其圖片和字型放入一個資料夾（請參閱封裝繪圖），而 GitHub 會將繪圖保存在 GitHub 儲存庫中（請參閱 GitHub）。還原 會回到上次儲存的版本。 關閉繪圖 選擇 檔案 > 關閉（Ctrl+F4）、按一下繪圖分頁上的關閉按鈕，或以滑鼠中鍵按一下分頁。全部關閉 會關閉所有繪圖，結束（Alt+F4）則會關閉 TraceDraw。 當繪圖有未儲存的變更時，TraceDraw 會先詢問是否要儲存：是 會儲存（若繪圖還沒有檔案，會要求輸入名稱），否 會不儲存就關閉，取消 則會保持繪圖開啟。當多個繪圖有變更時，它會逐一詢問；按「取消」即停止。  自動備份與復原 當自動備份開啟時，TraceDraw 會為您開啟的繪圖保留備份（工具 > 選項 > TraceDraw 的 儲存 頁面可設定頻率和位置；預設為每 20 分鐘一次）。正常關閉 TraceDraw 時會移除這些備份。 如果 TraceDraw 未正常關閉就結束了，例如停電後，下次啟動時它會提供這些備份：復原 會將每個備份以未儲存的繪圖開啟（之後「儲存」會詢問要存到哪裡），捨棄 則會將備份留在其資料夾中。同時執行的兩個 TraceDraw 視窗永遠不會提供彼此的繪圖。 在瀏覽器版本中，備份保存在瀏覽器為此網站提供的儲存空間，每個分頁各有自己的資料夾。關閉或重新載入有未儲存繪圖的分頁時會先詢問，下次開啟時會提供該分頁留下的繪圖；捨棄 會刪除這些備份。

h: 復原和重做 復原面板 縮放 縮放工具 平移 檢視
x: 復原、縮放和平移 您可以復原任何變更，並以任何縮放比例、從任何位置檢視您的繪圖。縮放和平移永遠不會變更繪圖。 復原和重做 編輯 > 復原（Ctrl+Z）會取消上一個變更；重做（Ctrl+Shift+Z）會再次執行它。 標準工具列上「復原」和「重做」旁邊的箭頭會列出各個步驟。選擇一個步驟，即可復原或重做到該步驟為止的所有變更。 重複 會再次套用上一個指令，例如套用到您選取的下一個物件。 復原面板 復原 面板會列出繪圖的每個變更，最舊的在最前面。按一下某個步驟，可讓繪圖回到該步驟之後的狀態；按一下較後面的步驟則可再次前進。從 視窗 > 面板 開啟它。  縮放 轉動滑鼠滾輪，即可以指標為中心放大或縮小。 使用標準工具列上的縮放方塊：輸入比例，或從其清單中選擇（10% 到 1600%），或縮放至選取範圍、所有物件、頁面、頁面寬度或頁面高度。 檢視 > 放大 和 縮小 會縮放一級；縮放至符合視窗（F4）會顯示所有物件，縮放至頁面（Shift+F4）顯示頁面，縮放至選取範圍（Shift+F2）顯示選取範圍。 在觸控板上以雙指捏合可縮放；在觸控螢幕上，無論使用哪個工具，都可以用兩指平移和捏合。 縮放工具 選擇 縮放 工具（Z 或 F2），然後： 按一下可在該點放大兩倍； Shift+按一下或按一下右鍵可縮小兩倍； 拖曳出一個矩形，可縮放至該矩形填滿視窗。 按兩下工具的按鈕，可縮放至符合所有物件。 平移 使用任何工具時，按住滑鼠中鍵並拖曳。 選擇 平移 工具（H）並拖曳。 Ctrl+滾輪可上下捲動，Alt+滾輪可左右捲動。 使用捲軸，其範圍涵蓋頁面及其周圍一個頁面大小的區域。 按住捲軸之間角落的「導覽器」按鈕，並將指標移到頁面縮圖上。 PgUp 和 PgDn 可前往上一頁和下一頁。 若要讓滾輪捲動而不是縮放，請在 工具 > 選項 > 工具 的 縮放/平移 頁面上變更滑鼠滾輪動作。之後滾輪會捲動，Shift+滾輪會左右捲動，Ctrl+滾輪則會縮放。請參閱工具選項。 檢視 檢視 選單用來選擇物件的繪製方式：線框 只顯示外框，一般 和 增強 會繪製填色和效果，像素 則會以匯出時的像素顯示繪圖。全螢幕預覽 會在螢幕上單獨顯示頁面；按任意鍵即可返回。僅預覽選取的物件 會將該預覽限制為選取範圍。檢視 選單也可以顯示或隱藏尺規、格點、參考線、出血和可列印區域；請參閱尺規、格點和參考線。

h: 面板顯示的內容 在頁面之間移動
x: 提示面板 提示 面板會在您使用工具時，說明您正在使用的工具。它一開始就是開啟的，位於 屬性 和 物件 旁邊；您可以使用 說明 > 提示 或從 視窗 > 面板 再次開啟它。  面板顯示的內容 首頁會介紹此面板，並列出各種主題，例如繪製線條、形狀、選取、移動和旋轉物件、效果、外框、填色、文字、AI 以及取得說明。每個主題都是一個連結。 主題頁面會說明該主題，並列出相關的工具，每個工具都附有圖示、名稱和用途。按一下工具即可查看其頁面。 工具頁面會告訴您如何使用該工具，每行一個指示，按鍵以粗體顯示，並連結到列出該工具的主題。 物件 頁面會在你選取東西時出現：它會說明你選取的是什麼 (曲線、矩形、文字、點陣圖、群組、裁剪框架、調和、尺度線等，或多個物件)、可以用它做什麼、適用的工具，以及屬性列為它提供的選項。 每個頁面最後都有 深入了解，這是連到本說明中完整解說該工具或主題之頁面的連結。 在頁面之間移動 當您選擇其他工具時，面板會顯示該工具的頁面。面板底部的列左側有 首頁，右側有 上一頁 和向前，就像網頁瀏覽器一樣。 選取物件會顯示它的頁面；按一下空白處取消選取，就會回到目前工具的頁面。使用繪圖工具繪製時，剛畫好的物件不會切換頁面，工具的頁面會保持顯示；按一下物件即可看到它的頁面。

h: 啟動時的訊息 與桌面版的差異
x: 瀏覽器版本 機器翻譯：本頁可能落後於英文版。 您可以在網頁瀏覽器中使用 TraceDraw，不需安裝任何東西。它與桌面版是同一個程式，只是為瀏覽器建置，因此選單、工具和檔案都相同。  啟動時的訊息 每次開啟頁面時，都會有一則訊息說明瀏覽器版本與桌面版是同一個程式，以及兩者有哪些差異。確定（或 Enter）會關閉訊息；另一個按鈕會開啟桌面版的下載頁面。 與桌面版的差異 速度。 大型繪圖、繁重的效果、描繪、馬賽克和大型匯出會比較慢，並且在完成之前讓頁面保持忙碌。桌面版則以全速執行。 檔案。 開啟和匯入會使用瀏覽器的檔案選擇器；儲存、匯出和列印則會下載檔案。不會列出最近的繪圖，因為瀏覽器無法重新開啟已上傳的檔案。 字型。 頁面自帶字型，並會在您的文字第一次需要時擷取更多字型。 設定會保存在該台電腦的該瀏覽器中。 按鍵。 當繪圖取得焦點時，程式的快速鍵會送到 TraceDraw 而不是瀏覽器，但剪貼簿按鍵、重新載入和瀏覽器的開發人員工具除外。Ctrl+N、Ctrl+T 和 Ctrl+W 一律由瀏覽器使用，因此請使用 檔案 選單來建立和關閉繪圖。 螢幕。 它適合搭配滑鼠和鍵盤的桌面瀏覽器。在平板電腦上，請使用觸控工作區（請參閱工作區）；手機螢幕太小，不適合編輯。 巨集。 巨集專案只能在桌面版中載入和執行。在瀏覽器中，任何巨集指令都會顯示說明訊息，並提供前往桌面版下載頁的按鈕。 更新。 瀏覽器版本永遠是最新版；不需要安裝任何東西。有未儲存的變更時，關閉或重新載入分頁、或離開頁面，瀏覽器會先詢問。自動備份保存在瀏覽器為此網站提供的儲存空間，下次開啟時會提供已關閉、重新載入或當機的分頁留下的圖面。安裝為應用程式時，會保留上次使用的版本，並在所有視窗關閉後的下次啟動時取得新版本；請參閱平板電腦與 Android 應用程式。 筆壓。 觸控筆可當作滑鼠使用，但瀏覽器不會傳遞筆壓，因此筆畫寬度一致。

h: Installing the browser version as an app The Android app Touch and pen
x: Tablets and the Android app TraceDraw runs on tablets in two ways: the browser version installed as an app (on an Android tablet, an iPad or a desktop computer), and a native app for Android tablets, phones and Chromebooks. Both are the same editor as the desktop version, with the same menus, tools and files. Installing the browser version as an app The browser version can be installed from the browser. It then opens full screen with the TraceDraw icon, without the browser's address bar and tabs, in any orientation, and keeps clear of a notch or rounded screen corners. Android tablet (Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet): open the page, then the browser's menu and Install app or Add to Home screen. Chrome may also offer it in a bar under the address bar. iPad (Safari): open the page, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. On an iPad or iPhone, as on an Android tablet, the Open and Import dialogs list every file, since the system would grey out .cdr files otherwise; pick a drawing TraceDraw opens. Desktop (Chrome, Edge): click the install icon at the right end of the address bar, or choose Install TraceDraw in the browser's menu. Once it has been opened, the installed app starts without a network connection, at the version you last used (fonts fetched from the web still need a connection the first time your text uses them). A new version is taken the next time the app starts after all its pages and windows were closed. It is the same program as the browser version, so the differences listed in The browser version apply. The Android app The Android app is TraceDraw built for 64-bit ARM tablets and phones and for Chromebooks with Intel or AMD processors. Its installation files (APK) are attached to the releases and to the nightly builds of the project on GitHub. The app does not check for updates itself; Help > Updates opens its store page. A new installation starts in the Touch workspace: larger bars and buttons, no rulers, panels or status bar; two fingers pan and a pinch zooms. Window > Workspace picks another one, and the choice is kept. See Workspaces. What works differently: Files. Open, Import, Save, Save As, Export and Publish to PDF go through the system's document picker. Save writes an opened document back in place. The Save Drawing dialog box asks only for the name, type and version; the system then asks where to save. Recent drawings reopen from the list and the Welcome Screen, as on the desktop. Clipboard. Text goes through the system clipboard: objects copied in TraceDraw paste in other apps as text, and text copied elsewhere pastes as text. Pictures copied in other apps are not read yet. Fonts. The system's fonts are used. Keyboard. A physical or Bluetooth keyboard works with the shortcuts. Help pages open in the browser. Not available on Android: printing, Send To, editing a bitmap in another program, and choosing a folder (such as an export folder or a font folder). Touch and pen On a touch screen, a finger or a pen works the canvas, the toolbox, the bars and the menus. Tap to click, drag to draw or move. In the Touch workspace two fingers pan and a pinch zooms. For pen pressure on desktop systems, see Drawing with a graphics tablet.

t: 將繪圖保存在 GitHub 上
h: 開始之前：權杖 從 GitHub 開啟繪圖 將繪圖儲存到 GitHub GitHub 拒絕儲存時 開啟較早的版本
x: 將繪圖保存在 GitHub 上 TraceDraw 可以從 GitHub 儲存庫開啟繪圖，並以提交 (commit) 的方式存回，桌面版和瀏覽器版皆可。每次儲存都會成為儲存庫歷程中的一個版本，之後可以再次開啟。這些指令位於 檔案 > GitHub。 開始之前：權杖 公開儲存庫不需要權杖即可開啟。若要開啟私人儲存庫以及進行儲存，請在 GitHub 上建立一個細粒度個人存取權杖 (fine-grained personal access token)，並授予該儲存庫內容的讀取和寫入權限，然後將它貼到 權杖 欄位中。 TraceDraw 執行期間會保留權杖。勾選 在這台電腦上記住權杖 可在下次繼續使用；此時權杖會以純文字儲存在您的偏好設定中（在瀏覽器中則儲存在該瀏覽器的儲存空間）。對話方塊也會記住上次使用的儲存庫、分支和路徑。 從 GitHub 開啟繪圖 選擇 檔案 > GitHub > 從 GitHub 開啟。 以 owner/name 的形式或其 github.com 位址輸入 儲存庫。 輸入 分支，或保留空白以使用 main。 輸入 儲存庫中的檔案 的路徑，例如 art/logo.tdraw。 按一下 確定。 繪圖會在新的分頁中開啟，並以檔案名稱命名。它會記住來源位置以及是哪一個版本。  將繪圖儲存到 GitHub 對於從 GitHub 開啟的繪圖，儲存（Ctrl+S）會將它存回。對於任何繪圖，請選擇 檔案 > GitHub > 儲存到 GitHub。 檢查儲存庫、分支和路徑。 撰寫一則 提交訊息，說明變更了什麼（預設為 "Update" 加上檔案名稱）。 按一下 確定。 繪圖會連同其字型儲存為 .tdraw 檔案，並成為該分支上的一個新提交。另存新檔 仍然會將檔案儲存在您的電腦上。  GitHub 拒絕儲存時 如果檔案在您開啟後已在 GitHub 上變更，或者該路徑已經有檔案而您的繪圖並非來自該檔案，GitHub 就會拒絕儲存，對話方塊會告知此情況。請儲存到其他路徑或分支，或先開啟較新的版本。對話方塊也會說明其他問題：權杖遭拒或沒有存取權限、要求過多、儲存庫、分支或檔案不存在、路徑是資料夾、檔案不是繪圖，或繪圖大於 100 MB。 開啟較早的版本 對於從 GitHub 開啟的繪圖，請選擇 檔案 > GitHub > 歷史記錄。方塊中會列出變更過該檔案的提交，最新的在最前面，並顯示其簡短 ID、日期、作者和訊息。選取一個並按一下「開啟」：該版本會以新繪圖的形式開啟，以檔案名稱和提交命名，且不與 GitHub 連結。
線條、形狀和外框 你在 TraceDraw 中繪製的一切都由線條和形狀組成。這些頁面介紹繪製它們的工具、如何逐一節點改變形狀、如何組合和切割它們，以及如何設定繪製其邊緣的外框。 線條和曲線用曲線飛出式選單中的工具繪製，矩形、橢圓、多邊形和其他形狀用各自的工具繪製。任何物件繪製後都可以用 形狀 工具改變形狀。

h: Freehand 2-Point Line Bezier Pen B-Spline Polyline 3-Point Curve Continuing a curve The property bar Editing curves afterwards
x: Drawing lines and curves A line in TraceDraw is a curve: a path made of segments that join at nodes. Segments can be straight or curved. A curve can be open, with two ends, or closed, when its end meets its start, and then it can be filled. The curve tools are in the Curve flyout of the toolbox. Every one of them draws a curve with the default fill and outline of new objects; change them afterwards in the Properties panel or with the color palette. Freehand The Freehand tool (F5) draws a line where you drag, like a pencil. Choose the Freehand tool. Drag on the page. Release the button to finish. TraceDraw follows the pointer and smooths the line when you release it. The smoothing (0 to 100, 50 at first) on the property bar sets how much: a higher value gives fewer nodes and a softer line. When you are zoomed in, the line keeps more detail. To draw a straight line with this tool, click where the line starts and click again where it ends. Hold Ctrl to keep the line to steps of 15 degrees. Esc drops the first click. With a graphics tablet, the pen's pressure sets the width of the line along it; see Drawing with a graphics tablet. 2-Point Line The 2-Point Line tool draws one straight segment: press where it starts and release where it ends, or click twice. Hold Ctrl to keep it to steps of 15 degrees. Bezier The Bezier tool draws precise curves node by node. Choose the Bezier tool. Click to place a corner node (a cusp), or drag to place a smooth node and pull out its handles, which set the direction and the bend of the curve. Go on placing nodes. Double-click or press Enter to finish. To close the curve, click its first node. Esc throws away the curve you are drawing. Hold Ctrl to place the next node in steps of 15 degrees from the last one, or to turn a handle in such steps. Every node snaps to what snapping is set to; see Snapping. While you drag a handle, hold C to make the node a cusp (only the outgoing handle follows), or Alt to move the node itself. Click the last node again to make it a cusp. A handle pulled out of the drawing window (over a panel or a toolbar) ends where you let go. While you draw, Ctrl+Z takes back the last node or handle, one at a time, and Ctrl+Shift+Z puts them back. A finished curve keeps these steps: undoing goes back to drawing it, with the tool chosen again and a line going on from the last node left, so you can undo node by node and draw on at once. What you are drawing shows over any color: the segments placed so far lie on a white line, and the handles are dashed in blue and white. Pen The Pen tool places nodes the same way as the Bezier tool: click for a corner node, drag for a smooth node, double-click or Enter to finish, click the first node to close. While the button is down, the handle follows the pointer, so you see the curve take shape. Its pointer is a pen nib whose tip is where the node goes. Two options sit on its property bar (and on the Curve tools page of the tool options): Preview mode (on at first): a solid blue line on a white one runs from the last node to the pointer, so you see the next segment before you click. Add and delete nodes automatically (on at first): with a curve selected and no curve being drawn, a click on a segment adds a node and a click on a node deletes it. While you draw a curve, every click places the next node, also on a segment or a node of a curve, so drawing never changes other curves by accident. With no curve being drawn, the Pen and Bezier tools also edit the selected curve: drag a node that is not an end node to move it, as with the Shape tool. B-Spline The B-Spline tool draws smooth curves from control points, without handles. Click to place each control point. The curve follows the points, starting at the first and ending at the last, and always stays inside them. While you draw, the control points show as a dashed line. Double-click or press Enter to finish. Click the first point (once there are three) to close the curve into a smooth loop. The result is an ordinary curve; the control points are not kept. Polyline The Polyline tool draws straight segments one after the other: click to add each corner, and double-click or press Enter to finish. Hold Ctrl to keep each segment to steps of 15 degrees. 3-Point Curve The 3-Point Curve tool draws an arc through three points: Drag from where the curve starts to where it ends. Hold Ctrl to keep this line to steps of 15 degrees, for a level arc. Move the pointer to bend the curve, and click the point it passes through. Hold Ctrl for a bow, a part of a circle that stands evenly on the line. Continuing a curve To add to an open curve, select it, then draw with the Freehand, 2-Point Line, Bezier, Pen, B-Spline or Polyline tool starting (or ending) on one of its end nodes. The new line becomes part of the curve: it runs on from that end; when it ends on the curve's other end, the curve closes; when it ends on an end of another part of the same curve, the two parts join. The Bezier and Pen tools also go on from an open curve that is not selected: press on one of its end nodes to select it and draw on. The next segment leaves smoothly, along the mirror of the curve's last handle; drag from the end node to pull a new handle instead, or click the end node a second time to make it a cusp, so the next segment leaves it straight. The pointer shows a node with a line going on from it when you are over an end node, and a ring when a click would close the curve. The curve keeps its look and stays selected, and the change is one undo step. Closed curves, several selected objects and objects inside groups are never continued. The distance that counts as "on the node" is set on the Curve tools page of the tool options; see Tool options. The property bar While a curve tool is active, the property bar shows the position, size, scale, angle and mirror buttons of the selection, its outline width, line style and start and end arrowheads, and a button that closes an open curve. h: Brush Strokes Modes Settings Painterly Brush Brushes and settings
x: Brush strokes and painterly brushes Brush strokes turn a line you draw into a filled shape with a varying width, like ink from a pen or a brush. Painterly brushes paint the outline of an object with marks of chalk, ink, watercolor and other media. Brush Strokes The Brush Strokes tool (I) draws strokes in one of five modes. A Preset, Brush, Calligraphic or Expression stroke stays the path you drew, an open curve of a few nodes, with the brush as its live outline: edit its nodes with the Shape tool afterwards and the brush follows. The Sprayer makes objects instead. To draw a brush stroke: Choose the Brush Strokes tool. Choose a mode and its settings on the property bar or in the Brush Strokes panel. Drag on the page. To turn existing curves into strokes, select them and click Apply to curve in the Brush Strokes panel; the curve stays a curve with the brush as its outline. With a graphics tablet, the pen's pressure sets the width of Preset, Brush and Expression strokes; see Drawing with a graphics tablet.  Modes Calligraphic: a flat nib of the given width, held at the given angle (45 degrees at first). The stroke is thinnest where you move along the nib and widest across it. Preset: a stroke whose width follows a profile: taper both ends (at first), taper start, taper end, bulge, wave or flat. The width is the widest point. Brush: a preset profile with a rough, dry-brush edge. Expression: the width follows the pen's pressure, or with a mouse your speed: slow strokes are wide. The pressure setting scales the effect. Sprayer: shapes (circles, squares, stars, hearts or leaves) placed along the line every spacing (8 mm at first), each between 70% and 100% of the width. Settings Width: 3 mm at first. Angle: the nib's angle, for Calligraphic. Smoothing: 0 to 100 (25 at first). Higher values smooth out wobbles. Pressure: how much the width follows the pen pressure (0.5 at first), for Preset, Brush and Expression. Spacing: for Sprayer. Painterly Brush The Painterly Brush tool, in the same flyout, paints a line made of brush marks. The brushstroke is an ordinary curve with no fill: the Shape tool reshapes it, the outline color colors it, and the marks follow. To paint a stroke: Choose the Painterly Brush tool. Choose a brush, a size and a transparency on the property bar. Drag on the page. To paint the outline of existing objects, click them to select them, then pick a brush: their outlines are painted with it. Changing the size or the transparency changes their brushstrokes. Clear Brushstroke gives the selected objects their plain outline back. Brushes and settings Brush: dry media (Chalk, which is the first, Charcoal, Soft Pastel), wet media (Ink Wash, Watercolour, Dry Brush) and textures (Bristle, Fur, Spray, Speckle, Cloud, Silk Ribbon). Brush size: 0.1 to 200 mm, 5 mm at first. Transparency: 0 to 100%, 20% at first. Most brushes thin out towards both ends. The marks are laid the same way each time the stroke is drawn, exported or printed. With "Scale with object" on, the marks grow and shrink with the object. In SVG and PDF exports the marks become filled shapes with their transparency.

h: Drawing with pressure Turning pressure off Which systems give the pressure
x: Drawing with a graphics tablet A graphics tablet's pen moves the pointer and clicks like a mouse, so every tool works with it. Where the system also tells TraceDraw how hard the pen presses, the Freehand and Brush Strokes tools let that pressure set the width of the stroke: press lightly for a thin line, harder for a wide one. The mouse draws an even width, as before. Drawing with pressure Choose the Freehand tool, or the Brush Strokes tool in the Preset, Brush or Expression mode. Draw with the pen, pressing harder where the stroke should be wider. Freehand: the new line gets a variable-width outline that follows the pressure along it. A feather-light touch gives a hairline, full pressure the full outline width of new lines. You can edit the line with the Shape tool and its outline in the Properties panel, as any line with a variable width (see Outlines). Brush Strokes: the pen scales the width of Preset, Brush and Expression strokes. The Pressure setting of the Brush Strokes panel (0.5 at first) says how much the width follows the pen: at 0.5 a stroke with no pressure is half as wide as at full pressure; at 1 it goes from nothing to the full width. Preset and Brush keep their shape along the stroke (a taper, a wave) and scale it by the pen; Expression takes the pen's pressure in place of the drawing speed. Calligraphic strokes and the sprayer's objects keep their size. The stroke shows as a thin line while you draw and takes its widths when you lift the pen. Apply to a curve in the Brush Strokes panel has no pen, so it builds the stroke without pressure. Turning pressure off The pressure is on at first. To draw with the pen at an even width, turn off Pen pressure sets the width of Freehand and Brush Strokes drags under Graphics tablet on the Curve tools page of Tools > Options > Tools. Which systems give the pressure Windows 8 and later yes yes Linux with X11 yes yes Linux with Wayland no (see below) no macOS yes yes Browser version yes no On a Wayland desktop (the default of several Linux systems) the pen does not reach TraceDraw yet. Start TraceDraw with tracedraw --x11 from a terminal: the window then opens through XWayland, where the pen moves the pointer, clicks and reports its pressure. Tip: For more control over the stroke afterwards, draw with pressure, then adjust the width nodes with the Variable Outline tool.

h: Shape Recognition Sketch
x: Sketching and shape recognition Two tools turn quick hand-drawn strokes into clean objects: the Shape Recognition tool recognizes the shape you meant, and the Sketch tool builds a smooth line from several strokes. Shape Recognition The Shape Recognition tool (Shift+S) turns a freehand stroke into the shape it looks like, as you drew it: a tilted rectangle stays tilted. Choose the Shape Recognition tool. Draw the shape in one stroke. A stroke whose ends come close together is taken as closed. Release the button. What you get: An open stroke that is nearly straight becomes a straight line; otherwise a smooth curve. A closed stroke with four corners near right angles becomes a rectangle. When it is nearly level, it comes out level. A closed, rounded stroke becomes an ellipse, level when nearly level and never tilted when nearly round. A closed stroke with three corners becomes a triangle, and one with four other corners a four-sided shape. Anything else becomes a smooth closed curve. The new object takes the default fill and outline and is selected. On the property bar, Shape recognition sets how readily strokes become shapes, and Smoothing how much the leftover curves are smoothed. Each is None, Lowest, Low, Medium (at first), High or Highest. With recognition at None, every stroke stays a curve. Sketch The Sketch tool (S) lets you build a line from several short strokes, as you would with a pencil. Choose the Sketch tool. Draw a stroke. It is smoothed and selected. Draw the next stroke starting near the end of the first. With Join on, it is added to the same curve. On the property bar, Join adds a stroke to the selected open curve when it starts close enough to its end; the distance beside it sets how close (5 mm at first). Smoothing sets how much each stroke is smoothed, from None to Highest.

h: Drawing with a box Rectangle Corners 3-Point Rectangle Ellipse 3-Point Ellipse The Corners panel
x: Drawing rectangles and ellipses Rectangles and ellipses stay rectangles and ellipses after you draw them: you can change their corners, turn an ellipse into a pie or an arc, and still resize them freely. To edit them node by node, convert them to curves with Object > Convert to Curves. Drawing with a box The Rectangle, Ellipse, polygon, star, spiral, graph paper, common shapes and action lines tools all draw by dragging a box. While you drag, the object itself follows the pointer, with the settings of the property bar. Hold Ctrl to draw a square, a circle or a regular shape. Hold Shift to draw from the center out. You can press or release it while dragging. The start and end points snap to what snapping is set to. The new object takes the default fill and outline (no fill and a thin black outline at first) and is selected. To change those defaults, see Object styles and defaults. Rectangle Choose the Rectangle tool (F6) and drag from one corner to the opposite one. Double-click the tool's button to draw a rectangle the size of the page; hold Shift while you double-click to frame the selection instead. Corners The property bar sets the corners of the selected rectangles, or of new ones when nothing is selected: The corner style: Round (a quarter circle), Scalloped (a quarter circle cut inwards) or Chamfered (a straight cut). The four sizes: top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right. The size is the radius, or for a chamfer how far from the corner the cut starts. A corner is at most half the shorter side. Edit corners together (the lock, on at first) gives all four the size you type in one. Relative corner scaling (on at first): the corners grow and shrink with the rectangle. Turned off, they keep their size when you resize the rectangle and stay round when you stretch it. You can also drag a corner node with the Shape tool to round all corners at once. 3-Point Rectangle The 3-Point Rectangle tool draws a rectangle at an angle: Drag to draw the base line, at any angle (hold Ctrl for steps of 15 degrees). Move the pointer to set the height and click. Ellipse Choose the Ellipse tool (F7) and drag a box. Hold Ctrl for a circle. On the property bar, choose Ellipse, Pie or Arc. For a pie or an arc, set the start and end angles (in degrees, counterclockwise from the right) and the direction. You can also drag the node of an ellipse with the Shape tool to make a pie (drag inside) or an arc (drag outside). 3-Point Ellipse The 3-Point Ellipse tool draws an ellipse at an angle: Drag to draw the center line of the ellipse, at any angle (hold Ctrl for steps of 15 degrees). Move the pointer to set the height and click. The Corners panel The Corners panel rounds, scallops or chamfers the corners of curves, which the rectangle settings cannot do. Open it from Window > Panels.  Select one or more objects. Rectangles, ellipses, polygons and text become curves when the corners are cut. Choose the Operation: Fillet (a round arc that touches both sides), Scallop (a notch, a quarter of a circle around the corner) or Chamfer (a straight cut). Set the Radius for a fillet or scallop (2 mm at first), or the Chamfer distance for a chamfer: the first distance along the side the path comes in on and the second along the side it leaves on. Equal distances keeps them the same. The result shows as a dashed outline on the drawing. Click Apply. A corner is a node where two segments meet at an angle; smooth nodes are not corners. With the Shape tool and some nodes selected, only those corners are cut. A corner whose sides are too short for the cut is skipped. On a stretched object a fillet or scallop still comes out round, with the radius measured on the page.

t: Drawing polygons, stars, spirals and other shapes
h: Polygon Star Spiral Common Shapes Action Lines Graph Paper
x: Drawing polygons, stars, spirals and other shapes These tools draw ready-made shapes by dragging a box. As with rectangles, hold Ctrl to keep the shape regular and Shift to draw from the center; see Drawing with a box. Polygon The Polygon tool (Y) draws a regular polygon. Set the number of points (3 to 500, 5 at first) on the property bar before or after drawing. The first corner is at the top center. Polygons are symmetric: when you move one node with the Shape tool, the matching nodes of every side move with it, so you can turn a pentagon into a flower in one drag. Star The Star tool draws a star. Its property bar starts with two buttons that choose what it draws: Star: a star with the given number of points (5 at first) and sharpness (0.5 at first; 0 makes a polygon, 1 the thinnest spikes). Complex star: a star whose sides cross, made by joining each point to one further on (9 points and sharpness 2 at first). Its middle stays empty. With some numbers of points it is made of several closed shapes, as six points give two triangles. Spiral The Spiral tool (A) draws a spiral, an open curve. On the property bar set the revolutions (1 to 100, 4 at first) and choose a symmetrical spiral, whose turns are evenly spaced, or a logarithmic one, whose turns grow further apart. Hold Ctrl to draw a round spiral. Common Shapes The Common Shapes tool draws ready-made shapes. Click the shape button on the property bar to choose one from five sets: Basic shapes: parallelogram, trapezoid, diamond, triangles, hexagon, octagon, plus, heart, lightning, crescent, ring, cylinder, cube, frame, teardrop, smiley face and no symbol. Arrows: in every direction, chevron, pentagon, notched, striped and bent arrows. Flowchart: process, decision, data, document, terminator, connector, storage and the other usual symbols. Banners: ribbons, waves, scroll, explosion, burst and pennant. Callouts: rectangle, rounded, oval, cloud and line callouts. Then drag a box. The shape becomes one curve with the default fill and outline. Parts that should look separate, such as the faces of a cube, are separate parts of the curve, and holes such as the middle of a ring stay holes whatever the fill. Action Lines The Action Lines tool draws speed lines in a comic-book style: a group of lines (2 to 500, 12 at first) that are parallel (at first) or radial. Their lengths vary, but the same box always gives the same lines. Graph Paper The Graph Paper tool (D) draws a grid of cells: a group of rectangles that fill the box exactly. Set the rows and columns (4 by 3 at first) on the property bar. Hold Ctrl for square cells. The default points, revolutions, rows and columns are also on the tool pages of the options; see Tool options.

t: Shaping curves with the Shape tool
h: Nodes and segments Selecting nodes Moving nodes and bending segments Rounding corners of curves The property bar Aligning nodes Rectangles, ellipses, polygons and other objects
x: Shaping curves with the Shape tool The Shape tool (F10) edits the nodes and segments of a curve: you move nodes, bend segments, add and delete nodes and change how each node joins its segments. Nodes and segments Select a curve with the Shape tool. Its outline shows in the node color, its nodes as small markers, and the first node of each part of the curve as a slightly larger triangle. A selected node shows its control handles: dashed lines that end in an arrow at the control point. A node is one of three types: Cusp: the segments meet at an angle; each handle moves on its own. Smooth: the curve passes through without a corner; the two handles stay in line. Symmetrical: smooth, with both handles the same length. The pointer shows what a press would take: a small square over a node, a dot over a control handle, a wave over a segment. Selecting nodes Click a node to select it alone; Ctrl+click adds it or takes it out of the selection. Shift+click selects every node from the last selected one to the one you click. Drag a marquee around nodes. The property bar's selection mode chooses a rectangular or a freehand marquee; Alt+drag always draws a freehand one, and Alt+Shift+drag adds its nodes to those selected. Tab and Shift+Tab select the next or previous node; Home and End the first or last. Ctrl+A, the select all nodes button, or a double-click on the tool's button selects every node. Moving nodes and bending segments Drag a node to move the selected nodes. Hold Ctrl to move only horizontally or vertically. Nodes snap like drawing points, also to the other nodes and segments of their own curve. Drag a segment to bend it: the point you grab follows the pointer while the nodes at its ends stay. A straight segment becomes curved. Cusp nodes at its ends stay cusp, and their other handles stay where they are. Drag a control handle to change the bend. While you drag a node, a segment or a handle, the page keeps the picture it had before the drag and the curve follows the pointer as the thin line the tool draws over it. The outline, with its width nodes, brush, arrowheads and effects, is drawn again once, when you release the button. The arrow keys nudge the selected nodes (Shift for a larger step, Ctrl for a smaller one). Double-click a segment to add a node there, a node to delete it. Click a segment to mark a spot, then press + to add a node there. Delete or - deletes the selected nodes; + adds a node in the middle of each segment that ends at them. Neighbouring nodes deleted together leave one curve fitted to the old outline, so the shape keeps its general form. With nodes selected, C switches them between cusp and smooth, S between smooth and symmetrical, and Y makes them symmetrical. With nodes selected, Ctrl+C copies the segments between them as new curves, Ctrl+X cuts them out, and Ctrl+D duplicates them. Right-click a node or segment for a menu of the commands below. With several objects selected, the object picked last shows its outline in the node color (blue) and the others in the secondary node color (red), also while a node is dragged, so you can tell them apart. End nodes of two different objects are not joined, by Join nodes or by dropping one on the other: combine the objects first (Object > Combine, Ctrl+L), then join their ends. Rounding corners of curves Rings inside the corners of a curve let you round a corner by dragging. They are off at first, so they do not get in the way of editing nodes; turn on Show corner rounding rings on curve nodes (Shape tool) on the Nodes and Handles page of Tools > Options > TraceDraw to use them. Drag the ring of a corner between two straight sides to round it. A rounded corner keeps its ring: drag it again to change the radius, further in or back to a sharp corner. This also works on corners rounded in saved drawings and with the Corners panel. On a stretched curve the corners come out round on the page, not oval. Rectangles round their corners by their own nodes, whatever this option says. The property bar Selection mode: rectangular or freehand marquee. Add node and Delete node. Join nodes joins two end nodes into one; Break curve splits the curve at the selected node. Convert to line and Convert to curve make the segment ending at the node straight or curved. Cusp, Smooth and Symmetrical set the node type. Reverse direction turns the curve round; Extend curve to close joins two selected end nodes with a straight segment; Extract subpath makes the part of the selected node a curve of its own; Close curve closes an open curve. Stretch and scale nodes and Rotate and skew nodes frame two or more selected nodes with handles: the corner handles scale (or rotate), the side handles stretch (or skew) only those nodes. Align nodes opens the Node Align dialog box (see below). Reflect horizontally and Reflect vertically: moving a node moves the selected nodes on the other side the mirrored way, so both sides of a shape change together. Elastic mode: the selected nodes move less the further they are from the one you drag, down to half as much for the furthest. Select all nodes. Reduce nodes removes nodes that are not needed, from the selected nodes or from the whole curve. Drag the curve smoothness slider to remove more nodes gradually. Aligning nodes To line up nodes: Select two or more nodes with the Shape tool. Click Align nodes on the property bar. In the Node Align dialog box, tick Align horizontal, Align vertical or both, and click OK. The selected nodes move onto a common horizontal or vertical line, or onto one point when both are ticked. The align keys work on the selected nodes too, two or more: L and R line them up with the leftmost or rightmost node, T and B with the top or bottom node, and E puts them on the middle of their height. Their control handles move with them. (C keeps making a node cusp here.) h: Using a shaping brush Smooth Smear Twirl Attract and Repel Smudge Roughen
x: Smoothing, smearing and roughening outlines The shaping brushes of the Shape flyout reshape the outline of an object where you drag over it, like a sculptor's tool: Smooth, Smear, Twirl, Attract and Repel, Smudge and Roughen. Using a shaping brush Select the curves to change. Other objects are converted to curves first. The brushes change only the selected objects: with nothing selected a drag does nothing, and the status bar says to select an object first. Choose the tool and set its Nib size (the radius of the brush, 10 mm at first) and its other settings on the property bar. Drag over the outline. The effect is strongest at the center of the nib and fades to nothing at its edge. Only the parts of the outline within reach change; open curves stay open and closed ones stay closed. Each drag is one undo step. The settings are kept for the next time. Smooth The Smooth tool removes wobbles and extra nodes where you drag. Rate (1 to 100%, 20% at first) sets how strongly. Smear The Smear tool (W) pulls the outline along with the pointer, as if you smeared wet paint. Pressure (1 to 100%, 100% at first) sets how far it moves. Twirl The Twirl tool turns the outline around the pointer into a swirl. Speed (1 to 100%, 50% at first) sets how fast it turns, and the direction buttons choose counterclockwise or clockwise; hold Alt or Shift while dragging to turn the other way. Holding the pointer still keeps turning. Attract and Repel The Attract and Repel tool pulls the nodes inside the nib towards the pointer, or pushes them away. Speed (1 to 100%, 50% at first) sets how fast; choose Attract or Repel on the property bar, or hold Alt or Shift while dragging to swap them. Holding the pointer still keeps going. Smudge The Smudge tool (V) smooths the outline slightly, then smears it, so it is pulled without kinks. Pressure (1 to 100%, 100% at first) sets how far. Roughen The Roughen tool (E) adds jagged spikes along the outline. Frequency (1 to 10 spikes per 10 mm, 5 at first) sets how many, and Spike size (2 mm at first) how tall. The spikes are straight, so they stay sharp.

h: Crop Knife Segment Delete Eraser
x: Cropping, cutting and erasing Four tools of the Crop flyout take parts of objects away: Crop, Knife, Segment Delete and Eraser. Each change is one undo step. Crop The Crop tool removes everything outside a rectangle. Select the objects to crop, or select nothing to crop every unlocked object on the page. Choose the Crop tool and drag the crop area. The drawing outside it is dimmed. Adjust the area: drag inside it to move it, drag one of its eight handles to resize it, or type its position and size on the property bar. Double-click inside the area, press Enter or click Crop on the property bar. To give up, press Esc, click outside the area, click Clear crop area, or choose another tool. What happens to each object: objects wholly inside stay as they are, and objects wholly outside are deleted; closed shapes are cut to the area, and open curves are cut where they cross its edge; text becomes curves first; bitmaps, tables and symbols are placed inside a frame of the area, so their content stays whole and can be taken out again (see Clip frames); groups are cropped member by member. Knife The Knife tool splits objects along a cut. Select the objects to cut, or select nothing to cut every visible object on the page. Choose the Knife tool and the kind of cut on the property bar: Two-point line (a straight cut that runs on across the objects) or Freehand (a cut that follows your drag). Drag across the objects. On the property bar, Split separates the pieces with a hairline gap, so they still meet, and Gap removes a band of the width you type. With Keep as one object, the pieces of each object stay one object made of several parts. Open curves are split where the cut crosses them. Pieces keep the fill, outline and transparency and are selected. Bitmaps, groups and text are not cut. Segment Delete The Segment Delete tool deletes the parts of outlines between the places where they cross other outlines or themselves, for example the bits of lines that stick out past a crossing. Click a part of an outline to delete it. Drag a rectangle across outlines to delete every part it touches, on all objects at once. Each part goes whole, up to the crossings at its ends, even where it reaches past the rectangle; a closed shape that nothing crosses goes whole. Choose Freehand on the property bar and drag a stroke across outlines: every part the stroke crosses is deleted, up to the crossings with other lines, in one step. Hold Alt as a drag starts to use the other way (stroke or rectangle) for that drag only. Rectangles, ellipses and polygons become curves; a closed shape that loses a part opens, and an object with nothing left is deleted. Eraser The Eraser tool (X) rubs out parts of objects. Select the objects to erase, or select nothing to erase the object you start dragging on. Choose the Eraser tool. Set the thickness (6.35 mm at first) and the round or square nib on the property bar. Drag over the objects. A click erases one dot. Erased objects become curves; an object erased completely is deleted. Double-click an object with the tool to delete it whole. Bitmaps, groups and clip frames are not erased. The defaults of the eraser are on the Eraser page of the tool options; see Tool options.

t: Combining shapes: weld, trim and intersect
h: The target and the sources The operations Open lines and pictures The Shaping panel
x: Combining shapes: weld, trim and intersect Shaping builds new shapes from overlapping objects: join them into one, cut one with another, or keep only where they overlap. The commands are in Object > Shaping, on the property bar when two or more objects are selected, and in the Shaping panel. The target and the sources The last object you select is the target: it gives the result its fill, outline and transparency. The other selected objects are the sources. To choose the target, select the sources first, then Shift+click the target. The result goes on top of the active layer and is selected. Each operation is one undo step. When there is no result (for example two objects that do not overlap), nothing changes and the status bar says so. The operations Weld 2 objects one object covering all of them Trim 2 objects the target without what the sources cover Intersect 2 objects only the area all of them share Simplify 1 object each object without what the objects above it cover Front Minus Back 2 objects the front object without the ones behind it Back Minus Front 2 objects the back object without the ones in front of it Boundary 1 object an outline around the whole selection From the menu and the property bar, Weld removes the originals, Trim keeps the sources, Intersect keeps all of them, and Boundary keeps them all. Open lines and pictures An open line cuts a shape. Trim with an open line, polyline or curve as a source crossing a closed target cuts the target along it into separate pieces, each keeping the target's fill and outline. Several lines make more pieces; a line that ends inside the shape cuts nothing, and the status bar says so. Front Minus Back and Back Minus Front split along open lines the same way. An open line as the target of Weld, Trim or Intersect is cut by the closed objects and stays open: Trim keeps the parts outside them, Intersect the part inside, and Weld adds the parts outside to the welded shape. An open line used as a source of Weld or Intersect on a closed object takes no part; to cut a shape along a line, use Trim or the Knife tool (see Cutting and erasing). A picture as the target of Trim, Intersect or Weld is cropped to the result: its frame takes the new shape and the picture shows inside it. Areas filled side by side, and the results of Weld, Trim and Intersect, meet exactly where outlines cross, with no hairline gap between them. The Shaping panel Open the Shaping panel from Object > Shaping > Shaping.  Click one of the seven picture buttons to choose the operation. The panel shows its name, a picture and what it does. For Weld, Trim and Intersect, choose what to keep: Leave original source object and Leave original target object. Each operation remembers its own choice. Select the objects, the target last. Click the button named after the operation. It stays pale until enough objects are selected, and a line says how many are needed. Related: Combine (Ctrl+L) makes several objects one curve without changing their shapes, and Break Apart splits a curve into its parts again. See Objects and layers.

h: To join curves
x: Joining curves The Join Curves panel closes the gaps between the ends of curves, for example lines that should meet at a corner but stop short of it. Open it with Object > Join Curves.  To join curves Select the curves. Open parts inside one curve are joined too. Choose how the ends are joined: Extend: both ends carry on in their directions until they meet, as a corner. When the directions never meet ahead of both ends, a straight line joins them. Chamfer: a straight line between the ends. Fillet: as Extend, then the corner is rounded with the radius (2 mm at first). Bezier curve: a smooth curve that leaves and arrives in the directions of the ends. Set the gap tolerance (5 mm at first). Ends further apart are not joined. Click Apply. The closest pair of ends is joined first, then the next, until no pair is left within the tolerance; the two ends of one part close it. The joined curve takes the place, fill and outline of the curve you selected last, and the other curves are removed. When no ends lie close enough, nothing changes and the status bar says so. You can also join two end nodes of one curve with the Shape tool; see Shaping curves with the Shape tool. Drawing from the end of a selected curve also continues it; see Continuing a curve.

h: Opening the outline settings Outline Pen settings Outline Color Variable Outline
x: Setting outlines The outline is the line drawn along the edge of an object. You set its color, width, style, corners, line ends and arrowheads in the Outline section of the Properties panel. Opening the outline settings The Outline Pen tool (F12) opens the Outline Pen dialog box with every outline setting: color, width and its unit, style, miter limit, dashes, corners, line caps, position, arrowheads, calligraphy, Behind fill, Scale with object, the variable outline's width nodes and Overprint outline. The selected objects show each change live while the dialog box is open. OK keeps only what you changed, on every selected object, as one undo step; Cancel or Esc puts the outlines back. With nothing selected it sets the outline of new objects. The width list offers the same round widths as the property bar, in the outline unit (0.1, 0.2, 0.25 mm and so on).  Double-click the outline part of the status bar. Right-click a color of the palette to color the outline of the selection. Outline Pen settings Width: 0.2 mm for new objects. Hairline draws a line one screen or printer dot wide at every zoom. Paint: the outline can be painted like a fill: none, uniform color, gradient, pattern, texture or mesh. See Fills. Hairlines and arrowheads keep the plain outline color. Caps, the ends of open lines: Butt (at first), Round or Square. Corners: Miter (at first), Round or Bevel. The Mitre limit (45 degrees for new outlines) bevels corners sharper than it, so a thick outline on text or narrow turns does not grow long spikes. Dash: Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash dot. The dashes grow with the width. Arrowheads, at the Start and the End of open lines, filled in the outline color. To make your own, draw it, select it and choose Object > Create > Arrowhead. The nib stretch (0.1 to 1) and nib angle make a calligraphic outline: thinner across the nib than along it, like a flat pen. In the Properties panel they sit with the Mitre limit under the Advanced header after the common settings, closed at first unless one of them is set. Behind fill draws the outline under the fill, so only its outer half shows. Scale with object: the width grows and shrinks when you resize the object. To turn an outline into an object you can fill, choose Object > Convert Outline to Object (Ctrl+Shift+Q). The settings of new objects are explained in Object styles and defaults. Outline Color The Outline Color tool (Shift+F12) opens the Color panel to choose the outline color of the selection. See The Color panel. Variable Outline The Variable Outline tool, in the Shape flyout, makes an outline thicker or thinner along its length with width nodes. Select an object with an outline, such as a curve, a rectangle or an ellipse. An object with no outline gets a thin one. Choose the Variable Outline tool. Drag across the outline: a width node is added where you start, and the outline reaches to the pointer on both sides. Hold Shift (or Alt) as you start dragging to change only the side the pointer is on. Shift+click picks a run of nodes and Ctrl+click adds one; a drag then changes all the picked nodes. Add more nodes the same way. Between nodes the width changes smoothly. To change a node, click it and type the Left width and Right width on the property bar (left is to the left of the path's direction). Delete node or Delete removes the selected node, and Clear variable outline gives back the plain outline.

h: Placing a dimension Parallel Horizontal or Vertical Angular Segment Dimension style Dimensions that follow objects Callout
x: Dimension lines and callouts Dimension lines show the size of things in a technical drawing: a length, a horizontal or vertical distance, an angle or the length of a segment. Callouts point at something with a leader line and a label. Both stay live: when you move, scale or turn them, they are measured and drawn again. Placing a dimension Every dimension is placed in clicks, and the property bar says what to click next. While the last point is wanted, the dimension follows the pointer. Esc starts again. Points snap as drawing does, so snapping to nodes or objects gives exact measures; see Snapping. The new dimension is selected. Parallel The Parallel Dimension tool measures the straight distance between two points, at any angle: Drag from the first point to the second, or click both. Move the pointer and click where the dimension line goes. Horizontal or Vertical The Horizontal or Vertical Dimension tool measures only the horizontal or the vertical distance between two points, whichever is larger. Place it as a parallel dimension. Angular The Angular Dimension tool measures an angle: Click the vertex of the angle. Click a point on the first side, then a point on the second side. Click where the arc goes. The angle is measured counterclockwise from the first side. Segment The Segment Dimension tool measures a segment of an object: click the segment to take its two ends, then click where the dimension line goes. Dimension style The property bar shows these settings with the dimension tools and when the selection is all dimensions. Changes apply to the selected dimensions and to the next ones you make. Precision: 0 to 6 decimals (2 at first). Units: the drawing units (at first) or any other unit. Lengths follow the drawing scale, so at 1:100 a 10 mm line reads 1000 mm; see Document options. Show units: the unit after the number (the degree sign for angles). Prefix and Suffix: text before and after the number. Text: above the line (at first), in the line, or below the line. Label size: 1 to 500 points (10 at first). Font of the label (the font of new text at first) and the label color (black). Line color (black) and line width (a hairline at first, up to 50 mm), for the lines and arrowheads. Arrowheads: arrow (at first), open arrow, dot, tick or none. Round ends: round caps and joins on the lines (off). The Options menu: the extension line gap between the measured points and the extension lines (0), how far the extension lines run past the line (2 mm), horizontal text for linear dimensions (off), join lines at corners (off), which makes the extension lines and the dimension line (or an angle's arc) one line that turns a corner instead of running past it, and a corner radius (0 to 100 mm) that rounds those corners. The menu stays open while you type in it. The label always reads left to right and stays upright. Double-click it with the Pick tool to edit it in place: text that still holds the measured value keeps it live (the text before and after it become the prefix and suffix); text without it shows as typed until you delete it. Dimensions that follow objects A dimension whose ends you placed on an object holds to it: on its nodes (its corners, say), or on its edges (the sides of a rectangle, not only its corners). When you move, resize, turn or reshape the object, the dimension goes along, each end keeping its place on its node or along its edge, and the value changes with it. Moving the dimension by itself lets it go, as does deleting the object or the node it held to. When you move, scale or turn a dimension, it is measured and drawn again: a dimension scaled by 2 reads twice the length, and its label stays upright. Break Apart (Ctrl+K) frees the lines, arrowheads and label as objects of their own, and Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q) makes the dimension a group of plain curves. Either way it is no longer a dimension. Callout The 3-Point Callout tool draws a label with a leader line in two segments. Drag from the tip (what the callout points at) to the elbow, or click both. Click where the text goes. The text goes on that side of the elbow. Type the text. The sample text is selected, so typing replaces it. The leader always ends at the text: when you type more, change the size or move the text on its own (Ctrl+click it), the leader follows. Move the tip or the elbow with the Shape tool. The property bar, shown with the tool and when the selection is all callouts, sets: the outline width of the leader and shape (a hairline at first); the line style; the head at the tip (an arrow at first, or none); the callout shape around the text: none (at first), underline, rectangle, rounded rectangle or ellipse; the gap between the text and the leader or shape (1 mm at first).

h: Anchors Drawing a connector Connector settings Staying attached Editing anchors
x: Connector lines and anchors Connector lines join two objects and stay attached to them: when you move or resize the objects, the connector follows. They are useful for diagrams, flowcharts and organization charts. Anchors A connector attaches to an anchor of each object. Every object has four anchors, at the middle of each side of its bounding box. You can add your own anchors with the Edit Anchor tool; they move and scale with the object. Drawing a connector Three tools in the Connector flyout draw connectors: Straight-Line Connector: a straight line; Right-Angle Connector: horizontal and vertical segments with square corners; Rounded Right-Angle Connector: the same with rounded corners. To join two objects: Choose a connector tool. Drag from one object to the other. While you drag, the anchors of both objects show, and the line starts at the anchor that will be used. Release on the other object. When you start or end the drag on an anchor, that anchor is used; otherwise the closest pair of anchors of the two objects is used. The connector is an open line with no fill and the default outline. Connector settings The property bar, shown with the connector tools and when the selection is all connectors, has the three kinds of connector (with connectors selected, they change how those run), the corner radius of rounded connectors (3 mm at first), and the outline width, style and arrowheads of the selected connectors. Staying attached When you move, scale or reshape the joined objects, the connector runs again between their anchors. When you move the connector together with its objects, it stays attached. When you move the connector on its own, it lets go and becomes a plain line. Undo attaches it again. When one of its objects is deleted, the connector stays where it is. Editing anchors The Edit Anchor tool adds, moves and deletes anchors: Choose the Edit Anchor tool and click an object. Its anchors show as diamonds. Click inside the object to add an anchor there. Drag an anchor you added to move it. Select an anchor and press Delete, double-click it, or click Delete anchor on the property bar to remove it. Remove all custom anchors removes every anchor you added. The four anchors at the middle of the sides cannot be removed.
物件、符號和圖層 繪圖中的每個形狀、線條、文字和圖片都是物件。這些頁面介紹如何選取物件，移動、調整大小、旋轉和對齊它們，如何排列順序、群組以及用圖層組織它們，以及如何把它們當作符號重複使用。 這些頁面也介紹有特殊用途的物件：表格、條碼和 QR 碼、註解以及附加到物件的資料。

h: The Pick tool Moving, resizing and turning Dragging with the right button The property bar Selection groups The Freehand Pick tool
x: Selecting objects Before you change an object, you select it. The Pick tool (Space switches to it from most tools, and Space again takes you back to the tool you were using) selects, moves and resizes objects; the Freehand Pick tool does the same but selects with a freehand loop. The Pick tool Click an object to select it. A filled object counts where it is filled; an unfilled one on its outline. Text, groups, tables and pictures count anywhere inside their box. Shift+click adds an object to the selection or takes it out. Drag around objects, starting on an empty spot: the objects wholly inside the dashed frame are selected. Hold Alt as you finish the drag to select every object the frame touches; held from the start, the frame can start over an object (a background) too. Hold Shift to turn over the objects the frame takes: those selected are deselected and the others added. Hold Ctrl to keep the frame square. Ctrl+click selects an object inside a group, one level further in at each click. Its handles are round, and changes act on it alone; drag it from anywhere on it to move it alone. Ctrl+click on a clip frame starts editing its contents instead (see Clip frames). Alt+click selects the object beneath the selected one, to reach objects that are covered. Tab and Shift+Tab select the next or previous object. Esc selects nothing. Edit > Select All and a double-click on the tool's button select every object; Select All also selects all text, guidelines or nodes. The selected objects show eight square handles around them and a small cross in the middle. The status bar says what is selected and on which layer. The pointer shows the move arrows only over what is selected. Over any other object it keeps the plain arrow, since a press there picks that object first; dragging an unselected object still picks and moves it. A right click while you drag a selection frame is ignored: the frame goes on and selects when you let go of the left button. Drawing and shaping tools whose click has no job of its own (the rectangle, ellipse, polygon and other shape tools, the Knife, the connectors, Blend and others) select too: click an object to select it, Shift+click to add or take it away, Ctrl+click to reach into groups, and click empty space to select nothing. A drag still draws. The line tools and the Text tool keep their clicks. Moving, resizing and turning Drag a selected object, or the cross in its middle, to move it. Hold Ctrl to move only horizontally or vertically. The object snaps to what snapping is set to. Drag a corner handle to resize in proportion, a side handle to stretch in one direction. Hold Shift to resize from the center, Ctrl to resize in steps of 100% (crossing the other side mirrors the object), Alt to resize freely. Click a selected object again to show the rotation handles: drag a curved corner arrow to rotate, a side arrow to skew. Hold Ctrl for steps of 15 degrees. Drag the ring in the middle to turn about another point; double-click it to put it back in the middle. In this rotate mode, a node of the selection (or the middle of a segment) dragged turns the selection about the ring; let go near another object's edge and the node lands exactly on it, so an arc turned about one end can be laid onto a line. The rotate handle still snaps to other objects' nodes, midpoints and centres to aim the turn at one. While dragging, press Space or click the right button to leave a copy where the objects were; Esc cancels the drag. The arrow keys nudge the selection by the nudge distance (2.54 mm at first), with Shift by the super nudge distance and with Ctrl by the micro nudge distance. Set them on the Rulers page of the document options. + duplicates the selection in place. Dragging with the right button Drag a selected object with the right mouse button. When you release, a menu offers to move it there, copy it there, copy its fill, outline or all its properties to the object under the pointer, or place it inside that object as a clip frame. The property bar With nothing selected, the property bar shows the page size and orientation, the drawing units and the nudge distance. With a selection, it shows the position (X and Y), the size (W and H), the scale, the rotation angle, the mirror buttons, the outline width, to front and to back, and convert to curves. Text adds the text settings, and bitmaps the bitmap commands. With several objects, a group or a curve of several parts, it adds group, ungroup, combine, break apart, the shaping commands and the Align and Distribute panel. Selection groups Press Ctrl and a number from 0 to 9 to remember the selection under that number. Press the number alone to select those objects again, and again to zoom to them. Alt and the number add the selection to the group. Groups are saved with the drawing. The Freehand Pick tool The Freehand Pick tool works like the Pick tool, but a drag from an empty spot draws a loop. When you release, every object wholly inside the loop is selected; hold Alt as you release to select every object the loop touches, Shift to add to the selection. Hold Ctrl to draw a rectangle instead. The options of the Pick tool, such as whether a frame selects the objects it touches, are on the Pick page of the tool options; see Tool options.

h: The Transformations panel Position Rotate Scale and Mirror Size Skew The Free Transform tool Undoing transformations The Coordinates panel
x: Moving, scaling, rotating and skewing You can transform objects by dragging them with the Pick tool (see Selecting objects), by typing values on the property bar, with the Free Transform tool, or precisely with the Transformations panel. The Transformations panel Open the panel with Object > Transformations, or with Alt+F7 (Position), Alt+F8 (Rotate), Alt+F9 (Scale and Mirror) and Alt+F10 (Size). The buttons at the top choose one of five pages.  Every page ends with the reference point, a 3 by 3 grid that chooses the point of the selection that is placed, turned about or kept still (the center at first), Copies and Apply. Distances are in the drawing units, angles in degrees (counterclockwise), scales in percent. To transform the selection: Choose a page and type the values. Choose the reference point. Set Copies: 0 changes the selection itself; a number above 0 leaves the selection as it is and adds that many copies, each transformed once more than the one before. The copies are one undo step, and the last copy becomes the selection, so another Apply goes on from there. Click Apply. Position X and Y move the selection. With Relative position on (at first), they are a distance to move by; off, they are where the reference point goes, counted from the ruler origin. With Relative position on, the grid picks a direction: a side or a corner sets the distance to the selection's size, so each copy lands right next to the last one. Rotate Type the angle, and the Center to turn about. With Relative center on (at first), the center is counted from the reference point; off, from the ruler origin. Scale and Mirror X and Y scale in percent (100% at first). Mirror horizontally and Mirror vertically flip the selection. Proportional keeps both scales the same. Size W and H set the width and height of the selection. Proportional keeps the proportions. Skew X and Y slant the selection by angles. With Use anchor point on, the reference point stays still; off, the center does. The Free Transform tool The Free Transform tool, in the Pick flyout, transforms the selection about the point where you press. Choose a mode on the property bar: Free rotation (at first): turns the selection around the press point. Free angle reflection: mirrors the selection across the line from the press point to the pointer; moving the pointer turns that line. Free scale: scales about the press point. Free skew: horizontal movement skews horizontally, vertical movement vertically. Hold Alt to scale, Ctrl to skew or Shift to reflect for one drag, whatever the mode. With Apply to duplicate on, the press makes a copy and the drag transforms the copy, leaving the original as it was. The property bar also has the position, size, scale, angle and mirror fields. One drag is one step: Ctrl+Z puts the selection back as it was before the drag (and takes the copy away). Undoing transformations Object > Clear Transformations takes the selected objects back to how they were before they were scaled, rotated or skewed. The Coordinates panel The Coordinates panel draws an object from typed coordinates, or reshapes the selected one, with a dashed preview on the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels.  Choose the kind of object with the buttons at the top: rectangle or square, ellipse or circle, polygon or regular polygon, star, complex star, 2-point line or multipoint curve. Type its values: rectangles and ellipses: the position of the origin point (chosen in a 3 by 3 grid), the width and height, the angle of rotation, and the corners of the bounding box while the angle is 0; squares and circles: the position, the side or diameter and the angle; polygons and stars: the number of points or sides, the sharpness, the angle and the circle the points lie on; regular polygons: the number of sides, the length of a side, the angle and the center; 2-point lines: the start point and end point, or the length and angle; multipoint curves: the list of points, with buttons to add and delete points and to close the curve. Instead of typing, click a button with a pointer and target, then click or drag on the drawing to set that value. A right click cancels. Click Create object to add it, or Replace object to reshape the selected rectangle, ellipse, polygon or curve while keeping its fill, outline, name and place. Positions are counted from the ruler origin, in the drawing units.

h: Aligning Distributing Fit objects to a path
x: Aligning and distributing objects Aligning lines objects up by their edges or centers; distributing spaces them evenly. Use the Align and Distribute panel, the commands of Object > Align and Distribute, or the keys below.  Aligning Select the objects. Select the one the others should line up with last. In the Align part of the panel, choose Align to: Active object (at first): the object selected last; with one object selected, the page; Page edge: the edges of the page; Page center: the center of the page; Grid: each object to the nearest line of the document grid. Click one of the six buttons: left edges, centers on a vertical line, right edges, top edges, centers on a horizontal line, or bottom edges. Use outline: align the outer edges of the outlines: with this on, the outer edges of the outlines meet, instead of the paths themselves. The keys always align to the object selected last: L Align Left R Align Right T Align Top B Align Bottom E Align Centers Horizontally C Align Centers Vertically P Center to Page Distributing Select three or more objects (two or more to distribute across the page). In the Distribute part, choose Distribute to: Selection extent (at first): the first and last objects stay where they are, and the others move between them; Page extent: the objects spread across the whole page, the first touching one side and the last the other. Click one of the eight buttons: left edges, centers, gaps or right edges across the page, or top edges, centers, gaps or bottom edges down it. Spreading the gaps gives equal space between the objects whatever their sizes. With too few objects the buttons are pale and the panel says how many are needed. Each align or distribute is one undo step. To place copies at even distances in one step, see Step and repeat. Fit objects to a path The Fit Objects to Path panel places objects along a line, a curve or the outline of a shape, with copies, spacing, placement and rotation of your choice. Select the objects, then the path last (Shift+click), and choose Object > Fit Objects to Path. See Fitting objects to a path for every setting.

h: Placing objects on a path The settings Objects and path Spacing Copies Placement Rotation Order Tips and limits
x: Fitting objects to a path The Fit Objects to Path panel places objects along a line, a curve or the outline of a shape: beads on a string, letters or stars round a seal, a row of fence posts along a road, dashes of your own along a border. It can make copies to fill the path, space them evenly or at a set distance, stand them on the path or turn them with it. Placing objects on a path Select the objects to place, then the path last (Shift+click). The panel shows how many objects are selected and what kind of object the path is. Choose Object > Fit Objects to Path to open the panel. Change the values you need (see below). Once a value changes, dashed outlines on the canvas show where every object and copy will go. Click Apply. Fitting undoes in one step. Copies go into the layer of the object they copy, with its fill, outline and effects. After an Apply that made copies, the objects placed and the copies are selected (not the path). The panel starts from the default values, with no outlines, each time you select other objects or work in another drawing; the values you enter stay while the same objects are selected. The settings The panel's groups, from top to bottom: Objects and path Keep originals (off): the selected objects stay where they are and copies of them are placed. Group all objects (off): what was placed goes into one group, which is selected. Treat subpaths as contiguous (on): a path made of several pieces is walked piece after piece, as one path. Off, only the first piece is used. Spacing Spacing: Evenly along the path (the default) spreads the objects over the whole path; Fixed distance puts them the Distance apart (10 mm at first). Measure between: between the Centers of neighbouring objects (the default) or between their Edges, so objects of different sizes get the same gap. Start offset (0): moves the first object along the path from its start. A negative value is allowed. End offset (0, open paths only): keeps the objects away from the end of the path. Place the row at (fixed distance only): puts the row at the Start (the default), in the Middle or at the End of the path. Copies Each object once (the default): each selected object is placed once. Number of objects (1 to 1000, 10 at first): that many objects in all: the selected ones, then copies of them in the same order. Fill the path (fixed distance only): as many as fit on the path. There are never more than 1000 objects in all. Placement Placement: On the path (the default), Above the path or Below the path, with a Distance from the path (0 at first) between the objects and the path. "Above" is on the left of the path's direction. Reference: the point of each object that goes on the path: its Center of rotation (the default; the centre, or where you moved it with the Pick tool), or a point of its Bounding box or Bounding box with outline. Origin (box references only): one of nine points of the box, picked in the grid (the centre at first). The bottom middle point makes the objects stand on the path. Rotation Rotation: Rotate objects to follow the path turns each object with the direction of the path; Fixed angle (the default) turns them all alike. The Angle (0, in degrees counterclockwise) is added in either case. Ignore initial rotation (off): straightens objects that were turned before they are placed. Under Modify rotation, the Style adds a turn to every object: None (the default): no extra turn. Uniform: every object turns by the Start angle. Progressive: each object turns a little more than the one before, the Spin angle (360 at first) times the Revolutions (1) over the whole row. Jitter: each object turns by a different amount, up to the Range (±) (15 degrees) either way. The same object turns the same way every time, in the preview and after Apply. Progressive jitter: both. Tick Clockwise to turn the other way. Only the fields the style uses can be changed. Order Order: which object goes first: As selected (the default), Reversed, Left to right, Right to left, Largest first, Smallest first, Large and small in turn, Top to bottom, Bottom to top, Tall to short, Short to tall, Wide to narrow, Narrow to wide or Random (shuffled the same way each time for the same objects). Reverse direction (off): starts from the other end of the path. Tips and limits On a closed shape the objects go all the way round, the closing side included, without the first and last meeting. On an open path, an object that would land past an end stays at that end. With more than 200 objects each one previews as its box; with more than 200 selected there is no preview, but Apply works. To place text along a path instead, see Adding and editing text. To spread objects in a straight row, see Aligning and distributing.

t: Making copies with Step and Repeat
