h: To make copies
x: Making copies with Step and Repeat The Step and Repeat panel makes several copies of the selection, each moved by the same distance from the one before: a row of buttons, a column of lines, a grid of tiles. Open it with Edit > Step and Repeat (Ctrl+Shift+D).  To make copies Select the objects to copy. Set the number of Number of copies (1 to 999). Under Horizontal settings, choose how the copies are spaced across: Offset: the distance from one copy to the next, measured from the same point of each; Spacing: the gap between one copy and the next, so the copies never overlap whatever their size. Then type the distance. 0 keeps the copies in line. Do the same under Vertical settings. Click Apply. The copies are added to the active layer and selected. Distances are in the drawing units. The values stay as you typed them: after an Apply (the copies it made are selected) and for the next objects you select, the panel keeps the same number of copies, distances and modes until you change them. With nothing selected the fields wait, keeping their values. A new session starts from one copy, 6.35 mm across and 0 down. To copy with a rotation or a scale at each step, use the Copies field of the Transformations panel; see Moving, scaling, rotating and skewing.

h: The Objects panel Layers Master layers Renaming objects and layers Changing the order Grouping and combining Locking and hiding objects
x: Organizing objects and layers The Objects panel shows how the current page is organized: its layers, the objects on each layer, the groups and the master layers that appear on every page. Use it to select, name, hide, lock and order objects and layers. Objects higher in the list are drawn in front.  The Objects panel The panel lists the page with its layers, topmost first, then the Master Page with the master layers, the guidelines (Guides) and the Document Grid. Each object shows a thumbnail, the object itself drawn small with its fill and outline, and its name, or what it is when it has none ("Rectangle", "Curve with 8 nodes"). Click an object to select it; Shift+click adds it to the selection. Its layer becomes the active layer. Click the arrow of a group to see the objects inside it. Each layer has three buttons: Show/hide, Print and export the layer and Lock layer. A hidden or locked layer cannot be edited. The padlock of Guides locks all the guidelines of the page. Hidden objects show their name and thumbnail dimmed. To make the thumbnails larger or smaller, drag the slider between the small and the large square at the bottom of the panel, turn the mouse wheel over it, or hold Ctrl and turn the wheel over the list. The size is remembered. A thumbnail is drawn again only when its object changes, so long lists stay quick. Layers A layer is a sheet on which objects lie. The active layer, shown in bold with a colored bar, is where new objects go when you draw, paste, duplicate or import. Click a layer to make it active. New Layer, at the bottom of the panel, adds a layer on top and makes it active. Right-click a layer for Rename, Move up, Move down and Delete layer. A page always keeps one layer. Delete at the bottom of the panel deletes the selected objects, or the active layer when nothing is selected. Master layers Objects on a master layer appear on every page, under the page's own layers: use them for a logo, a header or page numbers. Click the New Master Layer (All Pages); right-click for odd or even pages button to add one for all pages; right-click it to add one for odd or even pages only. A master layer's menu has Show on to choose All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. You can select and edit master objects from any page they show on. To put a master layer over the page's own objects, tick In front of the page's layers in its menu, or select one of its objects and choose Object > Order > To Front of Page (Ctrl+Home); To Back of Page (Ctrl+End) puts the layer behind the page's objects again. Renaming objects and layers Double-click a layer or an object in the panel, or choose Rename from its menu, to open the Rename Layer or Rename Object dialog box. Type the new name and click OK. An object with an empty name shows what it is again. Double-click the page row to rename the page.  Names help you find objects in the panel and in Find and replace, and are kept in exported SVG files. Changing the order Object > Order moves the selected objects: To Front of Page, To Back of Page, To Front of Layer, To Back of Layer, Forward One, Back One, In Front Of, Behind (click the object to go in front of or behind) and Reverse Order. Grouping and combining Object > Group > Group (Ctrl+G) makes the selection one group that moves and resizes together. Ungroup (Ctrl+U) splits it again, and Ungroup All also splits the groups inside it. To edit an object inside a group without ungrouping, Ctrl+click it. Combine (Ctrl+L) makes the selected objects one curve of several parts, with one fill and outline; where the parts overlap, holes appear. Break Apart (Ctrl+K) splits a curve into its parts. Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q) turns a rectangle, ellipse, polygon or text into a curve you can edit node by node. Locking and hiding objects Object > Lock > Lock Object keeps the selected objects from being selected or changed; Unlock Object and Unlock All Objects release them. Object > Hide > Hide Object hides the selected objects; Show All Objects shows them again. In the Objects panel every object's row has its own eye and padlock, to hide or show and lock or unlock it from the list, a locked object too. Selecting an object on the page scrolls the list to its row, so an object far down a long list comes into view. To keep objects out of the way while you work on others, see also Focus mode.

h: With objects selected With nothing selected
x: The Properties panel The Properties panel (Alt+Enter) shows and changes the properties of the selected objects: their outline, fill, transparency and more, depending on what is selected. It is open at first, beside Hints and Objects. Open it again with Object > Properties.  With objects selected The top of the panel names the selected object (and how many more are selected) and gives its position and size. Under it, a row of buttons opens and closes each section the object has: QR code, for a QR code: its content and look; see Barcodes and QR codes. Outline: color, width, paint, caps, corners, dashes, arrowheads and more; see Setting outlines. Fill: the kind of fill and its settings; see Fills. F11 opens this section. Transparency: how much of what lies below shows through; see Transparency. Rectangle, for rectangles: the corner settings; see Corners. FX: the bitmap effects applied to the object; see Bitmap effects. Character, for text: the font, size, Bold and Italic, and a button to Edit with the Text tool (F8). Summary: a summary of the object. The sections you closed stay closed the next time. A change applies to every selected object and is one undo step. With nothing selected With nothing selected, the panel says No objects selected and shows the Default properties for new objects: the fill and outline that new shapes and lines get. Change them here to draw with other colors from the start. See Object styles and defaults.

h: To place objects inside a frame Editing what is inside Opacity masks Empty frames
x: Placing objects inside a frame A clip frame is a closed object that holds other objects and shows only the parts of them that lie inside it, like a picture in a window. The frame keeps its own fill and outline; the objects inside stay whole and can be taken out again. The commands are in Object > Clip to Frame. To place objects inside a frame Select the objects to place inside. Choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame. Click the closed object that will be the frame. The objects keep their position. You can also drag the objects onto the frame with the right mouse button and choose to place them inside; see Dragging with the right button, or drag them onto the frame with the Pick tool holding W or Alt before you release. Editing what is inside Edit Contents enters the frame: only the objects inside can be edited, the rest of the page is dimmed and the frame shows as an outline. Finish Editing Contents, the button on the property bar, or Ctrl+click off the objects inside leaves it. Extract Contents makes the objects inside ordinary objects again; the frame stays, empty. Lock Contents to Frame (on at first): moving, scaling or rotating the frame takes the contents along. Turned off, the frame moves alone and the contents stay where they are on the page. Double-clicking a frame with the Pick tool, or Ctrl+click on it, also enters it, with the object under the pointer selected; see Focus mode. While you edit the contents, the dimmed objects outside the frame cannot be picked (by a click, a marquee, Select All or Tab). Undo stops at the start of the edit: undoing past it leaves the edit with the frame as it was; redo enters it again, and undoing Finish goes back into it. Opacity masks Object > Clip to Frame > Opacity Mask turns the selected clip frames into opacity masks: the frame is no longer drawn, and its brightness decides how much of the contents shows: fully where it is white, not at all where it is black, and nothing outside the frame. Fill the frame with a gradient for a soft fade. Invert Mask swaps that, so black shows. Choose the command again to turn the mask back into a plain frame. Empty frames Right-click an object and use its frame type commands: Create empty clip frame turns each selected object into an empty clip frame, ready to hold objects. No frame turns an empty clip frame back into the object it was. Create empty text frame replaces the object by an empty paragraph text frame of its size, ready for the Text tool. Cropping a bitmap with the Crop tool or the Shape tool also places it in a clip frame; see Cropping, cutting and erasing.

h: To create a symmetry Editing a symmetry Removing or keeping the copies
x: Drawing with symmetry Symmetry draws live mirrored copies of an object across one or more mirror lines. The copies follow every change you make to the original, so you draw one half (or one slice) and see the whole. The commands are in Object > Symmetry. To create a symmetry Select an object. Choose Object > Symmetry > Create New Symmetry (Alt+S). A vertical mirror line is placed at the right edge of the object, so the copy appears next to it, and TraceDraw goes straight into editing the symmetry. Editing a symmetry Edit Symmetry (Alt+E) edits the symmetry of the selected object. A bar at the top left of the drawing window sets: the number of mirror lines, 1 to 12, spread evenly around the center. With more lines you get a kaleidoscope: with n lines there are 2*n* - 1 copies; the center (X and Y); the angle of the first line (0 to 360 degrees); Show full preview (copies drawn in full, or as red outlines when off) and Show symmetry lines. Edit the originals as usual, with any tool; the copies follow. A click or a marquee picks one of the originals inside the symmetry, and objects you draw, paste or duplicate join it. Drag a mirror line with the Pick tool to move the lines; click a line to show round handles at its ends and drag one to turn the lines. While an object with symmetry is selected or edited, its mirror lines show as dashed lines. Click Finish on the bar, or choose Finish Editing Symmetry (Alt+Shift+E), to stop editing. Removing or keeping the copies Remove Symmetry (Alt+Shift+S) removes the symmetry; the copies go away. Break Symmetry Link (Alt+X) turns the copies into objects of their own, which no longer follow the original.

h: Entering and leaving focus mode While in focus mode Settings
x: Focus mode Focus mode lets you edit the objects inside a group or a clip frame without ungrouping it, with the rest of the drawing faded behind it. Entering and leaving focus mode Double-click a group or a clip frame with the Pick tool. Or right-click an object and choose Bring into focus. For an object inside a group, the group gets the focus and the object stays selected. Double-click a group inside the focused group to go one level deeper. Press Esc with nothing selected to go up one level, and leave focus mode from the top. The cross on the breadcrumb bar leaves at once. While in focus mode A bar at the top left of the drawing window shows the name of the drawing, then each group on the way down. Click a step to go back to that group, or the name of the drawing to leave focus mode. Clicks and marquees select the objects inside the focused group, so you can move, color or delete them with the Pick tool as usual. Everything else is faded. Exports and printing are not affected. Settings How faded the other objects are is set by the visibility of inactive objects (0 to 100%, 20% at first) on the Edit page of Tools > Options > TraceDraw. Whether a double-click enters focus mode is set on the same page. See TraceDraw options.

h: Making a symbol Placing instances Turning instances back into objects
x: Symbols A symbol is an object you define once and place many times. Each copy, called an instance, is a link to the definition: edit the definition and every instance changes. Symbols keep files small and repeated parts the same. They are listed in the Symbols panel (Ctrl+F3).  Making a symbol Select the objects that make up the symbol. Click New symbol from selection in the Symbols panel, or choose Object > Symbol > New Symbol or Object > Create > Symbol. The selection becomes the first instance of the new symbol. Placing instances The panel lists the symbols of the drawing, each with the number of its instances. Click Insert beside a symbol to place a new instance, or choose Object > Symbol > Insert Symbol. Instances can be moved, scaled and turned like any object. An instance copied in one drawing and pasted in another brings its symbol along (and the symbols it shows), so it shows the same objects there. Pasting again reuses the symbol already brought. Turning instances back into objects Select instances and click Revert to objects, or choose Object > Symbol > Revert to Objects. They become ordinary objects that no longer follow the symbol.

h: Adding and editing data
x: Object data The Object Data panel attaches your own information to an object, as named fields: a part number, a price, a note. The data is saved with the drawing and goes with the object when you copy it.  Adding and editing data Select an object. With nothing selected, the panel says Select an object.. The panel lists the object's fields in two columns, Field and Value. Click a name or a value to edit it. Click Add field to add a field, or one of the buttons for a common field: Name, Cost, Comments and CDRStaticID. Click the x at the end of a row to remove the field. When the selected objects have a Cost field with a number, the panel shows their total cost. Some features keep their own data in objects, such as dimension lines, callouts, connectors and anchors; you rarely need to change those fields by hand.

h: To add a link Bookmarks Links in exported files
x: Links and bookmarks The Links and Bookmarks panel gives objects a hyperlink, so a click on them in an exported PDF, SVG or web page opens a web address, writes an email or goes to another page. It also lists the named objects of the drawing as bookmarks. Open it from Window > Panels.  To add a link Select one or more objects. Type the address in the Hyperlink field and leave the field. The buttons Web, E-mail and Page put https://, mailto: or #page= in front of the text, so for a page link you only type its number. Click Remove to take a link away, or empty the field. Bookmarks Under Bookmarks (named objects), the panel lists one button per object that has a name. Click one to select the object and zoom to it. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers. Links in exported files In PDF files, each linked object becomes a clickable area over its box. A page link goes to the top of that page of the file. PDF/X files get no links, as those standards do not allow them. In SVG and web pages, the object itself is the link. A link on a group covers all its objects; the links of the objects inside are left out.

h: To paste in another form
x: Paste Special Edit > Paste Special chooses how the content of the clipboard comes into the drawing, when it could come in more than one way: for example text copied from another program can become a text object, and an SVG copied from a web page can become editable shapes or a picture.  To paste in another form Copy something, in TraceDraw or in another program. Choose Edit > Paste Special. Under Paste as, choose one of the forms the clipboard offers: Objects (internal clipboard): objects copied in TraceDraw, as they were; Vector objects (SVG text): SVG text, turned into shapes you can edit; Bitmap: an image, as a bitmap; Artistic text: plain text, as a line of text. Click OK. When the clipboard holds nothing that can be pasted, the dialog box says The clipboard is empty. The ordinary Paste (Ctrl+V) pastes in the first form available, and Paste in View (Ctrl+Shift+V) pastes in the middle of the window.

h: Adding to the Shelf Placing an item Arranging items Removing an item Where the Shelf is kept
x: The Shelf The Shelf panel keeps objects and colors apart from any drawing, so you can place them in this drawing or another one, today or after TraceDraw restarts: logos, stamps, frames, a set of colors. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click a selection and choose Add to Shelf.  Adding to the Shelf Select objects and click Add Selection. The item is named after the object (its name, or what it is), or "n objects". Symbols become plain objects, and the object styles they use go along. Click Add Colours to keep the colors of the drawing's document palette and its color styles as one item. The Shelf holds up to 500 items. Placing an item Drag an item onto the drawing to place a copy under the pointer. Double-click an item, or choose it and click Place, to place a copy in the middle of the view. The copies go on the active layer and are selected; one undo removes them. A color item adds its colors to the document palette and its color styles to the drawing. Arranging items Click an item to choose it. Right-click it for Place, Rename and Remove. Drag an item onto another to move it to that place. Removing an item Choose an item and click Remove. Removing cannot be undone, so TraceDraw asks first: click Remove to confirm or Cancel to keep it. Tick Do not ask again to remove items without asking; to be asked again, turn on Before an item is removed from the Shelf on the Warnings page of the global options.  Where the Shelf is kept On the desktop, the Shelf is a file in your preferences folder. In the browser, it is kept in that browser's storage, which holds only a few megabytes, so large bitmaps may not be kept.

h: Finding and replacing text Finding objects Finding and replacing by properties
x: Finding and replacing The Find and Replace panel (Ctrl+F) finds text in the drawing, and replaces it, finds objects by name, or finds objects by their fill, outline, outline width, font or type and replaces those. Open it with Edit > Find and Replace.  Finding and replacing text Choose Text. Type what to look for in Find, and the new text in Replace with. Tick Match case to tell capitals from small letters, and Whole words only to skip the text when it is part of a longer word. Click Find Next to select the next text object that holds it, or Find All to select them all. Click Replace to replace it in the selected text, or Replace All to replace it everywhere. The panel says how many were found. Finding objects Choose Objects, type part of a name, or a kind of object such as "Rectangle", and click Find Next or Find All. The search covers the current page. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers. Finding and replacing by properties Choose Properties. In Look in, choose This page or Whole drawing. Under Find objects with, tick what to look for: Type, Fill, Outline (a colour, or None), Outline width or Font. An object is found when it has everything ticked. From Selection takes these from the selected object, for example to find every object filled with its colour. Click Previous or Find Next to select the objects one by one (on other pages too), or Find All to select those on this page. To change them, tick under Replace with the new fill colour, outline colour, outline width or font, and click Replace All. All the changes undo in one step. A fill colour looked for is replaced wherever it is used, in gradients too. Locked objects are left as they are. For every option, how colors are compared and what each replacement does, see Finding and replacing by properties.

h: Finding objects Replacing properties How objects are compared
x: Finding and replacing by properties The Properties mode of the Find and Replace panel finds objects by how they look and what they are: every object filled with one red, every outline 0.2 mm wide, every text in a font you no longer want, every bitmap. It then selects them, or changes their fill, outline or font all at once. Finding objects Choose Edit > Find and Replace (Ctrl+F) and click Properties. In Look in, choose This page (the default) or Whole drawing (every page, then the master layers). Under Find objects with, tick what to look for. An object is found when it has everything ticked: Type (off; Rectangle at first): only objects of one kind: Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon or star, Curve, Artistic text, Paragraph text, Group, Bitmap, Clip frame, Table or Symbol. Fill (on; black at first): objects filled with this color, as a uniform fill or in a gradient or mesh fill, or None for objects without a fill. Outline (off): objects whose outline has this color, or None for objects without an outline. Outline width (off; 0.2 mm at first, in the outline unit): objects whose outline has this width. Font (off): text that uses this font family, in any mix of capitals and small letters. To look for what an object has, select it and click From Selection: its fill color (or none), outline color (or none), outline width and font fill the fields, ticked where it makes sense (the width and the type stay unticked). Reset clears everything back to the defaults. Click a button: Previous or Find Next selects the objects found one at a time, going round at the end. With Whole drawing, the page of each object comes into view. Find All selects every object found on the current page. The status bar says how many were found in all and how many on this page. The panel shows the number of objects found. Replacing properties Find the objects as above. Under Replace with, tick what to change and set the new value: Fill: when a fill color is looked for, that color is replaced by the new one wherever it is used, in gradients and mesh fills too; otherwise the objects get a uniform fill of the new color. Outline: when an outline color is looked for, outlines of that color take the new one; otherwise every outline does. Objects without an outline stay without one. Outline width: every outline of the objects found takes the new width. Font: when a font is looked for, text in that font takes the new one; otherwise all the text of the objects found does. Click Replace All. All the changes undo in one step. The status bar says in how many objects something changed. Locked objects, and objects on locked layers, are found but left as they are. How objects are compared Colors count as the same when they are in the same model with every value within half a percent, or, in different models, when they show as the same color on screen. A spot color matches the same ink at the same tint, and the registration color matches only itself. Widths count as the same within half a thousandth of a millimetre. In groups and clip frames, the objects inside are checked at any depth, and the group is found when one of them matches. With only Type ticked, the group's own type counts. Only objects at the top level are selected, since those are what you can select. To find text or names instead, see Finding and replacing.

h: Adding a comment Reading and answering
x: Comments The Comments panel collects review notes on a drawing: pins, boxes and arrows on the page, each with a text and replies. Comments are saved with the drawing (in .tdraw files) and are never printed or exported. Open the panel from Window > Panels.  Adding a comment Type your name in Name. It signs your comments and replies. Left empty, the author of the drawing is used. Next to Add, click Pin, Box or Arrow. On the page, click to place a pin, or drag to draw a box around something or an arrow pointing at it. Type the comment. Each comment shows its number in an orange bubble on the page. Reading and answering The panel lists the comments, with how many are open, each with its number, author, date and time, page, text and replies. Click a card to choose the comment and go to its page; with the panel open, you can also click a bubble or a box on the page. Edit the text of the chosen comment, or type in the Reply field and press Enter or click Reply. Resolve marks a comment as dealt with; Reopen opens it again. Resolved comments are hidden unless Show resolved is ticked. Hide marks hides the bubbles, boxes and arrows on the page. Delete removes a comment and its replies. Every change is one undo step. Deleting a page deletes its comments.

h: Creating a table Typing in cells Changing rows and columns Converting text and tables
x: Tables A table is an object made of rows and columns of cells, each of which can hold text and a fill. Draw tables with the Table tool and change them with the Table menu. Creating a table Choose Table > Create New Table (or Object > Create > New Table). In the Create New Table dialog box, set the Number of Rows, the Number of Columns and the height and width (100 by 75 mm at first), and click OK. The table is placed in the middle of the page and selected. Or choose the Table tool and drag a rectangle: the table fills it, with equal rows and columns.  On the property bar of the Table tool, set the number of rows (3 at first) and columns (4 at first), the cell fill (none at first), and the border width and color. With a table selected, the fill and border change that table; otherwise they apply to the next table you draw. Typing in cells With the Table tool, click a cell and type. Text editing works as in any text: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U format the selected characters, or the whole cell. Enter adds a line, Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous cell, and the arrow keys step to the next cell at the edge of the text. A row grows when its text needs more height. Shift+click adds cells to the selection. Changing rows and columns The Table menu acts on the active cell and the selected cells: Insert: Row Above, Row Below, Column Left and Column Right. The new row or column takes the size of its neighbour. Select: Cell, Row, Column or Table. Delete: Row, Column or Table. A table keeps at least one row and one column. Distribute: Rows Evenly or Columns Evenly, keeping the size of the table. Merge Cells (Ctrl+M) makes the selected cells one cell, with their texts in order; Unmerge Cells splits it again, keeping the text and fill in the top left cell. Split into Rows and Split into Columns split the active row or column into two halves. Converting text and tables Convert Text to Table: each paragraph of the selected text becomes a row. The dialog box asks what separates the cells: commas, tabs, nothing (each paragraph is one cell, in one column) or characters of your own under User defined, and tells how many rows and columns the table will have. It starts with tabs when the text has any, else commas when it has any. The spaces around each cell's text are left out, so "Anna, Ben, Carl" with commas makes three cells. Convert Table to Text: the cells are joined by tabs and the rows by line breaks. The defaults of the tool are on the Table page of the tool options; see Tool options.

h: Making a barcode Step 1: the standard and the data Step 2: printer and sizes Step 3: the text QR codes
x: Barcodes and QR codes TraceDraw makes barcodes for products, labels and inventory, and QR codes that phones can read. Both are made of ordinary vector shapes, so they print sharp at any size. Making a barcode Choose Object > Insert > Barcode to open the Barcode Wizard. It has three steps; a Sample preview under each shows the barcode as it will be made. Use Next and Back to move between steps, and Finish on the last one.  Step 1: the standard and the data Choose one of the standards and type the data. Choosing a standard puts a sample in the field, and the wizard says what the standard accepts: Codabar: up to 30 digits and the signs - $ : / . +, between start and stop characters A to D. Code 39: capital letters, digits and - . space $ / + %. Code 128: any printable character. EAN-13, EAN-8 and UPC-A: 12, 7 or 11 digits, or one more with the check digit, optionally followed by a space and a 2- or 5-digit add-on. UPC-E: 6 digits, or the number system (0 or 1) and 6 digits. Interleaved 2 of 5: up to 40 digits. Data the standard cannot hold keeps you on this step with a message. Step 2: printer and sizes Printer: the resolution of the printer, 150 to 2400 dpi (300 at first). Bars are made a whole number of printer dots wide, so they print evenly. Units for the sizes below. Bar width reduction: printer dots taken off every bar to make up for ink spreading (1 at first). The barcode keeps its width. Magnification (scale): 100% is the standard size. Bar height (1 inch at first), with the resulting Symbol width: {w}. Wide to narrow: 2.0 to 3.0, for Codabar, Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5. Advanced adds Add the check character (Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5) and the Quiet zone, a white margin behind the bars in modules. Step 3: the text The Font, Size (12 points at first), Weight and Alignment of the readable text. Options, available where the standard uses them: Center sys/check, Place text above, Show add-on text, Add-on text at bottom, Show FACT data, Show asterisks, Show quiet zone marks and Show start/stop. Make this bar code human readable (show text): turn it off for bars without text. Finish places the barcode in the middle of the page as one group and selects it. QR codes Choose Object > Insert > QR Code. A QR code is placed in the middle of the page at once, and the Properties panel opens at its QR Code section: Choose the kind of content: URL, Email, Phone number, SMS, Contact (vCard), Text or Location. Fill in its fields, such as Address (URL), or First name, Last name, Phone number and Email address for a contact. A field applies when you leave it. Fields the kinds share are kept when you change the kind. Set the look: Pixel fill and Background fill (any fill), Pixel outline and Pixel size (2.5 mm at first). Click Validate to check that the code reads back. A green message says it does; a red one says why not, for example when the pixels are not dark enough against the background. The QR code stays editable: move, scale or turn it as any object and change its content later. To make it plain shapes, ungroup it. Content that cannot be encoded, or too much of it, changes nothing and shows in red.
色彩、填色和透明度 每個物件內部都可以有填色，邊緣可以有外框。這些頁面介紹如何從色盤和 色彩 面板選擇色彩，填色的種類（單色、漸層、圖樣、材質或網格），如何讓物件透明，以及如何用色彩樣式、特別色和色彩管理保持色彩一致。

h: 選擇色彩 取樣色彩 特別色油墨
x: 色彩面板 色彩 面板（Shift+F11）可調配色彩，並將其套用到選取範圍的填色或外框。外框色彩 工具（Shift+F12）也會開啟它。從 視窗 > 面板 開啟它。  選擇色彩 選取物件。面板會從第一個物件的填滿色彩開始。 在其中一個檢視中調配新色彩： 色彩檢視器：在方塊中按一下或拖曳以設定飽和度（由左至右）和亮度（由下至上），在其旁邊的色條中設定色相； 色彩滑桿：色彩模型 的每個組成分量各有一個滑桿：RGB、CMYK（預設）、HSB、HSL、Lab、灰階或 YIQ； 調色盤：調色盤的色樣。 頂端的三個按鈕可顯示或隱藏各個檢視；可以任意組合顯示。您也可以輸入 #rrggbb 值。 按一下面板底部的 填色 或 外框 以套用新色彩。鎖（鎖定填色和外框）把填色和外框綁在一起，任一按鈕都會把色彩同時套用到兩者。"..." 按鈕（更多動作）展開其他動作：無填色, 無外框, 交換色彩, 加入文件調色盤, 加入自訂特別色 和 加入色彩樣式調色盤。 舊色彩和新色彩會並排顯示。當新色彩無法以 CMYK 油墨精確印出時，面板會顯示警告。 取樣色彩 按一下 滴管，然後按一下繪圖上的任何位置以取得該處的色彩。接著按一下 使用取樣的 {c}，使其成為新色彩。另請參閱滴管。 特別色油墨 在按鈕下方，特別色油墨 會列出繪圖的特別色油墨；請參閱特別色。

h: 使用調色盤 文件調色盤 調色盤面板 編輯調色盤
x: 調色盤 沿著視窗底部排列的調色盤是為物件上色最快的方法。在它下方，文件調色盤會收集您的繪圖所使用的色彩。您可以開啟更多調色盤、建立自己的調色盤並加以編輯。 使用調色盤 按一下色彩 填滿選取範圍（沒有選取任何物件時，設定新物件的填色） 以右鍵按一下色彩 為選取範圍的外框上色 Ctrl+按一下色彩 將該色彩的十分之一混入選取範圍的填色 按住色彩 顯示該色彩較淺、較深、較暗淡和較鮮豔的色調供選擇 將色彩拖曳到物件上 填滿物件，或放在邊緣上時為其外框上色 按一下有叉號的色塊 移除填色（以右鍵按一下：移除外框） 兩端的箭頭可捲動調色盤，右端的按鈕則可一次顯示所有色彩。將指標停留在色彩上，即可查看其名稱和數值。左端的調色盤選單按鈕會開啟調色盤選單。 調色盤可以移到視窗的其他邊緣，或設為浮動：拖曳其虛線握把即可。 在每一側，它可以停駐在視窗邊緣，也可以緊鄰繪圖區，位於繪圖區與該側的面板或工具箱之間。拖曳時，藍色條帶會顯示它將停駐的位置；在其握把上按右鍵可從清單中選擇位置。 文件調色盤 您套用到物件的每個色彩都會加入文件調色盤，它會隨繪圖一起儲存。其滴管會加入指標下方的色彩，其選單包含自動更新（可停止自動加入色彩）、從選取範圍新增、從文件新增、刪除色彩和重設調色盤（只保留繪圖仍在使用的色彩）。您也可以將色彩或物件拖曳到它上面。若要顯示或隱藏它，請參閱自訂選項。 調色盤面板 調色盤 面板會列出您擁有的調色盤，以及每個調色盤中的色彩數量。使用 視窗 > 調色盤 > 調色盤管理員 開啟它。  勾選調色盤即可將其顯示在繪圖視窗下方。 編輯 會在調色盤編輯器中開啟它。 Lock 會鎖定您開啟或建立的調色盤，使調色盤編輯器無法變更它；Unlock 允許再次編輯。 開啟調色盤 會開啟調色盤檔案（.tdpal、.gpl、.ase 或 .aco）。 從文件建立調色盤 和 從選取範圍建立調色盤 會以繪圖或選取範圍中使用的色彩建立調色盤。 文件調色盤的色彩顯示在底部；按一下可填滿選取範圍，以右鍵按一下可為外框上色。 編輯調色盤 視窗 > 調色盤 > 調色盤編輯器 會開啟調色盤編輯器。  選擇要編輯的 調色盤，或按一下 新增 開始建立。 輸入其 名稱。 按一下色彩以選取它；新增色彩 會加入目前的色彩，移除色彩 會移除選取的色彩。 按一下 儲存調色盤 將其儲存為檔案。 按一下 關閉。 內建調色盤無法編輯；請建立新的調色盤，或編輯其複本。

h: 填滿物件的方式 均勻填色 漸層填色 編輯填色對話方塊 互動式填色工具 區域填色工具 網狀填色 圖樣和材質填色 一個物件上的多重填色
x: 填色 填色會為封閉物件的內部上色。TraceDraw 有六種填色：無、均勻（單一平面色彩）、漸層（彼此融合的色彩）、圖樣、材質 和 網格（在格網節點之間流動的色彩）。 填滿物件的方式 按一下調色盤中的色彩，為選取範圍套用均勻填色。 使用 屬性 面板（F11）的 填色 區段：以那一排圖片選擇填色種類，然後設定其選項。 使用 互動式填色 工具（G）直接在物件上設定漸層。 使用 區域填色 工具填滿由多個物件圍成的區域。 使用 網狀填色 工具（M）建立網狀填色。 沒有選取任何物件時，您選擇的填色會成為新物件的填色。 均勻填色 均勻填色是單一色彩，可使用任何色彩模型。從調色盤、色彩 面板（請參閱色彩面板）或 屬性 面板的填色區段中選擇。 漸層填色 漸層會融合兩種以上的色彩。其設定位於 屬性 面板的填色區段中： 類型：線性（沿著直線）、放射狀（從中心向外）、圓錐（繞著中心）、方形（以逐漸擴大的方形）或 Shaped（依循物件的外框，從邊緣向內）。 Gradients：可作為起點的現成漸層。 色標：色彩及其在漸層上的位置，數量為 2 到 64 個。選取一個色標可變更其色彩或位置；新增色標 和 移除色標 可新增和移除色標。匯入漸層 會從 .ggr 漸層檔案取得色彩。 線性、圓錐和方形漸層的角度、邊緣填補（兩端各有多少為實色），以及放射狀、圓錐和方形漸層的中心偏移。 Repeat：None、Sawtooth（色彩從頭再跑一次）或 Mirror（色彩來回往返），並可設定 Cycles。 Bilinear：色彩從第一個跑到最後一個再返回。 Invert colours：色彩以相反順序排列。 類型下方的色條會顯示將要繪製的完整色彩排列。 編輯填色對話方塊 F11 開啟所選物件填色的 Edit Fill 對話方塊。漸層會顯示預覽、Fill picker、類型、重複方式和色帶：按一下節點選取，拖曳移動，按兩下新增或刪除節點。色帶下方是節點的顏色、透明度、位置、Midpoint 和 Reverse。Transform 包含旋轉、中心和邊緣填補。確定 套用您所做的變更，並包括 Overprint fill。對話方塊開啟期間，所選物件會隨著你的修改即時顯示填色；取消 或 Esc 會還原原本的填色。  互動式填色工具 互動式填色 工具（G）可直接在物件上編輯填色。 選擇此工具並在物件上拖曳：您會得到一個從按下處到放開處的線性漸層。按住 Ctrl 可讓角度以 15 度為增量。按一下則會套用預設填色。 拖曳物件上的節點以變更漸層：線性漸層的兩個方形節點可轉動其方向和長度；放射狀、圓錐或方形漸層的節點可移動其中心。 將調色盤色彩拖曳到節點上可重新上色，拖曳到節點之間的線上則可在該處新增色彩。 屬性列包含填色種類及其設定：均勻填色的色彩；漸層則有類型、起始和結束色彩、角度以及邊緣填補。 區域填色工具 區域填色 工具可填滿任何封閉區域，即使是由多個重疊物件形成的區域也可以，方法是以該區域建立一個新物件。周圍的物件保持不變。 選擇 區域填色 工具。 在屬性列上選擇填色和外框：指定（旁邊的色彩，外框則還有寬度）、使用預設值（新物件的填色和外框；若預設為無填色，則使用一種色彩，讓區域能夠顯示）或無。 在區域內按一下。 新物件會放在作用中圖層的最上層並被選取。在外框上按一下，或在沒有任何物件圍住的區域中按一下，都不會產生任何物件。 網狀填色 網狀填色是覆蓋在物件上的節點格網，每個節點都有自己的色彩和透明度；色彩會在節點之間平滑流動。它適合用於寫實的陰影。 選擇 網狀填色 工具（M），並在屬性列上設定列數和欄數（預設為 2 x 2，最多 50）。 按一下物件。物件會得到一個與其填色同色的網格。 按一下節點以選取它，然後按一下調色盤中的色彩為其上色。拖曳節點可彎曲色彩的流動。 在網格內按兩下，可在最近的節點處新增一列或一欄；選取節點並按 Delete 可移除其所在的列和欄。 屬性列還有平滑色彩（讓色彩融合得更柔和）、所選節點的透明度，以及清除網格（移除網狀填色）。變更網格的列數和欄數時會保留其色彩。 圖樣和材質填色 圖樣 填色會重複拼貼：雙色、向量圖樣或點陣圖。請參閱圖樣填色。 材質 填色是自動產生、外觀自然的材質：雲彩、大理石、雜訊 或 木紋，並可設定其色彩和比例。 一個物件上的多重填色 在 屬性 面板的填色區段中，新增填色 會在物件本身的填色上再繪製另一個填色，一開始是可供修改的複本。其他填色會顯示為「填色 2」、「填色 3」等，每個都有自己的編輯器和移除按鈕。外框區段也可以用同樣的方式新增更多外框。 填色也可以繪製在外框上；請參閱設定外框。

h: 從您的物件建立圖樣 圖樣設定 匯出檔案中的圖樣
x: 圖樣填色 圖樣填色會在物件內部重複拼貼。拼貼可以是雙色、一組向量物件（全彩向量圖樣）或點陣圖。拼貼固定在頁面上，因此移動物件時不會滑動。 從您的物件建立圖樣 繪製構成一個拼貼的物件並選取它們。 選擇 物件 > 建立 > 圖樣填色。 在 建立圖樣 對話方塊中，選擇 類型：向量 會將物件保留為向量，在任何大小下都保持銳利；點陣圖 則會將其製成圖片。 按一下 確定。  此圖樣會成為新物件的填色。若要套用到已繪製的物件，請在 屬性 面板的填色區段中選擇 圖樣。 圖樣設定 在 屬性 面板的填色區段中，選擇 圖樣，然後選擇圖樣種類及其設定。對於向量圖樣，面板會顯示拼貼包含的物件數量，以及其寬度和高度：變更這些值時，拼貼的內容也會隨之縮放。 匯出檔案中的圖樣 SVG 檔案會將向量圖樣保留為向量。PDF 和 EPS 檔案則會以匯出解析度將其轉為圖片，並裁剪至物件範圍。

t: 使用滴管複製色彩和屬性
h: 色彩滴管 屬性滴管
x: 使用滴管複製色彩和屬性 滴管工具會從一個物件取得色彩或一整組屬性，並將其套用到其他物件。兩者都分為兩個步驟，顯示在屬性列上：選取（取樣）和套用（以樣本上色）。取樣之後，工具會切換為套用；按一下選取按鈕即可再次取樣。Esc 會捨棄樣本並回到 選取 工具。 取樣時指標為滴管，套用時為油漆桶。影像即使在群組或框架內也能取色。 色彩滴管 選擇 色彩滴管 工具。 按一下物件以取得其色彩：均勻填色的填滿色彩、漸層的第一個色彩，或外框色彩。在點陣圖上，它會取得指標下方像素的色彩，並依屬性列上設定的樣本大小（1 x 1、2 x 2 或 5 x 5 像素）取平均值。Shift+按一下會優先取得外框色彩。 按一下物件即可以該色彩填滿它們；Shift+按一下可為其外框上色（沒有外框的物件會得到一條細外框）。在空的封閉形狀內按一下會將其填滿。 屬性列會顯示取樣的色彩。 移動指標吸取色彩時，指標旁的小框會顯示其下方的色彩：色樣、調色盤色彩或特別色的名稱、在繪圖色彩模式（CMYK 或 RGB）下的數值以及十六進位值。色彩選擇器的滴管也會顯示同樣的小框。 屬性滴管 屬性滴管 工具可一次將多項屬性從一個物件複製到其他物件。 選擇 屬性滴管 工具。 在屬性列上選擇要複製的內容： 屬性：外框、填色和文字（字型、大小和樣式；文字內容本身保留）。預設全部開啟。 變形：大小、旋轉和位置。預設關閉。 效果：透明度、下拉式陰影和即時效果。預設關閉。 按一下要複製來源的物件。 按一下每個要複製到的物件。Shift+按一下則會改為取樣另一個物件。 每次按一下都是一個復原步驟。

h: 建立色彩樣式 使用和編輯樣式 色彩和諧
x: 色彩樣式 色彩樣式是繪圖中的物件所使用的具名色彩。變更樣式時，所有以該樣式填色的物件也會隨之變更，這能讓設計的色彩保持一致，也能快速嘗試其他配色方案。樣式會列在 色彩樣式 面板中；從 視窗 > 面板 開啟它。  建立色彩樣式 從選取範圍建立新項目 會為選取物件中每一個尚未成為樣式的填滿色彩新增一個樣式。 新增色彩樣式 會以 色彩 面板的目前色彩新增一個樣式。 使用和編輯樣式 每個樣式都會顯示其色彩、名稱和三個按鈕： 按一下色彩可變更它：以該色彩填色的物件會隨之變更； 按一下名稱可重新命名； 填色 會以該樣式填滿選取範圍，外框 會為其外框上色； x 會移除樣式（物件保留其色彩）。 色彩和諧 和諧編輯器 會從 基底色彩 建立一組搭配協調的樣式： 選擇 基底色彩。 按一下一種和諧配色：類比色、互補色、分割互補色、三角色、四角色 或 單色。 和諧配色的色彩會以樣式的形式加入，並以該和諧配色命名。

h: 套用透明度 設定
x: 透明度 透明度讓物件下方的內容能透過物件顯示出來。它可以處處相同，也可以像漸層一樣在物件上變化，或依循圖樣或材質。 套用透明度 使用 透明度 工具：按一下物件，然後在屬性列上選擇透明度種類，或在物件上拖曳以建立從不透明（按下處）到透明（放開處）的漸層透明度。之後漸層的節點會像 互動式填色 工具那樣顯示在物件上：拖曳起點、終點或圓形傾斜節點；拖曳兩個節點之間的橫條（中點）可改變過渡到一半的位置；按兩下線條新增節點，按兩下節點將其移除。 在 屬性 面板的 透明度 區段中設定。 設定 種類：無透明度、均勻（預設）、漸層（線性、放射狀、圓錐、方形或造形，與漸層填色相同）、圖樣 或 材質。 程度：0 到 100%（預設為 50%）。對於漸層，色標是灰色色階：白色為不透明，黑色為完全透明。 合併模式：色彩與下方內容的混合方式。一般（預設）只是單純透出；其他模式，例如相加、相減、差異化、色彩增值、相除、若較亮、若較暗、色相、飽和度、色彩和反轉，則以其他方式組合色彩。 套用至 填色、外框 或 全部。 凍結：保留目前透出的內容，即使下方的物件移動也不改變。 要移除透明度，請按一下屬性列末端的 Clear Transparency（或將類型選為 無透明度）。 若要複製另一個物件的透明度，請使用 物件 > 複製效果 > 透明度來源。關於由物件亮度定義的透明區域，請參閱不透明度遮罩。

h: 新增特別色油墨 使用特別色油墨 色票簿 印刷和匯出中的特別色
x: 特別色 特別色是以自己的印版印刷的具名油墨，例如金屬色或品牌色，而不是由青色、洋紅色、黃色和黑色混合而成。每個繪圖都會保留一份其特別色油墨的清單。每種油墨都有一個由印刷色組成的替代色，用於在螢幕上顯示它，以及在無法使用該油墨的地方使用。 新增特別色油墨 開啟 色彩 面板，調配出油墨應有的色彩。 在 特別色油墨 下方輸入 油墨名稱。 按一下 新增特別色油墨。 名稱在同一個繪圖中不可重複。 使用特別色油墨 特別色油墨 清單會顯示每種油墨的色樣、名稱，以及 填色 和 外框 按鈕，這兩個按鈕會以您設定的 色調（0 到 100%，預設為 100%）將油墨套用到選取範圍。每一列末端的叉號會將油墨從清單中移除；使用它的物件會保留其替代色。 色票簿 調色盤檔案可以是特別色油墨的色票簿（例如含有特別色項目的 .ase 調色盤）。其中的特別色項目會以特別色開啟，名稱與色票簿中相同；套用其中一個會將該油墨加入繪圖。TraceDraw 不隨附需授權的色票簿，但您擁有的色票簿可以像任何調色盤一樣開啟。 印刷和匯出中的特別色 在 PDF 檔案中，每種油墨都會成為以其名稱命名的分色色彩，讓印刷廠取得該油墨。 列印分色時，每種油墨會在青色、洋紅色、黃色和黑色印版之後各有自己的印版。請參閱列印。 在螢幕上以及在點陣圖、SVG 和 .cdr 檔案中，特別色會以其替代色依其色調顯示。

h: 繪圖的描述檔 新繪圖的預設值 預覽印刷色彩
x: 色彩管理 螢幕以紅、綠、藍光顯示色彩；印表機則混合青色、洋紅色、黃色和黑色油墨。色彩管理使用色彩描述檔來描述每個裝置，讓色彩從螢幕到印刷頁面都保持相同的外觀。這些設定位於 工具 > 色彩管理，也就是 色彩管理設定 對話方塊。在您按一下 確定 之前不會有任何變更。  繪圖的描述檔 文件 分頁設定作用中繪圖的描述檔。 目前的描述檔 顯示繪圖目前使用的 RGB、CMYK 和灰階描述檔。 選擇套用新描述檔的方式： 指定新的 (保留色彩值)：色彩值保持不變，其外觀則依新描述檔改變； 轉換 (保留色彩外觀)：轉換 CMYK 色彩，使其在新描述檔中看起來相同。 選擇 RGB 描述檔、CMYK 描述檔 和 灰階 描述檔。每個清單都先列出預設描述檔，然後是您電腦上找到的所有描述檔。載入色彩描述檔 會加入描述檔檔案（.icc、.icm）。 主要色彩模式：CMYK 或 RGB。 演算方式：無法顯示的色彩如何納入可顯示範圍：相對色度（預設）、感應式、飽和度 或 絕對色度。 CMYK 描述檔會隨繪圖保存，也會寫入版本 16 以上的 .cdr 檔案。 新繪圖的預設值 預設 分頁設定新繪圖所使用的設定，以及色彩的轉換方式。 預設集：適用於北美、歐洲、日本或網頁與螢幕工作的現成設定。儲存預設集 會以 預設集名稱 儲存您自己的設定；刪除預設集 會移除一個預設集。 預設的 RGB 描述檔、CMYK 描述檔 和 灰階描述檔、主要色彩模式 以及 演算方式。 色彩轉換： 色彩引擎：TraceDraw ICC 引擎（使用描述檔）或 內建公式； 保留純黑：只使用黑色油墨的色彩在轉換後仍只使用黑色油墨； 將灰色對應為 CMYK 黑（預設開啟）：轉換為 CMYK 的灰色只使用黑色油墨； 黑點補償（預設開啟）：讓最暗的色調保持區別。 開啟原則：您開啟的檔案其描述檔會如何處理，分別針對 RGB、CMYK 和灰階：使用內嵌的色彩描述檔、指定預設色彩描述檔 或 轉換為預設色彩描述檔。當檔案使用其他描述檔或沒有描述檔時，色彩描述檔不符時警告 和 缺少色彩描述檔時警告 會在狀態列中顯示訊息。 匯入與貼上原則：對於您匯入或貼上的內容，選擇 轉換為文件色彩描述檔 或 指定文件色彩描述檔。 特別色定義：特別色是以 Lab 值、CMYK 值 還是 RGB 值 定義。 預覽印刷色彩 檢視 > 校樣色彩，或狀態列右端的校樣按鈕，會以印刷時的樣子顯示繪圖：CMYK 油墨無法印出的色彩看起來會比較暗淡。色彩 面板也會針對這類色彩發出警告。 沒有載入描述檔時，TraceDraw 會以其本身對塗佈紙上印刷油墨的模型來轉換色彩。

t: Converting colors to CMYK or RGB
h: Converting the colors What is converted How the colors are worked out
x: Converting colors to CMYK or RGB A drawing often mixes colors defined in RGB (for screens) with colors defined in CMYK (for printing inks). Before you send a drawing to print, or reuse a print job on the web, Tools > Convert Colors turns every color of the selected objects, or of the whole drawing, into one model in a single step. Converting the colors To convert only some objects, select them first. Choose Tools > Convert Colors. Under Convert to, choose CMYK (the default) or RGB. Under Colors of, choose The selected objects (the default when something is selected) or The whole drawing, which also takes in the pages' backgrounds and the symbols. Tick Convert spot colors too to turn spot colors into their CMYK or RGB mix as well (off at first). Click OK. The status bar says how many colors changed. All the changes undo in one step. When every color is already in the model you chose, or nothing is selected, nothing changes. What is converted Solid fills, the stops of gradients, the colors of mesh fills, patterns and textures. Outlines, text and table cells. The colors of effects (contours, blends, extrusions, bevels, block shadows and the others) and of drop shadows. Objects inside groups and clip frames, at any depth. Bitmaps take the color mode: converted to CMYK, a picture's pixels change to show the colors the inks can print; converted to RGB, only the mode changes and the pixels stay. See Bitmap color modes. The registration color never changes, so marks still print on every plate. Spot colors stay spot colors unless you tick Convert spot colors too. A color that is already in the model stays as it is. How the colors are worked out The conversion goes through the color management profiles: the drawing's own CMYK profile when it carries one, else the RGB and CMYK profiles, the rendering intent and the black point setting of Tools > Color Management. See Color management. Tip: A color converted to CMYK and back to RGB is not the color you started with when it was too bright for the inks. Keep a copy of the drawing before converting a whole drawing.
特殊效果 效果改變物件的外觀而不改變物件本身：漸變填滿兩個物件之間的空間，輪廓圖在物件周圍畫出環，封套使它彎曲，立體化使它看起來有體積，陰影使它從頁面上浮起。大多數效果是 動態的：物件保持自己的形狀，效果由它產生，因此你可以隨時變更或移除效果。 效果位於 效果 功能表、工具箱的效果飛出式選單以及各自的面板中。 點陣圖效果 改變圖片的像素，或改變當作圖片繪製的物件的像素。

h: Managing effects Other effect commands
x: The Effects panel An object can carry several live effects at once, applied one after the other. The Effects panel lists the effects of the selected object in the order they apply, from the top down. Open it with Window > Panels > Effects.  Managing effects Each row of the list has: a check box that turns the effect on or off. An effect turned off keeps its place and settings, but is not drawn, exported or printed; the effect's name, dimmed while it is off; up and down arrows that move the effect earlier or later, which changes the result (for example a contour of an envelope, or an envelope of a contour); a cross that removes the effect. Every change is one undo step. Each effect is still edited with its own tool or panel. Other effect commands Effects > Flatten Effects turns the effects of the selected objects into plain objects. Effect Picker shows a list of effects to apply to the selection. Object > Clear Effect removes the effect of the selection. Object > Copy Effect copies an effect from another object, and Clone Effect makes a clone that follows it; see Copying and cloning effects.

h: To blend two objects Blend settings Controls on the canvas Blending along a path Removing or splitting a blend Saving as .cdr
x: Blends A blend draws a series of intermediate steps between two objects, changing shape, size and color from one to the other. Use it for smooth shading, repeated patterns or a shape that turns into another. To blend two objects With the tool: Choose the Blend tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from the start object to the end object. With the panel: Select two objects. Open the Blend panel with Effects > Blend (Ctrl+F8). Set the options and click Apply.  Both objects stay objects of the drawing: move, resize or recolor either one and the steps follow. Deleting the end object removes the blend. Blend settings With a blend selected, every change on the property bar or in the panel applies at once. Blend steps: the number of steps (5 at first, up to 999). Spacing, for a blend on a path: the distance between steps; the number of steps follows from the length of the path. Rotation: turns the steps progressively; Loop turns them about the middle between the two objects instead. Acceleration: the object slider makes the steps crowd towards one end; the color slider does the same for the colors. Apply to sizing makes the object acceleration change the sizes too, and Link acceleration keeps the two sliders together. Reset puts both back to even. Color Blend: Direct (straight from one color to the other), Clockwise or Counterclockwise (around the color wheel). The tool's property bar has the steps, rotation and the two accelerations. Controls on the canvas Pick a blend with the Blend tool (click its start or end object, or a step) to show its controls: a square on the start object, a crossed square on the end object, the line between them and two sliders on it, the object acceleration above and the color acceleration below. Drag a slider toward the start or the end to crowd the steps or the colors there. The blend follows live, each drag is one undo step, and the property bar follows. A slider goes as far one way as the other: at 100 % the middle step sits right by the start object, at -100 % right by the end object. Drag an end square to move its object, so the blend changes direction. Drop it on another object to make that object the new start or end, with the blend's settings. The object acceleration moves the steps toward one end also when the blend follows no path. A bitmap effect on the start object keeps the blend drawn. Blending along a path Select the blend. Click New path in the Blend panel and click a curve. The steps follow the curve. Rotate all objects turns each step along the curve, and Blend along full path places the first and last steps at the ends of the curve. Removing or splitting a blend Clear blend removes the steps and leaves both objects. Break apart turns the steps into objects of their own, grouped. Object > Break Blend Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same. Saving as .cdr A blend saved as .cdr (version 9 or later) stays a blend: the file holds the two objects and the blend record between them, so the program that opens the file shows the steps and lets you change the blend. The steps, spacing and the two objects go into the file; acceleration, rotation, a path and the colour direction come back in TraceDraw (version 14 or later), other programs start from their defaults.

h: To add a contour Contour settings
x: Contours A contour draws evenly spaced copies of an object's outline inside it, outside it, or to its center, like the lines of a map. It is a live effect: change the object and the contour follows. To add a contour With the tool: Choose the Contour tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object: away from its middle for an outside contour, towards it for an inside one. The further you drag, the larger the spacing. With the panel: Select an object. Open the Contour panel with Effects > Contour (Ctrl+F9). Set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot take a contour. Contour settings The property bar and the panel show the settings of the selected contour and change it at once. To center, Inside or Outside (at first). Steps: 3 at first, up to 999. To center makes as many as fit. Offset: the distance between steps (2 mm at first). Corners: mitered (sharp, at first), round or beveled. Color direction: direct, clockwise or counterclockwise around the color wheel, from the object's colors to the last step's. The fill and outline colors of the last step (white and black at first). An object without a fill gives unfilled steps. Object acceleration and color acceleration (-100 to 100%) crowd the steps or the colors towards the object or towards the last step. Outside steps are drawn behind the object, inside steps in front of it. Clear contour removes the contour; Break apart turns the steps into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Contour Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To distort an object Distortion settings
x: Distortion The Distort tool bends an object's outline in three ways: push and pull (spikes or petals), zipper (zigzag teeth) and twister (a swirl). It is a live effect: you can change, move or remove the distortion at any time, and the object keeps its own outline. To distort an object Choose the Distort tool from the Effects flyout. Choose the kind on the property bar. Drag on the object. The distortion is centered where you start. Push and pull: drag right to push the nodes out (spiky shapes with hollow sides), left to pull them in (rounded petals). A straight side bends from its middle, so a square pulled in gets four round lobes. Zipper: the further you drag, the taller the teeth. Twister: drag around the starting point; full turns count. The handle follows the pointer as far out or as near as you drag it and stays that long; its length does not change the twist. The center of a selected distortion shows as a diamond: drag it to move the center. Dragging again replaces the distortion; an object has at most one. Groups and bitmaps are not distorted. Distortion settings The property bar shows and changes the selected distortion: the kind: Push and pull, Zipper or Twister (choosing another kind changes a selected distortion); for push and pull, the amplitude (-200 to 200, 20 at first); for zipper, the amplitude (0 to 100 mm, 2 mm at first) and the frequency (teeth per segment, 6 at first), with Random (uneven teeth), Smooth (rounded teeth) and Local (teeth shrink away from the center); for twister, clockwise or counterclockwise, the number of whole rotations and the extra degrees. A value changed on the property bar shows on the selected object at once, also when it has no distortion yet. The zipper draws one more line than its frequency, and its amplitude, frequency and angle have handles on the page to drag. The twister spirals smoothly to the ends of a shape. Object > Clear Effect removes the distortion.

h: To add an envelope Editing the frame Envelope settings
x: Envelopes An envelope is a frame of nodes around an object; the object is bent to fill the frame, and follows when you move its nodes. Use it to arch text, bulge a shape or fit artwork into a flag or a circle. The object keeps its own shape, so the envelope can be changed or removed at any time. To add an envelope With the tool: Choose the Envelope tool from the Effects flyout. Click an object. It gets a frame of eight nodes: the corners and the middle of each side. Drag the nodes to reshape the frame. With the panel (Effects > Envelope, Ctrl+F7): Select an object. Click Add new, or click one of the 24 preset shapes (arch, circle, flag, heart, cloud, speech bubble and more) to use it as the envelope.  Editing the frame The editing mode, chosen on the property bar or in the panel, decides what happens to the sides when you drag a node: Straight line: the sides stay straight; Single arc: the sides become one smooth arc; Double arc: the sides become S curves; Unconstrained (at first): the node carries its handles; click a node to see its two handles and drag them to bend each side on its own. Double-click the frame to add a node, a node (other than a corner) to delete it. In the unconstrained mode the property bar also has Add node and Delete node. The Shape tool edits the frame the same way. Envelope settings Presets on the property bar: arch, bulge, squeeze, flag, perspective and circle. Mapping, how the object fills the frame: Putty (at first), Original (spread evenly along the frame), Horizontal or Vertical (only across or only up). Keep lines: straight segments of the object stay straight. Add new envelope puts a fresh frame around the object as it now looks, over the envelope it has. Copy envelope properties: click another object to copy its envelope (as Object > Copy Effect > Envelope From). Click an object without an envelope, such as a circle, a star or a curve you drew, to fit the selected text or objects into its shape. Clear envelope removes the last envelope.

h: Place the photo and the design Follow the chest with an envelope Let the cloth show through: Multiply Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame Tips
x: Making a T-shirt mockup A mockup shows a design on a photo of the real thing, here a T-shirt, so you can judge it before it is printed. Four tools from the rest of this Help do the work: an envelope bends the design over the chest, a transparency merge mode lets the cloth's folds and shading show through the print, and a clip frame keeps the print on the shirt.  Place the photo and the design Choose File > Import and import a photo of a plain shirt, front view, in good light. Draw or import your design, place it over the chest and size it there. If the design is made of several objects, select them all and choose Object > Group, so the next steps treat it as one. Follow the chest with an envelope Cloth is not flat. A slight curve makes the print look as if it lies on the shirt. Select the design and choose the Envelope tool (or open Effects > Envelope). Use Single arc and drag the middle nodes a little: the bottom one down, the top one up and the side ones out. Keep it subtle. Each object of a group is bent from the box of the whole group and keeps its own colours. See Envelopes.  Let the cloth show through: Multiply A print takes on the shading of the cloth under it. The Multiply merge mode does the same: each color is multiplied by what is beneath, so the folds and shadows of the photo darken the design where they darken the shirt. Select the design and choose the Transparency tool, or open the transparency settings in the Properties panel. Choose Uniform and set the amount low (0 to 10 %). Set Merge mode to Multiply. See Transparency.  Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame A large print, or one placed near a sleeve, can reach past the shirt's edges.  Draw the outline of the shirt over the photo with the Bezier or Pen tool, following its edges (it does not need to be exact where the print does not reach). Give it no fill and no outline. Select the design, choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame and click the outline. The print is cut to the shirt and keeps its Multiply merge mode: it still mixes with the photo beneath the frame. See Placing objects inside a frame.  Tips A white or light shirt shows Multiply best. On a dark shirt, try If Lighter for a light print, or keep Normal with a little transparency. To try another design, use Edit Contents, or Extract Contents, replace the design and place the new one inside again. Group the photo, the frame and the design to move the whole mockup.

h: To extrude an object Extrusion settings
x: Extrusions An extrusion turns a flat object into a solid-looking body, with sides that run from its outline to a copy of it, lit and shaded. It is a live effect: change the object and the body follows. To extrude an object With the tool: Choose the Extrude tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object. For a parallel extrusion the body runs along the drag; for the others the end of the drag is the vanishing point. Drag the handle (a square with a cross) to move the vanishing point. With the panel (Effects > Extrude, Ctrl+F10): select an object, set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot be extruded. Extrusion settings The panel has five pages, chosen with the buttons at its top; the property bar has the main settings and a 3D menu with the rest. Camera: the type of extrusion: small back (at first), big back, small front, big front, back parallel or front parallel. Back types grow behind the object, front types in front of it. The depth (1 to 99, 20 at first), the vanishing point (X and Y, counted from the page origin or the object's center), and whether it is locked to the object (moves with it) or to the page. For parallel types, X and Y are the offset. Rotation: turns the body in space about X, Y and Z (-360 to 360 degrees); Reset puts it back. Lighting: the angle (135 degrees at first), intensity (50 at first) and elevation of the light, and two more lights you can turn on. Color: Object fill (the object's color, at first), Solid (one color) or Shade (a gradient from one color to another on each side). Bevel: a beveled edge on the front face, with its width. Clear extrude removes the extrusion; Break apart turns the faces into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Extrude Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To add a block shadow Settings
x: Block shadows A block shadow is a solid shadow that runs straight out from an object, as if the object were a thick block. It is drawn below the object as one filled shape, which suits signs and cut vinyl. To add a block shadow Choose the Block Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object in the direction the shadow should go. Settings On the property bar: Depth: how far the shadow reaches. Direction: its angle, 0 being to the right, counterclockwise. Color: 60% black at first. Gap: a clear band between the object and the shadow (0 at first). Clear block shadow removes the effect. With a shadowed object selected, the fields change its shadow; otherwise they set the next one.

h: To add a drop shadow Settings
x: Drop shadows A drop shadow is a soft shadow beneath an object, as if it floated above the page. It is a copy of the object's silhouette in the shadow color, offset and blurred. To add a drop shadow Choose the Drop Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object to where the shadow should fall. Clip frames and groups take shadows too: a frame casts the shadow of what it shows (its fill and the contents within it), and a group the shadow of each of its objects. A click on a shadow with the Pick tool selects its object; with the Drop Shadow tool it shows the shadow's handles, and a drag on the shadow moves it. Shadows show in exported and printed PDF files, with their color, opacity and feathering. Settings On the property bar: the offset of the shadow (2 mm right and 2 mm down at first); its opacity (50% at first); its feathering, how soft its edge is (15% at first); its color (black at first). A change there applies at once to the selected objects, also to an object that has no shadow yet: choose Flat, or an edge, to give it that kind of shadow directly. Shadow handles can be grabbed from a little outside the squares. Object > Clear Effect removes the shadow. To copy the shadow of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Drop Shadow From.

h: To bevel an object
x: Bevels A bevel makes the edges of an object look raised or carved, by lighting one side of the edge and shading the other. It is a live effect, set in the Bevel panel; open it with Effects > Bevel.  To bevel an object Select a filled object. In the Bevel panel, choose the style: Soft edge: the edge slopes into the object, lit on one side and shaded on the other; Emboss: the object seems pressed out of the page; the bevel is drawn around the outline instead of inside it. Set the look of the bevel: Depth: how far the bevel reaches from the edge, into the object for a soft edge and out of it for an emboss; Level: how many steps the light and the shade are cut into across the bevel. 1 gives two flat tones, more fade them smoothly from the edge inwards; Light angle: the direction the light comes from; Intensity: how strong the light and the shade are; Light color and Shadow color: the colours of the lit and the shaded side; Emboss color: the colour the bevel is toned from. Tick the box and pick a colour to use your own; left off, the object's own fill is used. Click Apply. When you select an object that already has a bevel, the panel shows that bevel, and changing a setting edits it right away. To copy a bevel from another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Bevel From. Object > Clear Effect removes it. The extrusion panel also has a bevel for the front face; see Extrusions.

h: To make a lens Kinds of lens Options
x: Lenses A lens changes how the objects beneath it look, without changing them: it can brighten, tint, magnify, invert or apply bitmap effects to everything it covers. Move the lens and the view through it changes. Lenses are set in the Lens panel (Effects > Lens, Alt+F3).  To make a lens Draw a closed object over the objects to change, and select it. In the Lens panel, choose the kind of lens and its settings. Click Apply. Kinds of lens Brighten brightens (or darkens) what lies beneath rate, -100 to 100 (50) Color add adds a color, as light color and rate Color limit lets only a color through color and rate Custom color map maps dark to light onto a range of colors from and to colors, direction Fish eye bulges what lies beneath rate, -1000 to 1000 (100) Heat map shows brightness as warm and cold colors palette rotation Invert inverts the colors  Magnify enlarges what lies beneath amount, 1 to 100 (2) Tinted grayscale shows it in shades of one color color Transparency makes the lens see-through, tinted rate and color Wireframe shows the objects as outlines outline and fill colors Bitmap effects runs bitmap effects over what lies beneath Add effect, in order Options Frozen: keeps what the lens shows now, even when the objects beneath change. Viewpoint: shows another place through the lens. Remove face: shows the lens only over other objects, not over the empty page. To add a bitmap effect as a lens from the effect picker, choose Effects > Effect Picker and apply it as a lens.

h: Adding perspective to an object Drawing in perspective
x: Perspective Perspective makes an object look as if it lay on a plane that recedes into the distance. You can add perspective to an object you have drawn, or draw straight onto a perspective grid. Adding perspective to an object Select an object. Choose Object > Add Perspective. Drag the four corner nodes with the Shape tool to tilt it. To copy the perspective of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Perspective From. Drawing in perspective View > Draw in Perspective shows a perspective grid over the page. While it is on, every object a drawing tool makes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons, curves, brush strokes, text frames) is laid onto the active plane of the grid. Objects you paste, duplicate or move with the Pick tool stay as they are. The bar at the top left of the drawing window has: Finish: leaves the mode; the objects keep their perspective; 1-Point, 2-Point and 3-Point: the kind of grid; the planes: Ground, Left, Right (and Top for a 1-point grid). The active plane is drawn strongly; Grid: shows the grid lines; Depth (5 to 98%): how far the grid reaches towards the vanishing points; Put on plane: lays the selected objects onto the active plane. Drag the vanishing points (circles) and the near corners (squares) to change the grid. An object laid on a plane gets an ordinary perspective effect, whose four corners you can still edit with the Shape tool.

h: Copying an effect Cloning an effect
x: Copying and cloning effects Instead of setting up an effect again, you can copy it from an object that already has it. Copying an effect Select the objects that should get the effect. Choose Object > Copy Effect and the kind of effect: Drop Shadow From, Transparency From, Envelope From, Perspective From, Distortion From, Extrude From, Contour From, Blend From, Lens From, Bevel From or Block Shadow From. Click the object to copy from. A right-click cancels. The effect is fitted to each object: an envelope or perspective is stretched to its size, a distortion keeps its center at the same place within it. When the object you click has no such effect, nothing changes and the status bar says so. The copy is one undo step. Cloning an effect Object > Clone Effect copies the shadow (Shadow From) or the transparency (Transparency From) of another object, and keeps following it: change the source and the clones change too, until you edit a clone's own effect. Edit > Clone makes a clone of a whole object, and Copy Properties From (Ctrl+Shift+A) copies the fill, outline or text properties of another object: tick what to copy (outline pen, outline color, fill, text properties), click OK, then click the object to copy from.

h: Vector Mosaic Picture Mosaic
x: Vector and picture mosaics A mosaic rebuilds the selected objects, or a picture, out of many small tiles. A vector mosaic uses colored shapes; a picture mosaic uses photos from a folder of your own. Vector Mosaic Open the Vector Mosaic panel with Effects > Vector Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to turn into a mosaic. Set the options: Density: tiles per inch (10 at first); Scale: the size of each tile within its cell (1 at first); Screen angle: how the rows are turned (30 degrees at first). Keep original: off deletes the selection once the mosaic is made. Limit colors: reduce the tiles to at most that many colors (16 at first). Method: Uniform (every tile full size, transparency flattened on white), Size modulation 1 (the tile size follows the opacity, at first) or Size modulation 2 (darker areas give bigger tiles). Merge adjacent: combine up to that many neighbouring tiles of one color; Weld adjacent overlap: one curve per color instead of one object per tile. Shape: circle (at first), square or custom. For a custom tile, select a closed curve and click Select. Click Apply. The mosaic is one group placed on top of the selection, and is selected. Picture Mosaic Open the Picture Mosaic panel with Effects > Picture Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to rebuild. Under Library, click Browse and choose a folder of pictures (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF; up to 1000). The panel shows how many it holds. Set the options: Keep original (on at first). Columns: tiles across (30 at first); the rows follow from the shape of the selection. Blending: how much of the selection shows over the tiles (20% at first). Allow duplicates (on), with the tile spacing: the fewest tiles between two uses of one picture. Composition: single, stack or array; Edges: stretch the last row or remove it; Output priority and the resolution: how large the mosaic is in pixels. The panel shows the resulting size. Click Apply. Note: Picture libraries need the desktop version; the browser version cannot read folders.

h: To apply a bitmap effect The effect groups Special dialogs Editing the effects of an object The Effect Picker Effects that spread past the edges
x: Bitmap effects Bitmap effects change pixels: blur, sharpen, adjust colors, add textures and artistic strokes. They work on bitmaps and also on vector objects, which are then drawn as the picture the effects make while keeping their own shape, fill and outline. Effects are kept apart from the original pixels: you can edit, hide, reorder or remove any of them later, and removing the last one gives the original back. To apply a bitmap effect Select one or more objects. Choose a group in the Effects menu and an effect. Effects without settings apply at once. The others open a dialog box you can size, with the first selected object before and after in the Before and After preview and the settings on the right. The effect also shows on the drawing and follows every value as it changes (untick Preview to switch that off); the work is done in the background, so the window keeps answering on large pictures. Click OK to keep what the drawing shows as one undo step; Cancel or Esc put the drawing back exactly as it was. The settings sit in a panel at the right; under it Reset puts every setting back to its default, and the two arrows undo and redo the changes made in the dialog box.  The change to the whole selection is one undo step. With a bitmap selected, Ctrl+B opens Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Ctrl+Shift+B Color Balance and Ctrl+Shift+U Hue/Saturation/Lightness. The effect groups 3D Effects Cylinder, Emboss, Page Curl, Pinch/Punch, Sphere Adjust Auto Adjust, Image Adjustments, Contrast Enhancement, Local Equalization, Target Color Balance, Tone Curve, Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Color Balance, Gamma, Hue/Saturation/Lightness, Selective Color, Replace Colors, Desaturate, Channel Mixer Art Strokes Charcoal, Conté Crayon, Crayon, Cubist, Impressionist, Palette Knife, Pastels, Pen & Ink, Pointillist, Scraperboard, Sketch Pad, Watercolor, Felt Marker, Paper Grain Blur Directional Smooth, Gaussian Blur, Smooth Jagged Edges, Low Pass, Motion Blur, Radial Blur, Smart Blur, Smooth, Soften, Zoom Camera Colorize, Diffuse, Photo Filter, Sepia Toning, Vintage Photo Color Transform Bit Planes, Halftone, Psychedelic, Solarize Contour Edge Detect, Find Edges, Trace Contour Correction Dust and Scratch Creative Crystallize, Fabric, Frame, Glass Tiles, Mosaic, Scatter, Tinted Glass, Stained Glass, Vignette, Vortex Custom Bump Map Distort Blocks, Displace, Mesh Warp, Offset, Pixelate, Ripple, Swirl, Tile, Wet Paint, Whirlpool, Wind Noise Add Noise, Maximum, Median, Minimum, Remove Moiré, Remove Noise Sharpen Adaptive Unsharp, Directional Sharpen, High Pass, Sharpen, Unsharp Mask Texture Cobblestone, Wrinkles, Etching, Plastic, Relief Sculpture, Stone Transform Deinterlace, Invert Colors, Posterize Special dialogs Image Adjustments opens a larger dialog box: a large preview you can zoom, pan and rotate, shown alone, side by side or split; Auto adjust and pickers for the white and black points; sliders for temperature, tint, saturation, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows and midtones, with a histogram; undo and redo inside the dialog; and snapshots of settings to compare. Contrast Enhancement shows the histogram with markers to drag for the input and output levels, eyedroppers for black and white, and Auto adjust. Tone Curve edits a curve per channel (master, red, green, blue) in four styles (curve, straight, freehand, gamma), over the histogram; curves can be saved and loaded. Colors of the picture, such as in Replace Colors, have an eyedropper: click a preview to take the color under the pointer. Editing the effects of an object The FX section of the Properties panel lists the effects of the selected object, first applied at the top. Each row has a check box to show or hide the effect, Edit (opens its dialog box), Move up, Move down and Delete. Add effect opens the effect groups. Effects > Flatten Effects makes the effects permanent: a bitmap keeps what it shows, and a vector object becomes a bitmap. The Effect Picker Effects > Effect Picker opens a window that stays open while you work, with every effect as a small picture. Type in the search field to find effects, or choose a group or Recent from the list. With something selected, click a tile to apply the effect. You can also apply an effect as a lens. Effects that spread past the edges Blurs and similar effects can reach past the edges of a bitmap. With Bitmaps > Inflate Bitmap > Auto Inflate Bitmap on (as at first), the bitmap grows to make room for them. See Resampling and straightening. To save a bitmap with its effects as a PNG file, right-click it and choose Save Bitmap As.

h: Adding text Editing text Formatting from the property bar The Text panel Paragraph text frames Moving and turning characters Text on a path Other text commands
x: Adding and editing text Adding text Choose the Text tool (F8). For artistic text, click where the text starts and type. Press Enter to start a new line. For paragraph text, drag a frame, then type. The text wraps at the edges of the frame. Press Esc to finish. An empty text is removed. New artistic text is 24 points, paragraph text 12 points, in the first sans-serif font found. Change the defaults by formatting with nothing selected. To make an existing object a text frame, right-click it and choose to create an empty text frame; see Empty frames. Text > Insert Placeholder Text fills the selected frames with sample text, as much as fits. Editing text Click text with the Text tool, or double-click it with the Pick tool, to edit it in place. Text > Edit Text (Ctrl+Shift+T) opens a box with the whole text to edit instead; OK puts it back in the drawing, and the characters you did not change keep their formatting. Typing, Ctrl+V insert at the caret, replacing the selection Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste the selected characters; the Edit menu, the toolbar and the right-click menu do the same while you edit. Pasted here, they keep their font, size and colors; other programs get their plain text Backspace, Delete delete the selection, else the character before or after Enter, Shift+Enter new paragraph, new line Arrow keys, with Ctrl move by a character or a word; Shift selects Home, End, with Ctrl start or end of the line, or of the text Ctrl+A select all Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U bold, italic, underline Ctrl+L, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+R align left, center, right Ctrl+J, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+N full justify, force justify, no alignment Shift+F3 change case (see Writing tools) Double-click select a word A new alignment keeps artistic text in place at the reference point of the X and Y fields of the property bar; in a frame it applies to the paragraphs at the caret. Text in right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) is laid out right to left, also when it is mixed with left-to-right words, and selections shade every selected letter. Keyboards and input methods that send characters (such as those for Tamil and other Indian scripts on Windows) type into text and fields, and Alt codes typed on the keypad give their character once. Letters typed with AltGr (Polish ą ę ł, German @ € { }) type into text and fields, also on Windows. On Android the on-screen keyboard types every script its input methods compose (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Tamil). Older fonts that set the letters of a script at the places of Latin ones (some Tamil fonts) type as their keyboards expect: Autocorrect does not change the letters typed in them. All your typing in one editing session is one undo step. Formatting from the property bar With the Text tool, or with text selected, the property bar has the font list, the size (type it or pick from the list), bold, italic, underline, the alignment (left, center, right, full justify), bullets and drop cap for paragraph text, Text (Ctrl+T) and Edit Text. The button beside the font size opens the sliders of a variable font's axes (see Variable fonts). While editing, they act on the selected characters; otherwise on the whole selected texts, and only the setting you change: a new font for several texts keeps each one's size, bold and italic. Your choice also becomes the default for the next text. The font list shows each family in its own font, with the ones you used last at the top. Type to narrow the list. A family with several styles has an arrow that shows them. See Fonts and glyphs. The Text panel The Text panel (Ctrl+T) has every text setting, in three sections you can open and close: Character, Paragraph and Frame. The three buttons at the top show the panel from that section on. Full justification spreads Chinese and Japanese lines to the edge of the frame by adding room between the characters, and paragraph text in those scripts breaks lines by their rules: punctuation such as ，。、 and closing brackets never start a line, and opening brackets never end one. Letters given another color keep the font's kerning with their neighbours.  Character: the font, style and size; range kerning (-50 to 200%) and underline; the fill, background and outline of the characters. More options under the section: character offsets and angle, strikethrough and OpenType features. Paragraph: the alignment (none, left, center, right, full justify, and forced justify, which spreads the last line too); line spacing in percent of the character height, points or percent of the font size; left, first-line and right indents; space before and after paragraphs; character and word spacing. The gear opens custom hyphens. Frame, for paragraph text: the background color of the frame, the vertical alignment (top, middle, bottom), fit text to frame, columns (1 to 8) and the gap between them, and links to the bullets, drop cap and columns dialog boxes, and hyphenation. Every change applies to the selected characters while editing, or to the selected texts, and is one undo step. With no text selected, the settings become those of new text. The button at the top right gives new text the settings of the selected text. Paragraph text frames Frames show as dashed lines. A frame turns red, with a small tab under its bottom edge, when its text does not fit; the text that does not fit is not drawn, printed or exported. To make it fit: drag the frame's handles to enlarge it. The text flows again; the letters keep their size; choose Text > Paragraph Text Frame > Fit Text to Frame to resize the text to fill the frame; link the frame to another one, so the text flows on: Link. Unlink breaks the link. Or click the small tab under the frame's bottom edge, then click another frame (on this page or another one) or click or drag on an empty spot for a new frame: the text flows on into it. You can also drag from the tab and let go over another frame or an empty spot. a picked frame also has a small tab over its top edge: click it, then click the frame
