h: Tabs Columns Bullets Drop caps Hyphenation
x: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps The Text menu has four dialog boxes for laying out paragraph text. Each acts on the selected paragraph text. Their settings are also in the Frame section of the Text panel. Tabs Text > Tabs sets where the Tab character jumps to. At first there is a tab stop every 12.7 mm (half an inch). Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Tabs. Under Tab stops, change the positions, or click Add tab to add one. Click Close.  Columns Text > Columns splits a text frame into columns; the text flows from one column into the next. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Columns. Set the number of Columns and the Gutter, the space between columns (5 mm at first). Click Close.  To break to the next column at a given place, insert Column/Frame Break from Insert Formatting Code. Bullets Text > Bullets puts a bullet before each paragraph. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Bullets. Tick Use bullets, and set the bullet Symbol and the Indent (5 mm at first). Click Close.  Drop caps A drop cap is a large first letter that spans several lines. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Drop Cap. Tick Use drop cap and set the Lines dropped (3 at first). Click Close. The letter is scaled so its top meets the top of the first line and it sits on the baseline of the last line it spans; the lines beside it are shortened to make room.  Hyphenation Text > Use Hyphenation lets the selected text's words break at the end of lines (while you type in a text, the paragraphs at the cursor; with no text selected, it is the setting for new text), with at least two letters before and three after the break. A comma or other punctuation next to a word does not stop it from breaking, and words with an apostrophe (such as Italian dell'anno) break too. Words with a capital letter are never broken. To decide yourself where a word may break, see Custom hyphens.

h: The Fonts panel Font lists and the filter Variable fonts Missing fonts The Font Sampler The Glyphs panel The Font Manager
x: Fonts and glyphs TraceDraw uses the fonts installed on your computer, fonts you add in the Font Manager, and fonts that come with a drawing. This page explains the panels and the dialog box for working with fonts and special characters. The Fonts panel The Fonts panel lists the font families.  Type in the filter field to narrow the list. Under Fonts in document are the families the drawing uses. A family that is not installed is marked missing; its text shows in a similar font and keeps its font name. A family that came with the drawing is marked embedded. Click a family to give it to the selected text, or to make it the font of new text. Font lists and the filter The font lists of the property bar, the Text panel, the Glyphs panel and the options work the same way: Type to jump to a family. The last five families you picked are at the top ("used last"), and every family's name is drawn in its own font. The mouse wheel over the closed list picks the next or previous family for the text being edited or selected. A font that came with the drawing and is not installed says "Embedded" at the end of its row and after its name in the font box: its text is drawn with the copy that came with the drawing. The Filter button at the top of the open list shows the filter's choices beside the list. Each click filters at once and leaves the list open; the button counts the choices made, such as "Filter (2)", and Clear filter at the top of the choices removes them. The choices, in sections that fold: Fonts shown: all fonts, installed fonts, the fonts in this drawing, or in the browser version the fonts to download. Style: serif, sans serif, script, decorative, monospaced, symbol. Weight: light, regular, bold. Width: condensed, normal, expanded. Technology: TrueType, OpenType, variable. Scripts: Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Bengali, Thai, Korean, Japanese, Chinese and symbols. OpenType features: ligatures, kerning, small capitals, the kinds of figures, fractions, superscripts and subscripts, ordinals, slashed zero, swashes, alternates and stylistic sets, each on its own. Embedding rights: installable, editable, preview and print, restricted, bitmap only. Folders: the folders the fonts are in, as the Font Manager lists them: each folder you added to the libraries and the system's font folders, not their subfolders. Within a section a family needs one of the ticked choices (every ticked one for the OpenType features), and it needs what every section asks. The values are read from the font files themselves; with thousands of fonts the list fills in over a moment the first time. Variable fonts A variable font holds a range of weights, widths and other designs in one file. To set them on text: Select the text, or the letters, in a variable font. Click the button beside the font size on the property bar (or in the first section of the Text panel). It is greyed out, with a tip saying why, when the font is not variable. The Character section of the Text panel shows the same sliders. Drag the slider of an axis: Weight, Width, Slant, Italic, Optical size, or the font's own axes by the names it gives them, each over the font's range. The text follows the slider while you drag, so you can judge it on the page. Letting go of the slider, or typing a value, keeps it as one undo step. Default axes takes the values off. The values are saved in .tdraw files and drawn in exports and PDF files; a weight set this way replaces the bold TraceDraw would otherwise draw. Missing fonts When a drawing uses fonts that are not installed, the Missing Fonts dialog box asks which installed font draws each one, for this session or for good. See Missing fonts. Install the fonts and the text shows in them again. Drawings saved as .tdraw, and .cdr files with embedded fonts, can carry their fonts along. The Font Sampler The Font Sampler panel (Text > Font Sampler) shows a line of sample text in several fonts, one under the other, to compare them.  Type the sample text at the top; left empty, a sentence in your interface language is used. Set the size (10 to 96, 28 at first). Add fonts by typing part of a name and clicking one of the matches (up to 24 fonts); the cross removes one. At first the panel lists the text font and the fonts of the drawing. Click a sample to give that font to the selected text. The Glyphs panel The Glyphs panel (Text > Glyphs, Ctrl+F11) shows every character of a font, to insert symbols and special characters.  Choose the font. Choose a character range: the entire font, Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, punctuation, numbers, currency, arrows, mathematical operators or symbols. Click a character. It is inserted at the caret of the text you are editing, or as a new text in the middle of the page. Hover a character to see its name and code. A small arrow under a character means the font has alternates for it (such as swashes or small capitals); click it to see them. The glyphs you used last are at the top of the panel. Type in the search field above the grid to find characters: type the characters themselves (such as é), or a Unicode code point such as U+20AC, 0x20ac or 20AC. The line above the grid shows the code point, the character and the range of the character under the pointer. The Font Manager Tools > Font Manager opens the Font Manager, a window that organizes your fonts.  Libraries (top left): My fonts (the installed fonts), the folders you added, Favorites and your collections. Double-click a collection to rename it; right-click for more. Filters (bottom left): by status (installed, not installed, protected system fonts, duplicates), embedding rights, technology (TrueType, OpenType, variable), weight, width, style, character range and OpenType features. h: Choosing the fonts that stand in Turning the dialog box off and on Other ways to deal with missing fonts
x: Missing fonts A drawing made on another computer can use fonts that are not installed on yours. TraceDraw always shows such text in an installed font that looks close, and keeps the text's own font name. When the drawing opens, the Missing Fonts dialog box lets you choose which installed font draws each missing one, for now or for good. Choosing the fonts that stand in When you open a drawing with missing fonts, the Missing Fonts dialog box lists them: Each row shows the Missing font and the font it is Drawn with now. The first choice in the list is the font TraceDraw picked by itself, marked "(automatic)": a font drawn to the same widths when there is one, else one of the same style. To use another font, open the list of the row and click an installed family. Type part of a name in Find a font to narrow the lists. Choose how long the choice holds: For this session only (the drawing keeps its fonts) (the default): the font you chose draws the text until TraceDraw closes, bold and italic text included. The drawing keeps its own font names, so it is saved with them and shows in its own fonts on a computer that has them. Replace in the drawing (saved with it): every text in the missing family, also in groups, clip frames, tables and symbols, takes the font you chose. This changes the drawing and undoes in one step. Click OK. Cancel, Esc or the close button change nothing: the automatic fonts stay. Either way, the status bar then names the fonts still missing and the fonts that draw them, or says they were replaced. When some objects of the file could not be read, their note follows the dialog box. Turning the dialog box off and on Tick Do not show this message again in the dialog box to stop it. The drawing then opens straight away and the status bar names the missing fonts. Click that note on the status bar to open the Warnings page of Tools > Options > Global, where Ask which installed font draws each missing one (the Missing Fonts dialog) turns the dialog box on again (it is on at first). When an opened drawing uses fonts that are not installed, on the same page, is a separate, plain message that only names the missing fonts after the drawing opens. Opening drawings from scripts, the command line or the AI connection never stops at this dialog box. Other ways to deal with missing fonts Install the fonts, or add their folder in the Font Manager (see Fonts and glyphs); the text then shows in them. In the Fonts panel, families the drawing uses that are not installed are marked missing. Drawings saved as .tdraw and .cdr files with Embed fonts carry their fonts along, and a package holds the font files in its Fonts folder. The preflight lists text in fonts that are not installed before you print or publish.

h: The Writing Tools dialog box Spell Checker Dictionaries Grammar Thesaurus Autocorrect Custom hyphens Change case Text statistics Encode Web-compatible text
x: Writing tools TraceDraw checks spelling and grammar, finds synonyms, corrects as you type, and fixes text that came in with the wrong characters. The commands are in Text > Writing Tools and the Text menu. The Writing Tools dialog box Text > Writing Tools > Spell Check, Grammar and Thesaurus open the Writing Tools dialog box at that tab. Check chooses whether to check every text of the page (Document) or only the selected texts (Selection).  Spell Checker Click Start. The first word not found shows, with suggestions under Replacements. Click a suggestion to put it in Replace with (double-click to replace at once), or type the right word. Click Replace for this place, Auto Replace for every place, Skip Once or Skip All to leave it, or Add to add the word to your own word list. Undo takes back the last replacement. Options has Ignore words with numbers, Ignore words in capitals and Add corrections to Autocorrect. Dictionaries TraceDraw checks spelling with Hunspell dictionaries: for each language a .dic file and an .aff file with the same name, such as pt_BR.dic and pt_BR.aff. Free dictionaries for most languages can be downloaded from the projects that make them; other programs often install them too. Open Tools > Options > Text > Spelling. Click Open Folder and copy the .dic and .aff files into that folder (folders inside it work too), or name a folder that already has dictionaries in Also read dictionaries from. Click Read Again. The Dictionaries list shows each one; clear a box to stop using it. A word is right when any dictionary in use knows it. Dictionaries installed on your system are used as well. Without any, only a built-in word list is used. Hyphenation dictionaries (hyph_ files such as hyph_pt_BR.dic) go in the same folders. Choose one under Text > Paragraph Text > Hyphenation patterns to hyphenate text in that language. Grammar The grammar checker finds doubled words, double spaces, spaces before punctuation, missing spaces after it, sentences that start in lower case, unbalanced brackets and quotes, repeated punctuation, sentences over 40 words, missing end marks and, in English, "a" and "an" before the wrong sound. For each finding it shows the replacement, the New sentence and the Rule Name. Click Start (then Replace), Skip Once or Skip Rule. Thesaurus Type a word (the first word of the selected text at first) and click Look Up. The meanings show with their synonyms: click one to pick it, double-click to look it up. Insert puts it in the text, keeping the capitals. Under Options, Close after inserting closes the dialog box after inserting, and Choose Thesaurus File uses a thesaurus file you have. Autocorrect Text > Writing Tools > Autocorrect opens the Autocorrect tab of Tools > Options > Text, which sets what is corrected while you type: Capitalize first letter of sentences; Correct two initial capitals ("THe" becomes "The"); Capitalize names of days ("monday" becomes "Monday"); Automatically create hyperlinks when typing web addresses: typing www.example.com or an address starting with http:// or https:// gives the text object that hyperlink, unless it has one; Language the language whose quotation marks are used (the interface language unless you pick another); Use typographic quotation marks, and Use straight quotation marks after numbers (e.g. 6'); Single quotes and Double quotes: the Open and Close marks, if you want others than the language's; the Replacement table, used when Replace text while typing is on: (c) becomes ©, (r) ®, (tm) ™, 1/2 ½ and so on. Type in Replace and With, then click Add; click a row to Delete it, or change its text and click Replace. Apply to Selection applies the rules to the selected text. Text you paste or import is never changed.  Custom hyphens Text > Custom Optional Hyphens (also the gear of the Paragraph section of the Text panel) defines where your own words may break, such as product names. Those words break only there when hyphenation is on. Choose the Language (Show all languages lists every one). Type the Word and the Hyphenated Word with hyphens where it may break, such as Trace-Draw. Click Add Definition. Remove Definition removes the selected definition. Under Automatically insert custom optional hyphens, When typing and When pasting and importing text turn hyphenation on for texts that hold a defined word. Click Apply to Selection to apply them to the selected text now, or OK to keep them.  Change case Text > Change Case (Shift+F3) changes the selected text to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case or tOGGLE cASE.  Text statistics Text > Text Statistics counts the text objects, lines, words, characters and fonts of the selected text, or of the page.  Encode Text that came from another program sometimes shows the wrong characters, such as "cafÃ©" instead of "café". Text > Encode fixes it: Select the text. Choose how the text Text was read as and what It really is (UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, Mac OS Roman or Windows-1251). Check the Preview and click OK.  Web-compatible text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies the selected text for web pages: gradient, pattern, texture and mesh fills become a flat color, and outlines, shadows and effects are removed.
範本和樣式 範本和樣式可以省去重複的工作。範本 是可以直接開始的現成繪圖。樣式 是命名的一組填色、外框和透明度，它與使用它的物件保持連結，因此一次變更就能更新所有物件。預設屬性 決定新物件的外觀。 對單一色彩以同樣方式運作的色彩樣式在 色彩樣式 中說明。

h: Starting from a template The built-in templates Saving your own templates
x: Templates A template is a drawing to start from: a blank page of a common size, or a designed business card, flyer, poster, letterhead or label to fill in. Opening a template makes a new, untitled drawing; the template itself never changes. Starting from a template Choose File > New from Template, or click New from Template on the Welcome Screen. Find a template: type in Search templates to match names and categories; choose where templates come from: All templates, Built in or My templates; choose a category, or All categories. Click a template to see it. With Show template details on, the pane on the right shows it large with its Category, Page size and Source. Click Open, double-click the template, or press Enter. The Size slider at the bottom makes the thumbnails larger or smaller, and Open template opens any .tdt or .tdraw file as a template.  The built-in templates Blank pages: A4 portrait and landscape, A3, Letter, business card (90 by 50 mm), A2 poster, web (1920 by 1080 pixels) and social media (1080 by 1080 pixels). Designed: two business cards, a sale flyer and an event flyer, a poster, a letterhead, a certificate, an invoice, a birthday banner, a quote post and a round label. They are made of ordinary shapes and text with sample text, so you can change every part. Saving your own templates Make the drawing you want to start from in the future. Choose File > Save as Template. Give it a name and save it. Templates you save appear under My templates. They are kept in the templates folder of your settings, so they are not available in the browser version.

h: Default properties Changing defaults with nothing selected Styles To make a style Using and changing styles
x: Object styles and default properties The Object Styles panel has two parts: the Default Properties of new objects, and the styles of the drawing. Both are saved with the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click an object and choose the object styles panel.  Default properties New objects take the fill and outline of their kind: Graphic: shapes, lines, tables and everything except text no fill, a thin black outline Artistic text: text without a frame black fill, no outline Paragraph text: text in a frame black fill, no outline In the panel, each kind shows its fill and outline, with From Selection (take the fill and outline of the selected object) and Reset (back to the defaults of a new drawing). Changing defaults with nothing selected When nothing is selected and you choose a fill or outline (click a palette color, use a fill tool, change the outline color or width), the change goes to new objects. TraceDraw asks which kinds of new objects it applies to: Tick Graphic, Artistic text and Paragraph text as needed. The kinds you ticked last time are ticked. Tick Use these kinds from now on without asking to skip the question from now on. Click OK. Cancel changes nothing.  The check box Ask which kinds a change with nothing selected applies to in the panel turns the question on or off. The Properties panel with nothing selected also edits the Graphic defaults. To keep the defaults for every new drawing, choose Tools > Save Settings as Default. Styles A style is a named set of properties: Fill, Outline (its color, width, line style and arrowheads) and Transparency. Objects you give a style stay linked to it: change the style and they all change. To make a style Select an object with the look you want. Click New style from selection. The style is named "Style 1" and so on, takes the fill, outline and transparency of the object, and is linked to every selected object. Using and changing styles Each style shows its swatches, its name (click it to rename), how many objects are linked to it, and its parts as check boxes: Apply gives the selection the style and links it. Update from selection takes the fill, outline and transparency of the selected object; every linked object follows. Turning a part off leaves that property to each object. Delete removes the style; linked objects keep their look. Break Link to Style unlinks the selected objects, which keep their look. You can still change a linked object directly; the next change of its style sets the style's parts again. Right-click an object to apply a style from its menu.
頁面和版面 一個繪圖可以有多個頁面，每個頁面有自己的大小和方向。這些頁面介紹如何新增、排列和編號頁面，設定文件選項（頁面大小、版面、背景、出血、尺規、格線和輔助線），放置輔助線，使物件貼齊，以及查看繪圖的屬性。

h: Moving between pages The Pages panel Inserting pages Deleting pages Duplicating a page Renaming a page Page size and orientation Page numbers Page background
x: Working with pages Moving between pages Click a page tab under the drawing window, or use the page navigator beside them (first, previous, next and last page). Press PgUp or PgDn. Choose Layout > Go to Page, type the page number in the Go To Page dialog box and click OK.  The Pages panel The Pages panel lists the pages of the drawing. Click a page to go to it. Its buttons Insert Page, Delete Page and Duplicate Page act on the current page, and Page Sorter View shows every page as a thumbnail. Open it from Window > Panels.  Inserting pages Choose Layout > Insert Page, or click one of the insert buttons of the page navigator (they add one page of the current size before or after the current page at once). In the Insert Page dialog box, set the Number of pages and choose Before or After the current page. Click OK.  Deleting pages Delete Page asks which pages to delete: the page number in Delete page (the current page to start with), and to delete a range, Through to page with the last page of it. All of them go in one step, which Undo brings back. A drawing keeps at least one page. Delete Page on a page tab's menu deletes that page at once. Duplicating a page Choose Layout > Duplicate Page, or right-click the page tab and choose Duplicate Page. Under Insert new page, choose Before selected page or After selected page. Choose Copy layer(s) only for a page with the same layers and nothing on them, or Copy layer(s) and their contents to copy the objects too. Click OK. The copy becomes the current page; Edit > Undo removes it. The page tab menu also has Insert Page After, Insert Page Before, Delete Page and Switch Page Orientation. Renaming a page Choose Layout > Rename Page, or double-click the page tab. Type the Page name and click OK.  Page size and orientation Layout > Page Size opens the Page Size dialog box: Type the Width and Height; Swap exchanges them. Tick Apply to all pages to change every page, or leave it off to change the current page only. Click OK.  Switch Page Orientation turns the page between portrait and landscape. With nothing selected, the property bar of the Pick tool also sets the page size and orientation. Its page size list has A4, Letter, A5, A3 and Legal first, then the sizes you saved, then about 130 sizes in groups (ISO A, ISO B and JIS B, North American, print shop, posters and banners, envelopes, cards and postcards, photo, screen and social media, web ads). Custom... opens the Page Size dialog box, and Edit This List... opens the document options at the page size, where you can save a size under a name. The full page settings are in Document options. Pages you add, and their first layer, are named in the interface language. Page numbers Layout > Insert Page Number puts a page number On Active Layer, On All Pages, On All Odd Pages or On All Even Pages. The numbers on master layers show the right number on every page. Object > Insert > Page Number places one in the text you are editing. Layout > Page Number Settings sets how they look: Start at: the first number; Prefix and Suffix: text around the number, such as "Page "; Style: 1, 2, 3, I, II, III, i, ii, iii, A, B, C or a, b, c; Position: Bottom centre, Bottom outer corner, Top centre or Top outer corner.  Page background Layout > Page Background sets the color behind every page; see Document options.

h: The layout Working in multipage view
x: Multipage view View > Multipage View lays every page of the drawing out on the desktop at once, so you can compare pages and edit them side by side. The layout The pages sit in a grid of four columns, in page order, so a page you add goes at the next place and the pages before it stay where they were. Each page shows its number and name below it; the current page's are in the normal text color, the others dimmed. Working in multipage view The current page is edited as usual: rulers, guidelines, grids and the status bar refer to it. Click or drag on another page to make it current and work there at once. The page tabs and the navigator change the current page too. Zoom To Fit (F4) fits every page in the window. The button with four small pages in the page bar, right after the page controls, turns the view on and off too; it is lit while the view is on. Choose Multipage View again to go back to one page at a time. Page Sorter View shows the pages as thumbnails instead; the two views exclude each other.

h: General Page size Layout Background Bleed Rulers Grid Guidelines
x: Document options Layout > Document Options opens the settings of the active drawing: page size, layout, background, bleed, rulers, grid and guidelines. Double-clicking a ruler or the page border also opens it. Choose a page from the list on the left. Changes show at once; OK keeps them and Cancel puts everything back. Save as default keeps the grid, ruler and guideline settings for new drawings. General  Rendering resolution: the resolution of effects that are turned into pixels, such as drop shadows and bitmap effects. Fill open curves (off at first): when on, open curves show their fill as if they were closed. Auto inflate bitmaps for effects (on at first): bitmaps grow to make room for effects that spread past their edges. Duplicate offset: how far Duplicate places the copy. Page size  Choose Page size for a paper size, or Label presets for sheets of labels, which set the page to the sheet size and add guidelines around each label. Size, Width and Height, and Portrait or Landscape. The save button next to Size keeps a custom size under a name you type, and the delete button forgets the saved size shown. Saved sizes appear in every page size list: the property bar, the Page Size dialog box, these options and the new document dialog box. Apply size to current page only: change the current page only. Show page border, and Add Page Frame, which adds a rectangle the size of the page. Rendering resolution, Bleed and Show bleed area (see below). Layout  The page shows how many pages the drawing has, with Page Sorter View and Switch Page Orientation, and lists the Master layers, each shown on All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. The buttons add a new master layer for all, odd or even pages. See Master layers. Background  Choose No background, a Solid color, or a Bitmap (Choose bitmap) to show behind every page. Bleed  Bleed is the part of the drawing that runs past the edge of the page, so the print has no white edge once trimmed. Set the Bleed distance and tick Show bleed area to see it. Printing and PDF export can include the bleed; see Printing. Rulers  Units: the drawing units (inches, millimeters, picas, points, pixels, ciceros, didots, feet, yards, miles, centimeters, meters or kilometers). Drawing scale: makes a distance on the page stand for a distance in the world, such as 1:100. Choose a typical scale, or type the page distance and the world distance. Rulers, positions, sizes and new dimension lines then show world distances; page sizes, outline widths and text sizes do not. Origin: where the rulers count from (Horizontal and Vertical); Reset origin to the page corner puts it back. You can also drag the origin out of the corner where the rulers meet. Tick divisions: the number of ticks between ruler numbers. Nudge: the Nudge distance of the arrow keys (2.54 mm), the Super nudge with Shift (5.08 mm) and the Micro nudge with Ctrl (0.254 mm). Show rulers. Grid  Document grid: Show grid, Snap to grid, the Horizontal and Vertical spacing (10 mm at first), as a distance or as lines per unit, and Show grid as Lines or Dots. Baseline grid: lines across the page for lining up text, with the Baseline grid spacing (14 points), the Start from top (12.7 mm) and the Line color. Pixel grid: the Color and Opacity of the grid of pixels, Show grid at 800% or higher zoom and Snap to pixels. Guidelines  Show guidelines and Snap to guidelines. Default guideline color and Default preset guideline color. Presets: one inch margins, bleed area, page borders, printable area, a three-column newsletter, a basic grid and an upper left grid. User defined: Margins (Top, Bottom, Left, Right), Columns (Number of columns and Distance between) and a Grid (Rows and Columns). Apply Presets adds them; a line that is already there is not added twice. See Rulers, grids and guidelines for working with guidelines on the page.

h: Rulers The document grid Guidelines The Guidelines panel
x: Rulers, grids and guidelines Rulers, grids and guidelines help you place objects precisely. None of them print. Rulers The rulers run along the top and left of the drawing window, in the drawing units; View > Rulers shows or hides them. A dashed line on each ruler follows the pointer. Drag from the corner where the rulers meet to move the origin, the point the rulers count from. Positions on the property bar, the status bar and in the panels count from it too. Drag from a ruler to add a guideline. Double-click a ruler to open its settings; see Document options, where you also set the units and the drawing scale. The document grid View > Grid > Document Grid shows a grid of lines or dots over the page, behind the objects; Document Grid in Snap To makes objects snap to it. Its spacing (10 mm at first) is set in Document options. When lines would be too close, only every second, fifth or tenth line is drawn. The baseline grid (Baseline Grid) draws lines across the page like a ruled notebook, for lining up text; the pixel grid (Pixel Grid) shows the pixels of the drawing in the Pixels view from 800% zoom. Guidelines Guidelines are lines across the drawing window that objects can snap to. Drag from the top ruler for a horizontal guideline, from the left ruler for a vertical one. With the Pick tool, click a guideline to select it (Shift+click adds), and drag it to move it. Drop it outside the drawing window, or press Delete, to delete it. Click the selected guideline again to show its rotation handles, and drag them to turn it. Right-click a guideline to delete, lock or unlock it, or open its properties. Locked guidelines can be selected but not moved or deleted. Edit > Select All > Guidelines selects every guideline of the page, and Guidelines shows or hides them. With guidelines selected (and no objects), Copy and Paste make copies in the same place, and Duplicate makes copies moved by the duplicate offset (set in Layout > Document Options, General). The Transformations panel moves, rotates and scales selected guidelines as it does objects. Guidelines are saved with the drawing in .tdraw files. .cdr files do not keep them: saving one says so on the status bar. The Guidelines panel The Guidelines panel places guidelines by their coordinates. Open it from Window > Panels.  Show and Snap turn guidelines on and snapping to them. Choose the Guideline type: horizontal, vertical or angled. Type the position (x, y, and the Angle for an angled one), counted from the ruler origin. Click Add to add a guideline, or select one in the list and click Modify to move it. The list shows the page's guidelines of that type (Ctrl+click to select several). Delete, Lock and Unlock act on the selected ones, and Guideline color and Guideline style (Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash dot) change their look. Ready-made sets of guidelines (margins, columns, grids) are on the Guidelines page of the document options.

h: Turning snapping on and off What objects snap to Snapping while moving Dynamic and alignment guides
x: Snapping Snapping pulls the pointer, and the objects you move, onto exact points: nodes, the middles of segments, the centers of shapes, guidelines, the grid or the page. It makes it easy to join lines and line objects up without zooming in. Turning snapping on and off View > Snap To, or the Snap To list on the standard toolbar, turns snapping to Pixels, Document Grid (Ctrl+Y), Baseline Grid, Guidelines, Objects (Alt+Z) and Page on and off. At first objects, guidelines and the page are on. The baseline grid works on its own too: with only it on, nodes and objects snap to its lines. Snap Off (Alt+Q) turns all snapping off and on again. What objects snap to When snapping to objects is on, these points attract the pointer within the snapping radius (10 screen pixels at first). Each shows its mark and, with screen tips on, its name. Node the nodes of outlines, the corners of rectangles, the points of polygons Intersection where two outlines cross Midpoint halfway along each segment Quadrant the top, bottom, left and right of ellipses Tangent where a line you draw touches an ellipse or curve Perpendicular where a line you draw meets a segment at a right angle Edge the nearest point of an outline Center the center of shapes, bitmaps and tables Text baseline the baseline of a line of text Points win over guidelines, guidelines over the grids, and edges come last. The modes, the radius and the marks are set on the Snapping page of the options; see TraceDraw options. Snapping while moving When you start moving a selection with the Pick tool on one of its points (a node, a midpoint or the center), that point is carried onto the other object's point or edge. Otherwise the edges and center of the selection's box snap to guidelines, grids, the page and other objects. The handles snap while you resize. Dynamic and alignment guides View > Dynamic Guides (Alt+Shift+D) shows temporary guides at 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees through the points you pass over, so you can draw along them. Alignment Guides (Alt+Shift+A) shows guides when the object you move lines up with others.

h: Describing the drawing The report
x: Document properties File > Document Properties opens the Document Properties dialog box. It keeps information about the drawing, such as its title and author, and reports everything the drawing holds.  Describing the drawing Language: the language of the drawing's text, or none. PDF files written from the drawing carry it, which helps screen readers. Title, Subject, Author, Copyright, Tags (keywords written to PDF and SVG files) and Notes (several lines). Rating: none or one to five stars. Click OK to keep the changes, as one undo step. Cancel leaves everything as it was. The title, subject and rating can also be set when you save; see Save As. The report Under the fields, a report lists what the drawing holds, in sections: File: the name and location of the file. Document: the pages and layers, the page size (in the drawing units and in pixels), the orientation and the resolution. Color: the color profiles, the primary color mode and the rendering intent. Graphic Objects: the number of objects and of points, the most points and parts one curve has, and the curves, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, groups and tables. Text Statistics: artistic and paragraph texts, characters, words and the fonts used. Bitmap Objects: the number of bitmaps, their total pixels and the largest one. Styles: object and color styles. Effects: each effect, with how many objects use it. Fills and Outlines: the objects by kind of fill and outline, and how many use each color model. Symbols: symbols defined and instances placed. The report helps before sending a file to print: for example, it shows which fonts the drawing needs and whether it holds RGB colors. For a full check, see Preflight.
點陣圖 點陣圖是由像素組成的圖片，例如相片和掃描檔。TraceDraw 把點陣圖放進繪圖，改變其色彩模式和大小，校正其角度，遮罩色彩，套用效果，並把它們描圖成形狀。它也能把向量物件轉換成點陣圖。 要匯入圖片，請使用 檔案 > 匯入；請參閱 匯入檔案。選取點陣圖時，屬性列上有點陣圖命令：編輯、裁切、描圖、校正和重新取樣。關於效果，請參閱 點陣圖效果。

h: 設定
x: 將物件轉換為點陣圖 點陣圖 > 轉換為點陣圖（也可使用 物件 > 轉換為點陣圖）會將選取的物件轉換為一個點陣圖。可用來將複雜的圖稿平面化，或為物件套用點陣圖效果做準備。這是一個復原步驟。  設定 解析度：從清單中選擇（72 到 600 dpi）或輸入值（36 到 2400；預設為 300）。 色彩模式：黑白（1 位元）、灰階（8 位元）、調色盤式（8 位元）、RGB 色彩（24 位元，預設）或 CMYK 色彩（32 位元）。 混色：適用於黑白和調色盤式，以混合網點來表現缺少的色調。 永遠套印黑色：點陣圖的黑色會套印在下方的色彩上。 消除鋸齒（預設開啟）：平滑的邊緣；關閉時會產生生硬的像素邊緣。 透明背景（預設開啟）；關閉時會將物件放在白色背景上。 對話方塊會顯示點陣圖未壓縮時的大小。

t: 變更點陣圖的色彩模式
h: 黑白 雙色調 調色盤式 為黑白點陣圖上色
x: 變更點陣圖的色彩模式 機器翻譯：本頁可能落後於英文版。 點陣圖 > 模式 會將選取的點陣圖轉換為其他色彩模式。所有選取的點陣圖會在一個復原步驟中變更，並保留透明度。有設定的模式會開啟一個對話方塊，其中有轉換前和轉換後的預覽；設定位於右側的面板中，面板下方的 重設 會恢復設定，兩個箭頭則復原和重做在對話方塊中所做的變更。 黑白 (1 位元) 只有黑和白（請參閱下文） 灰階 (8 位元) 灰色色階 雙色調 (8 位元) 一到四種油墨（請參閱下文） 調色盤 (8 位元) 最多 256 種色彩（請參閱下文） RGB 色彩 (24 位元) 點陣圖的模式變為 RGB；像素保持原樣 Lab 色彩 (24 位元) Lab 色彩 CMYK 色彩 (32 位元) 點陣圖的模式變為 CMYK，其像素顯示油墨能夠印出的色彩，由色彩管理設定檔計算 所有選取的點陣圖都處於某一模式時，選單會勾選 RGB 色彩 (24 位元) 或 CMYK 色彩 (32 位元)，狀態列會顯示所選點陣圖的模式，例如「Bitmap 600 x 400 px (CMYK)」。.cdr 檔案中的 CMYK 圖片以 CMYK 模式開啟，.tdraw 檔案會保留該模式。工具 > Convert Colors 也會以同樣方式設定所轉換的每個點陣圖的模式（請參閱轉換色彩）。 黑白  選擇轉換方法： 線條藝術：灰階值等於或高於臨界值（預設為 128）處為白色，其他地方為黑色； 有序：規則排列的網點圖樣； 半色調（預設）：以某個角度（45 度）和每英吋若干線數（60）排列的圓形、線條或方形網點網屏； 基數分佈：看似隨機的紋理； Jarvis、Stucki 和 Floyd-Steinberg：誤差擴散，對相片能產生最平滑的結果。 強度（0 到 100，預設為 50）會讓結果變亮或變暗。 雙色調  雙色調以少數幾種油墨印刷灰階圖片，只用少量色彩就能呈現豐富的色調。 選擇類型：單色調、雙色調（預設）、三色調或四色調，分別對應一到四種油墨。 按一下油墨以變更其色彩。 編輯其曲線：橫向是灰階等級（黑色在左側），縱向是該油墨的印刷量。在空白處拖曳可新增點，拖曳點可移動它，按兩下點或將其拖出格線則可移除。全部顯示也會繪製其他油墨的曲線。 儲存和載入會將油墨和曲線保存在檔案中。 調色盤式  調色盤：均勻色彩、標準 VGA（16 色）、自適應和最佳化（圖片本身的色彩，減少到您設定的色彩數量，最多 256 種）、灰階、系統或自訂（文件調色盤）。 混色：無、有序、Jarvis、Stucki 或 Floyd-Steinberg，並可設定混色強度。 產生的調色盤會顯示在設定下方。 為黑白點陣圖上色 只選取雙色點陣圖時，按一下調色盤色彩可為其背景上色，以右鍵按一下則可為其前景上色。

t: 重新取樣、拉直和擴大點陣圖
h: 重新取樣 拉直影像 擴大點陣圖 其他點陣圖指令
x: 重新取樣、拉直和擴大點陣圖 重新取樣 點陣圖 > 重新取樣 會為選取的點陣圖設定新的像素數量；它們在頁面上的大小保持不變。  以像素、百分比，或以其在頁面上的大小所產生的解析度輸入新的大小。開啟維持長寬比時，高度會隨寬度變更。 選擇方法： 平滑（相片），此為預設； 銳利，稍微清晰一些； 硬像素（像素藝術）：每個像素都維持為單一色彩的方塊； 放大並保留細節：平滑處理，並在圖片放大時加以銳利化。 按一下 確定。 對話方塊會顯示原始大小和新大小，以及新圖片佔用的記憶體。選取多個點陣圖時，每個點陣圖都會以相同的倍數縮放。 拉直影像 點陣圖 > 拉直影像 可修正傾斜、以斜角拍攝或因鏡頭而彎曲的相片。  使用格線（可調整其大小和色彩）來對齊圖片。 設定各滑桿：修正鏡頭扭曲（-100 到 100）、旋轉影像（-15 到 15 度）、垂直透視和水平透視（-100 到 100）。旋轉按鈕會先將圖片轉動四分之一圈。 開啟裁切影像時，結果會裁切為保有原始比例的最大矩形；裁切並重新取樣為原始大小會將其恢復為原始的像素數量。不裁切時，角落會是透明的。 按一下 確定。重設會將所有設定恢復原狀。 使用預覽上方的工具縮放和平移預覽。結果會取代像素，因此點陣圖上的效果會變成永久性的。 擴大點陣圖 某些效果（例如模糊）會擴散到點陣圖的邊緣之外。 點陣圖 > 擴大點陣圖 > 自動擴大點陣圖（預設開啟）會依效果所需擴大點陣圖，並加上透明邊界。 手動擴大點陣圖 可手動擴大選取的點陣圖：對於寬度和高度，以像素或百分比（100 到 1000%）輸入新的大小，並可使用維持長寬比。圖片會保持置中。  其他點陣圖指令 裁切點陣圖 會使用 裁切 工具裁切點陣圖；使用 形狀 工具拖曳點陣圖的角落也可以裁切它。 編輯點陣圖 會在另一個程式中開啟點陣圖。 用 AI 移除背景 會讓相片的背景變成透明。 移除背景: 移除背景. 中斷連結 和 從連結更新 適用於連結至檔案的點陣圖。 Save Bitmap As 會將點陣圖儲存為 PNG 檔案。

h: The dialog box Choosing the view Zooming and panning Picking colors on the preview
x: The Before and After preview Every dialog box that changes a picture shows the picture before and after the change in the same preview: Trace Bitmap, Remove Background, the color mode dialog boxes (Black and White, Duotone, Paletted), every bitmap effect and Image Adjustments. This page explains how to look at the picture there. The dialog box These dialog boxes are windows you size: drag an edge or a corner, or click the maximize button in the title bar. The preview fills the left of the window and grows with it; the dialog box's own settings sit in a white panel on the right, each label above its slider and the sliders as wide as the panel, with OK and Cancel under them. Under the panel, Reset puts the settings back and the two arrows beside it undo and redo the changes made in the dialog box: each slider release, list choice, check box and Reset is one step. A change made after undoing drops the steps that were undone. The preview follows every change of the settings by itself. While you drag a slider it shows a quick, smaller version at once, and the full view when you let go. Nothing is worked out again while the settings stay the same, so the dialog box stays quick on large pictures. Choosing the view The Preview list above the picture chooses what the preview shows: Before and After (the default): the picture above and the result below. Before and After side by side: the picture on the left and the result on the right. Before: only the picture as it is. After: only the result. Trace Bitmap calls this view Large Preview: the trace alone, as large as the preview. Wireframe Overlay (Trace Bitmap only): the curves of the trace drawn as thin lines over the picture, to see how closely they follow it. An Overlay slider appears beside the list: it sets how strongly the picture shows under the lines, from 0 (the lines alone) to 100 (the picture as it is), 80 at first. Before and After split (Image Adjustments only): one picture, the original on the left of a dashed line and the result on its right. Drag the line to move it. Image Adjustments starts on After. The labels Before and After sit in the corners of the panes. Transparent parts of the picture show a checkerboard. Zooming and panning The buttons beside the list: Zoom to fit (pressed at first) shows the whole picture in a pane. Zoom out and Zoom in zoom out and in by a quarter each click. The pan button (pressed at first) lets a drag on a pane move the picture. The wheel over a pane zooms about the pointer, so the spot under it stays in place. The two panes always share one zoom and one place: panning or zooming one moves the other the same way, so you compare the same spot. Image Adjustments also has Rotate left and Rotate right, which turn the view a quarter turn (the picture itself does not turn), and 100 %, which shows one pixel of the picture per point of the screen. A spinning mark after the pan button means the dialog box is still working out the result, such as a trace of a large picture; the window keeps answering meanwhile. Picking colors on the preview Some dialog boxes have an eyedropper that picks a color from the picture, such as the background color to remove. While it is on, a click on a pane takes the color under the pointer and the pan button is released. Click the pan button to stop picking. See also Tracing bitmaps, Removing the background, Bitmap color modes and Bitmap effects.

h: 快速描繪 描繪點陣圖對話方塊 預覽 設定 色彩 重設、復原和重做
x: 描繪點陣圖 描繪會將點陣圖轉換為向量形狀，讓您可以編輯、重新上色和縮放而不損失品質：掃描的標誌、草圖、相片都適用。 快速描繪 選取點陣圖並選擇 點陣圖 > 快速描繪。它會使用全域選項的 點陣圖描繪 頁面上所選擇的預設集（預設為美工圖案）。 Repeat Last Trace 不開啟對話方塊，依上次的方式再次描圖所選點陣圖；Open Last Trace Settings 以上次的設定開啟對話方塊。點陣圖的右鍵選單中也有這些命令，以及 中心線描繪 和 外框描繪。 描繪點陣圖對話方塊 點陣圖 > 外框描繪 和 中心線描繪 會列出預設集；選擇其中一個即可開啟描繪對話方塊。 外框描繪以形狀填滿色彩區域：線條藝術、標誌、細節標誌、美工圖案、低品質影像 和 高品質影像。 中心線描繪以開放曲線沿著線條描繪：技術插圖 和 線條繪圖。  對話方塊是一個可以調整大小和最大化的視窗。預覽佔據左側，設定位於右側的面板中，每當您變更設定時都會重新描繪：不必按任何按鈕就能看到結果。預覽下方的一行會計算描繪結果的曲線、節點和色彩數量。按一下 確定 將形狀放置在點陣圖上方（最暗的在最前面），或按一下 取消 保持點陣圖不變。 預覽 預覽 清單選擇預覽顯示的內容： 前後對照：點陣圖在上，描繪結果在下；或 Before and After side by side；之前 只顯示點陣圖。 Large Preview：只顯示描繪結果，和預覽一樣大。 線框疊加：描繪結果的曲線以細線畫在點陣圖上。清單旁邊會出現 Overlay 滑桿：它設定點陣圖在線條下顯示的強度，從 0（只有線條）到 100（點陣圖原樣），預設為 80。 清單後面的按鈕分別是縮放至適合、縮小、放大和平移。滾輪以指標為中心縮放，拖曳則移動圖片；兩個窗格一起移動。透明部分顯示棋盤格。 設定 設定 索引標籤包含： 描繪類型 外框或中心線，以及 影像類型 預設集。選擇一個預設集會把下方的滑桿設為適合該類圖片的值。 細節（0 到 100）：細節越多，保留的小區域和細線越多；細節越少，斑點和顆粒越平滑。 平滑處理（0 到 100，預設為 25）：曲線更平滑、節點更少。 轉角平滑度（0 到 100）：轉角更圓。 移除：從描繪結果中省略什麼。背景色彩移除到達圖片邊緣的背景，影像中的整個色彩移除該色彩的每個區域，無描繪所有內容。自動 沿圖片邊緣尋找背景色彩；指定 使用色票的色彩，您可以變更它，或用旁邊的滴管從預覽中取色。 物件：合併相同顏色的相鄰物件（預設開啟）把一種色彩的所有區域合成一條曲線；關閉時，每個獨立的色塊是一條單獨的曲線。移除物件重疊 讓每個形狀只佔自己的像素；關閉時，形狀會稍微伸到上方形狀的下面，相鄰形狀之間就不會出現縫隙。依顏色群組物件 把每種色彩的曲線放進各自的群組；當一種色彩的區域尚未合併時可用。 刪除原始影像：放置描繪結果時刪除點陣圖。 不適用於目前描繪類型的設定會顯示為灰色：中心線描繪只讀取細節和平滑度。 色彩 顏色 索引標籤設定 色彩模式（RGB、灰階或黑白）和 顏色數（2 到 256），並列出描繪結果的色彩及每種色彩的曲線數量。勾選兩種或更多色彩並按一下 合併選取的顏色，可將它們合併到第一種色彩；按一下某種色彩的色票，可用另一種色彩繪製它的曲線。變更會重新描繪圖片的設定時，這些屬於上一次描繪的編輯會被忘記。 重設、復原和重做 在設定面板下方，重設 恢復預設集的設定，兩個箭頭在對話方塊中所做的每項變更之間前後移動：每次放開滑桿、選擇清單項目、勾選核取方塊、編輯色彩和重設都是一步。復原後所做的變更會捨棄已復原的步驟。 選項 開啟全域選項的 點陣圖描繪 頁面，您可以在那裡選擇快速描繪的預設集以及每次描繪的起始選項，然後返回對話方塊。說明 按鈕會開啟此頁面。

h: 遮罩色彩
x: 從點陣圖中遮罩色彩 點陣圖遮色片 面板可隱藏或保留點陣圖中所選色彩的像素，例如讓白色背景變成透明。使用 點陣圖 > 點陣圖遮罩 開啟它。  遮罩色彩 選取一個點陣圖。 將色彩挑選到十個色彩欄位中： 按一下滴管，然後按一下點陣圖中的色彩；每個色彩都會填入選取的欄位並將其勾選； 或按一下從點陣圖選取色彩，以點陣圖最常用的十種色彩填入各欄位。 選取一個欄位並設定其容許度（0 到 100%）：像素的色彩與欄位色彩可以相差多少，仍然視為相符。 選擇隱藏選取的色彩（相符的像素會變成透明）或顯示選取的色彩（只保留相符的像素，此為預設）。 按一下 套用。 儲存遮色片和開啟遮色片會將各欄位保存在 .msk 檔案中；刪除會清空選取的欄位。每個點陣圖的變更都是一個復原步驟。

t: Removing the background of a bitmap
h: To remove a background Options Tips
x: Removing the background of a bitmap Bitmaps > Remove Background makes the background of a photo or scan transparent and keeps the subject. It works on this computer and needs no AI service. The property bar of a selected bitmap has the same command.  To remove a background Select one or more bitmaps. Click Bitmaps > Remove Background. The preview shows the bitmap before and after, with a checkerboard where it becomes transparent. Set the options below until the subject stands out cleanly. Click OK. Every selected bitmap changes in one undo step. Options Background The colors to remove, one row each. At first there is one row, Automatic: TraceDraw learns the background's colors from the edges of the picture (up to four, so a gradient or a two-tone backdrop works). Each row has: its swatch; an eyedropper: click it, then click a color in a preview or on the drawing, and the row takes that color. On the first row, Automatic goes back to the learnt colors; its own tolerance, a whole number from 0 to 100. It shows the Tolerance below until you change it; Remove color (x), which takes the row out. The last row always stays. Add color (+) adds a row: click it, then click the color in the Before preview or on the drawing. A pixel counts as background when it is close enough to any color of the list, each color with its own tolerance. Shortcuts with the eyedropper on Shift+click in a preview adds the color under the pointer as a new row and keeps the eyedropper on, so you can pick several colors in a row. Alt+click takes out the row whose color is nearest to the one under the pointer. A color picked in a preview is taken from the picture before the change, so a part already removed can still be picked. Tolerance How far a color may be from the background's and still count as background (0 to 100, whole numbers). It is the tolerance of every row that has none of its own. Raise it when some backdrop stays; lower it when parts of the subject go. Edge softness Feathers the edge of the subject, in pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge. Contiguous (on at first) Only the background connected to the edges of the picture goes, so a white shirt on a white backdrop keeps its inside. A color picked in a preview also starts the removal from the point where you clicked, so a hole inside the subject can go with one pick. Turn it off to remove every pixel near a listed color, for example all the holes of a letter or a ring. Remove specks (on at first) Small loose spots left in the background go too. Clean edge colors (on at first) Takes the old background's color out of the half-transparent pixels of the edge, so no light or dark halo shows when the subject goes on another background. Reset, under the settings, puts every option back, with one Automatic row; the two arrows beside it undo and redo the changes made in the dialog box. OK remembers the options and the list of colors until you close TraceDraw, so the next Remove Background starts with them. Tips It works best on a backdrop that differs from the subject: a studio background, a sky, a product on a plain table. For busy scenes, the AI command Remove Background with AI (see AI) separates subject and scene by their meaning. The result replaces the pixels; effects on the bitmap are made permanent. To fine-tune afterwards, use Masking colors.
列印 TraceDraw 透過產生可供列印的紙張 PDF 來列印，再由系統的檢視器把它傳送到印表機。這些頁面介紹列印對話方塊及其預覽、如何把資料合併到設計中以列印多個版本、如何在列印前檢查繪圖，以及如何為布條加上邊框和孔眼。

h: General Color Composite Layout Booklets Prepress PostScript and issues Print preview Other ways to print
x: Printing a drawing Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P). TraceDraw builds the sheets and sends them to the printer you choose, or opens a PDF of them in your system's viewer, where you choose the printer and print. In the browser version, the PDF is downloaded. Printing to a printer runs in the background: the window keeps working, the status bar says "Printing on ..." and then how the print went. The tabs are General, Color, Composite, Layout, Prepress, PostScript and Issues. Under them, Print preview opens the preview with these settings, and Apply keeps them for the next time.  General Destination: one of your system's printers, the system's PDF viewer (which then chooses the printer), a PDF file or a PostScript file. The gear button beside a printer opens its own settings, and the status, location and comment of the printer show under it. The dialog starts on the printer you printed to last. Orientation: match the layout, portrait or landscape. Sheet: the page's own size, the standard paper sizes, or a custom size you can save under a name. Print range: the whole document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5, 8-), or the selected objects; and all, odd or even pages of the document or of the list, for printing on both sides by hand. The selected objects print alone (nothing else of the page, its master layers or its background), on a page the size of the area they cover: with the sheet set to the page's size the paper is that area, on a fixed sheet they are centred at their size (smaller only when they do not fit, unless Keep page size is ticked), and the layouts repeat that area. Copies, collated as whole sets or not. Print as bitmap: each sheet becomes one picture at the resolution you give. Color Composite prints all colors on each sheet; Separations prints one gray page per ink (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, then each spot ink). In Print Preview you can untick inks under Print separations; only the ticked inks print. Convert spot colors to CMYK prints spot inks as their CMYK mix. Composite Print text in black. Always overprint black: full black fills and outlines print over the colors beneath. Layout As in document, Fit to page, or Scale to a percentage. Fit to page also shrinks objects larger than the page (or the selection, when you print only that) so they print whole on it. Bleed limit: how far beyond the page objects print (4 mm at first, or the drawing's own bleed). Paper margins (left, right, top, bottom, 0 at first) keep the paper's edges clear: the pages and their marks go in what is left. The imposition: several pages on one sheet, or a booklet, whose pages are paired for folding, with the sheet size and the gap between pages. A sketch shows the result. For the back of double-sided cards, tick Back side: the pages run right to left on the sheet, so each one prints behind its front, and the text is not mirrored. Keep page size keeps the pages at their size on a fixed sheet: they do not shrink for the marks, and the columns and rows stay as you set them (pages that do not fit run off the sheet, and a warning says so). Without it, the pages shrink to fit the columns and rows you ask for. In Print Preview, drag on the sheet to move the page information. Booklets Choose Booklet as the imposition to print two pages on each side of a sheet, ready to fold. Printing booklets explains it step by step. The page count is rounded up to a multiple of four with blank pages at the back, and the summary under the sketch says how many pages, blanks and sheets of paper it takes. To print only some of the pages, list them in Pages first. Binding: Saddle stitch nests every sheet inside the one before and staples them through the fold (8 pages: 8 1, 2 7 on the outer sheet). Perfect bound folds the sheets in signatures of Sheets per signature, stacks the signatures and glues them at the spine (one sheet per signature: 4 1, 2 3, then 8 5, 6 7). Creep (saddle stitch): how far the pages of the innermost sheet move toward the spine, so the fore edges line up after trimming; the sheets between move in proportion, the outer one not at all. Gap: the space between the two pages of a spread, centred on the fold. Prepress Invert and Mirror the whole sheet, for film. Print file information (the drawing's name or your own text, the page numbers, sheet number and date) and Print page numbers. Crop marks (and fold marks for booklets), Registration marks, Color bars and Densitometer scale. PostScript and issues With a PostScript file as the destination, the PostScript tab sets the language level (2 or 3). The Issues tab shows what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Apply keeps the settings for the next time; see Global options for the defaults. Print preview File > Print Preview, or Print preview in the Print dialog box, shows the sheets exactly as they will print, with the imposition and the marks. The bar at the top has Print, the sheet shown with previous and next (PgUp, PgDn), the zoom with Fit, the printer with its settings button and status, the number of copies with Collate, and Close (Esc). On a narrow window the bar takes two rows. The options on the left stand two to a row: the pages (all, current, a list, the selection, odd or even), fit to page or the scale, then the prepress options (separations, bleed, marks, page information, mirror, invert, transform and artwork position), then the layout with its sketch. Every change rebuilds the sheets at once. Drag the panel's edge to make it wider. With Print separations on, a box for each ink stands under it. All ticked shows the sheet; one alone shows its plate in gray; some show the colors those inks print together. Drag the dashed blue lines on the sheet to set the paper margins, and drag the sheet to move the artwork on its page (Artwork position shows the move, with Reset). Transform draws handles to stretch the artwork. Other ways to print File > Send To saves a PDF to your desktop or documents folder, or attaches it to an email. Publi

h: Printing a booklet Choosing the binding The settings Blank pages and the counts
x: Printing booklets A booklet prints two pages on each side of a sheet of paper, placed so that the folded sheets read in order: a menu, a program, a small catalog or a zine. TraceDraw pairs the pages for you; you choose how the booklet is bound. Printing a booklet Put the pages of the drawing in reading order, the cover first. Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P) or Print Preview. On the Layout tab, choose Booklet as the Imposition. Under Binding, click one of the two pictures (see below). Set the binding's fields: Sheets per signature for a perfect-bound booklet, Creep for a saddle-stitched one, and the Gap for either. Check the sketch and the counts under it, then print on both sides of the paper. To make a booklet of only some pages, list them in the pages to print on the General tab first. Choosing the binding Saddle stitch (the default): every sheet is folded inside the one before and the booklet is stapled through the fold. For eight pages, the outer sheet holds pages 8 and 1 on one side and 2 and 7 on the other; the inner sheet holds 6 and 3, then 4 and 5. Best for thin booklets. Perfect bound: the sheets go in signatures, small groups of Sheets per signature (4 at first, 1 to 32) folded together. The signatures are stacked and glued at the spine. The last signature takes the sheets left over. With one sheet per signature the pages pair as 4 1, 2 3, then 8 5, 6 7. Best for thicker booklets. The settings Sheets per signature (perfect bound only): how many sheets are folded together in each signature. Creep (saddle stitch only, 0 to 20 mm, 0 at first): when nested sheets are folded, the inner ones stick out at the open edge and lose more when the booklet is trimmed. Creep moves the pages of the innermost sheet this far toward the spine; the sheets between move in proportion and the outer sheet does not move. The crop marks move with the pages. Gap (0 to 100 mm, 0 at first): the space between the two pages of a spread, centred on the fold. On a sheet sized to the pages, the sheet grows by the gap. Blank pages and the counts A booklet always has a multiple of four pages, since each sheet holds four. When the drawing has another number, blank pages are added at the back. Under the sketch, the summary gives the number of pages, the blank pages added and the sheets of paper printed on both sides, and for a perfect-bound booklet the number of signatures. With Crop marks on the Prepress tab, a booklet also gets a dashed fold mark at the spine. See Printing a drawing for the other marks. Tip: Print one copy first and fold it to check the order and the margins before you print them all.

h: Setting up a merge The Print Merge panel Kinds of field Editing the records
x: Print merge Print merge fills a design with data, to make many versions of it: name badges, numbered tickets, certificates, labels with QR codes. Each record of your data becomes a copy of the page, filled in. Setting up a merge Design the page. Where a value goes, type the field name in angle brackets in a text object, such as <Name>. Choose File > Print Merge > Create/Load Print Merge. Add the data: Import file reads a CSV file (separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, as Excel or any other program saves it) or an Excel workbook (.xlsx, its first sheet) whose first line names the fields. Fields named like a photo or a picture, or whose cells are picture files, start as pictures, fields named QR as QR codes; the types show at once to be changed; or Add column to add fields by hand, then add records with +. Click Finish. The Print Merge panel opens, where you put the fields on the page and make the merge.  The Print Merge panel The Print Merge panel (also under Window > Panels) works with the data source you created or loaded: Create and Edit open the records. Choose the kind of field, Text, Picture or QR code, and the column under Data source columns. For a picture, Pictures folder chooses the folder your photos are in, when the data names only their files (a name without an extension, such as 1024, finds 1024.jpg or 1024.png). Placeholder image chooses a picture that stands in for the merged ones while you design, and Align and scale sets where each picture goes in its frame: click one of the nine points to anchor it, then choose Actual size, Fit proportionally, Fill proportionally (the frame cuts what is outside) or Stretch to fill. Insert Field puts the field in the text you are editing, or places a new text, picture frame or QR square in the middle of the view. Move and size it like any object. To put each photo inside a shape of your own (a circle, an oval, any outline, also inside a grouped card design), choose Image and the photo column, select the shape and click Place Inside Frame. Every card's photo then goes inside that shape, placed by the alignment and scale. Tick On every page (off at first) before Insert Field to put a text, picture or QR code field in the same place on every page of the drawing. Create Merged Document then fills the drawing's own pages, one record each, instead of making a new drawing. Move or resize the field on its page and the copies on the other pages follow it when you merge; a copy you moved by hand on its own page stays where you put it. Select a field and click Update Field to change its column or its alignment and scale. Create Merged Document makes the merged pages in a new drawing: the page you are on is copied once per record and each copy is filled in. Your design stays as it is. Print Merged Document does the same and opens Print. Perform Merge instead adds the filled copies to the current drawing, right after the page, named after the page and the record number. Kinds of field Text: replaces <Field> in every text of the page. Number: a counter you do not type: a start, a step and a number of digits (start 7, step 3, digits 3 gives 007, 010, 013). Its Format is 1, 2, 3 (the default), A, B, C or a, b, c (1 is A, 26 is Z, then AA), or Custom, which puts a text of your own before and after the number, for tickets and serial numbers ("Ticket T-" before, 4 digits and start 98 give Ticket T-0098, Ticket T-0099 and so on). When you add a Number column, untick Continually increment value to give every record the same number, or give an ending value to make the records from the start to the end at once (15 to 25 in three digits makes eleven records, 015 to 025), with no data file at all. Picture: the cell holds the path of a picture. A text holding only <Field> becomes the picture, as large as fits its box. Put that text inside a frame with Place Inside Frame (a photo frame) and the picture fills the frame, cut by it. A rectangle, ellipse or curve named <Field> (in the Objects panel) takes the picture inside it the same way. Fields work in groups and frames too, so a card can be grouped. QR code: a text holding only <Field> becomes a QR code of the cell's text. An empty cell, or a picture that does not load, removes that object from the record's page. Editing the records Configure columns renames fields, changes their type and counter settings, and removes fields. View single record shows one record as a form; use the arrows or Go to record to move through them. The placeholder buttons insert a field into the text you are editing. Save data source writes the records as a CSV file. To work on several cells at once, drag from one cell to another, or over the record numbers or the field names to take whole records or fields. Then Add adds as many empty records after them, Delete removes their records and Clear (or the Delete key) empties the cells. Edit Print Merge reopens the records.

h: The checks Using the list
x: Preflight Preflight checks a drawing for what tends to go wrong in print, before you print it or send it to a print shop. Choose File > Preflight. The Print dialog box also runs the checks and shows how many issues it found.  The checks Empty text object text with nothing in it Text does not fit its frame paragraph text with hidden lines Font not installed text in a font that is not installed Very small text text smaller than 5 points as printed Small text in rich black small black text made of several inks RGB color in a CMYK drawing screen colors in a drawing meant for print Object off the page objects outside the page and its bleed Low-resolution bitmap bitmaps below 200 dpi as placed Very high-resolution bitmap bitmaps above 1200 dpi Very thin outline outlines thinner than 0.1 mm White set to overprint white that would vanish when printed Empty page pages with no objects Objects that will not print objects on hidden or non-printing layers Warnings are likely problems; notes are worth a look. Using the list The top of the box shows the outcome. Each kind of issue has a heading with its count; click it to open or close it. Click an issue to go to its page and select its object. Under the list, the box says what to do about the kind you picked. Check again runs the checks again after you fix things. Choose checks turns checks on and off and sets their limits: the bitmap resolutions, the smallest text sizes and the thinnest outline. Defaults puts them back.

h: Source Border Grommets
x: Border and grommets Tools > Border and Grommet finishes large prints such as banners and canvases: it grows the page by a border and places grommet marks, where the eyelets will be punched, along its edge.  The preview on the left shows the final page, the border band, the original area (dashed) and the grommets, with the final height and width. Source Choose Page, or Selection to make the box of the selected objects the page. Border Tick Add border and choose its type: Mirror the edges: the design is mirrored out into the border; Stretch the edges: the edge pixels are stretched out; Solid color: the border is filled with one color. Set the size (31.75 mm at first), the same on every side. The design stays where it is; mirrored and stretched edges are made from a picture of the design, placed behind it, so your objects stay editable. Grommets Tick Add grommets, then set: Use border area: center each grommet in the border band; Size: the diameter of the grommet (6.35 mm at first); Margin: from the outer edge to the grommet (31.75 mm at first). Under Placement and distribution, choose the edges (corners, top, bottom, left, right; all at first), then the number of grommets per edge (4 at first) or the spacing between them. Corner grommets are shared by the two edges. The grommets are drawn as thin circles on a layer of their own. Reset puts every field back; OK is available when a border or grommets are on.
網頁圖形 用於網頁、應用程式和螢幕的圖形通常是螢幕解析度的點陣圖（PNG、JPEG、WebP、 GIF），或在任何尺寸下都清晰的 SVG 檔案。這些頁面介紹如何逐一匯出它們，以及如何一次匯出多個頁面和物件。 物件也可以帶有在匯出的 SVG、HTML 和 PDF 檔案中有效的連結；請參閱 連結和書籤。

h: Choosing a format Size and resolution Before exporting text
x: Exporting for the web File > Export For > Web opens the Export dialog box set up for screens: PNG at 96 dpi. It keeps its own settings, apart from Export. Office does the same for office documents (PNG at 150 dpi).  Choosing a format PNG: sharp edges and transparency; best for logos, icons and illustrations. JPEG: small files for photos; no transparency. Set the quality (1 to 100). WebP: small files with transparency; set the quality. GIF: few colors, with transparency. SVG: vector graphics that stay sharp at any size and keep links and object names. HTML: a web page with the drawing. Size and resolution For bitmap formats, set the resolution, or type the width or height in pixels: the other side follows the proportions of the page. For a 32 by 32 pixel icon, type 32. With Transparent background on, the empty parts of the page stay transparent in PNG, WebP and GIF files. Selected only exports only the selected objects, cropped to them; All pages exports every page. The preview shows what will be written, and the dialog box estimates the file size. Before exporting text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies text for the web. To export many pages or objects at once, see The Export panel.

h: Adding assets Exporting
x: The Export panel The Export panel keeps a list of assets (pages and objects) and exports them all at once, each in its own format, to one folder: the icons of an app in several sizes, every page of a set of social media posts. Open it from Window > Panels.  Adding assets Add pages adds every page of the drawing, named after the page. Add selection adds the selected objects as one asset, cropped to them, named after the object. New assets take the format and resolution set under New assets (PNG at 150 dpi at first). Each asset has a tick (only ticked assets are exported), its name (the file name), its format, its resolution for bitmap formats (72 to 2400 dpi) and a cross to remove it. The link under the name goes to the page or selects the objects. Exporting Click Browse to choose the folder (the first export asks for one). Click Export. The button shows how many assets will be written. Characters that files cannot have in their name become _, and two assets with the same name get " (2)", " (3)" and so on. The status bar says how many files were written. In the browser, every file is downloaded.
